m.verse: ...That year they began to eat the crops of the land of Canaan.
paras: Israel's weary wanderings were at last over, and the promised rest was attained. No more nomadic tents, fiery serpents, fierce Amalekites, or howling wildernesses: they came to the land flowing with milk and honey, and they ate the produce of the land. Perhaps this year, beloved Christian reader, this will be true for you or for me. The prospect is joyful, and when faith is actively at work, it brings pure delight. To be with Jesus in the rest that remains for the people of God is a cheering hope indeed, and to expect this glory so soon is double bliss. Unbelief shudders at the Jordan that still rolls between us and that good land, but let us rest assured that we have already experienced more afflictions than death at its worst can ever bring us. Let us banish every fearful thought, and rejoice with abundant joy in the prospect that this year we will begin to be "always with the Lord."

Some of the Lord's vast army will remain on earth this year to serve their Lord. If this is our appointed path, there is no reason why our New Year's text should not still be true. "Now we who have believed enter that rest." The Holy Spirit is the guarantee of our inheritance; He gives us "glory begun below." In heaven the saints are secure, and we likewise are preserved in Christ Jesus; there they triumph over their enemies, and we have victories too. Heavenly spirits enjoy communion with their Lord, and this is not denied to us; they rest in His love, and we have perfect peace in Him; they sing His praise, and it is our privilege to bless Him as well. This year we will gather heavenly fruits on earthly ground, where faith and hope have turned the desert into the garden of the Lord. In ancient days man ate the bread of angels, and why not now? Oh, for grace to feed on Jesus, and so to eat the fruit of the land of Canaan this year!

e.verse: ...We will rejoice and delight in You.
paras: We will rejoice and delight in You. We will not open the gates of the year to the mournful notes of the horn, but to the sweet strains of the harp of joy and the resonant cymbals of gladness. "Come, let us sing for joy to the LORD; let us shout to the Rock of our salvation!" We, the called and faithful and chosen, will drive away our griefs and set up our banners of confidence in the name of God. Let others lament over their troubles; we who have the sweetening tree to cast into Marah's bitter pool will magnify the Lord with joy. Eternal Spirit, our unfailing Comforter, we who are the temples in which You dwell will never cease from adoring and blessing the name of Jesus. We WILL—we are resolved about it! Jesus must wear the crown of our heart's delight; we will not dishonor our Bridegroom by mourning in His presence. We are appointed to be the choir of the skies; let us rehearse our everlasting anthem before we sing it in the halls of the New Jerusalem. We will REJOICE AND DELIGHT: two words with one meaning—double joy, blessedness upon blessedness!

Must there be any limit to our rejoicing in the Lord even now? Do not those who know His grace find their Lord to be fragrant henna and spikenard, calamus and cinnamon even now? And what richer fragrance could they have in heaven itself? We will rejoice and delight IN YOU. That last phrase is the meat in the dish, the kernel of the nut, the very soul of the text. What heavens are stored up in Jesus! What rivers of infinite bliss have their source—yes, and every drop of their fullness—in Him! Since, O sweet Lord Jesus, You are the present treasure and inheritance of Your people, favor us this year with such a sense of Your preciousness that from its first to its last day we may rejoice and delight in You. Let January open with joy in the Lord, and December close with gladness in Jesus.

m.verse: Devote yourselves to prayer...
paras: It is striking to observe how much of Sacred Scripture is devoted to prayer—giving examples, pressing commands, and proclaiming promises. We scarcely open the Bible before we read, "At that time men began to call on the name of the LORD"; and just as we are about to close the book, the "Amen" of a genuine prayer meets our ear. Examples abound. Here we find a wrestling Jacob; there, a Daniel who prayed three times a day; and a David who called upon his God with all his heart. On the mountain we see Elijah; in the dungeon, Paul and Silas. We have multitudes of commands and countless promises. What does this teach us, if not the sacred importance and necessity of prayer? We may be certain that whatever God has made prominent in His Word, He intends to be conspicuous in our lives. If He has said much about prayer, it is because He knows how greatly we need it. So deep are our necessities that until we are in heaven we must never cease to pray.

Do you need nothing? Then I fear you do not know your poverty. Have you no mercy to ask of God? Then may the Lord's mercy show you your misery! A prayerless soul is a Christless soul. Prayer is the first lisping of the believing infant, the shout of the fighting believer, and the quiet farewell song of the dying saint falling asleep in Jesus. It is the breath, the watchword, the comfort, the strength, and the honor of a Christian. If you are a child of God, you will seek your Father's face and live in your Father's love. Pray that this year you may be holy, humble, zealous, and patient; that you may enjoy closer communion with Christ, and enter more often into the banquet hall of His love. Pray that you may be an example and a blessing to others, and that you may live more for the glory of your Master. The motto for this year must be: "Devote yourselves to prayer."

e.verse: ...Let the peoples renew their strength.
paras: All things on earth need to be renewed. No created thing continues by itself. "You renew the face of the earth," was the Psalmist's cry. Even the trees, which do not wear themselves out with care nor shorten their lives with work, must drink the rain of heaven and draw from the hidden treasures of the soil. The cedars of Lebanon, which God has planted, live only because day by day they are full of sap drawn fresh from the earth. Nor can man's life be sustained without renewal from God. Just as we must replenish the body with regular meals, so we must restore the soul by feeding upon the Book of God, listening to the preached Word, and gathering at the soul-enriching table of the Lord's ordinances.

How quickly our spiritual strength fades when these means of grace are neglected! What poor, starved souls some believers are who live without the diligent use of God's Word and private prayer! If our devotion to God can survive without Him, He never created it; it is only a dream. For if God had fathered it, it would wait upon Him just as flowers wait for the dew. Without constant restoration we are not ready for the relentless assaults of hell, the severe trials of heaven, or even the conflicts within our own hearts. When the whirlwind is unleashed, woe to the tree that has not drawn up fresh sap and gripped the rock with many intertwined roots! When tempests arise, woe to the sailors who have not reinforced their mast, dropped their anchor, or sought the harbor! If we allow what is good to grow weaker, evil will surely gather strength and struggle desperately for mastery over us; and so, perhaps, a painful desolation and a tragic disgrace may follow. Let us draw near to the throne of God's mercy in humble prayer, and we will realize the fulfillment of the promise: "Those who wait upon the LORD will renew their strength."

m.verse: ...Appoint You to be a covenant for the people...
paras: Jesus Christ is Himself the sum and substance of the covenant, and as one of its gifts, He is the possession of every believer. Believer, can you fathom what you have received in Christ? "In Him all the fullness of Deity dwells in bodily form." Consider that word "God" and its infinity, and then meditate upon "perfect man" and all His beauty; for all that Christ, as God and man, ever possessed or could ever possess is yours—given out of pure, free favor, handed over to you to be your permanent inheritance forever. Our blessed Jesus, as God, is omniscient, omnipresent, and omnipotent. Will it not comfort you to know that all these great and glorious attributes are completely yours? Does He have power? That power is yours to support and strengthen you, to overcome your enemies, and to preserve you to the very end. Does He have love? There is not a drop of love in His heart that is not yours; you may plunge into the boundless ocean of His love and say of it all, "It is mine!" Does He have justice? It may seem a stern attribute, but even that is yours, for by His justice He will see to it that everything promised to you in the covenant of grace will certainly be secured to you. And all that He has as perfect man is yours. As a perfect man, the Father's delight rested upon Him; He stood accepted by the Most High. O believer, God's acceptance of Christ is your acceptance! For do you not know that the very love the Father set upon a perfect Christ, He sets upon you now? All that Christ did is yours. That perfect righteousness which Jesus accomplished through His stainless life—keeping the law and honoring it—is yours, and it is imputed to you. Christ is in the covenant.

My God, I am Thine—what a comfort divine!
What a blessing to know that the Savior is mine!
In the heavenly Lamb thrice happy I am,
And my heart dances with joy at the sound of His name.

e.verse: ...A voice of one calling in the wilderness: "Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him."
paras: The voice calling in the wilderness demanded a way for the Lord—a way prepared, and a way prepared in the wilderness. I want to heed the Master's proclamation and give Him a highway into my heart, built up by the work of His grace through the desert of my fallen nature. The four directions in the text require my wholehearted attention.

Every valley must be lifted up. Low and degrading thoughts of God must be abandoned; doubting and despair must be cast out; and self-seeking and earthly pleasures must be forsaken. Across these deep valleys a glorious highway of grace must be raised.

Every mountain and hill must be brought low. Proud self-reliance and boastful self-righteousness must be leveled to make a highway for the King of kings. Divine fellowship is never granted to haughty, arrogant sinners. The Lord regards the lowly and visits the contrite in heart, but the proud are detestable to Him. My soul, plead with the Holy Spirit to set you right in this matter.

The crooked places must be made straight. The wavering heart must have a clear path of wholehearted decision for God and holiness marked out for it. Double-minded people are strangers to the God of truth. My soul, see to it that you are honest and true in all things, living before the eyes of the God who searches every heart.

The rough places must be made smooth. The stumbling blocks of sin must be removed, and the thorns and briers of rebellion must be uprooted. So great a Visitor must not encounter muddy roads and rocky ground when He comes to honor His favored people with His presence. Oh, that this evening the Lord may find in my heart a highway prepared by His grace, so that He may ride in triumph through the furthest reaches of my soul, from the beginning of this year even to its close!

m.verse: ...Grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ...
paras: "Grow in grace"—not in one grace only, but in every grace. Grow in that root-grace: faith. Believe the promises more firmly than you have before. Let your faith grow in fullness, steadfastness, and simplicity. Grow also in love. Ask that your love may expand, becoming more intense, more practical, and influencing every thought, word, and deed. Grow likewise in humility. Seek to take a lowly place and recognize your own utter dependence on God. As you grow downward in humility, seek also to grow upward—drawing nearer to God in prayer and enjoying more intimate fellowship with Jesus. May God the Holy Spirit enable you to grow in the knowledge of our Lord and Savior.

Anyone who does not grow in the knowledge of Jesus refuses to be blessed. To know Him is eternal life, and to grow in knowing Him is to increase in true joy. Whoever does not long to know more of Christ knows nothing of Him yet. Whoever has tasted this wine will thirst for more; for although Christ completely satisfies, it is a satisfaction that does not dull the appetite, but sharpens it. If you know the love of Jesus, then just as the deer pants for streams of water, so your soul will long to drink more deeply of His love. If you do not desire to know Him better, you do not truly love Him, for love always cries, "Nearer, nearer!" Absence from Christ is hell, but the presence of Jesus is heaven.

Do not rest content, then, without a growing personal knowledge of Jesus. Seek to know more of Him in His divine nature, in His human relationships, in His finished work, in His death, in His resurrection, in His present glorious intercession, and in His future royal return. Stay close beside the cross, and contemplate the mystery of His wounds. An increase in love for Jesus and a deeper understanding of His love for us is one of the surest marks of true growth in grace.

e.verse: Although Joseph recognized his brothers, they did not recognize him.
paras: This morning our hearts longed to grow in our knowledge of the Lord Jesus; it is good tonight to consider a related theme—namely, our heavenly Joseph's knowledge of us. This was wonderfully complete long before we had the slightest awareness of Him. "Your eyes saw my unformed body; all my days were written in Your book before one of them came to be." Before we even existed in this world, we had a place in His heart. When we were enemies to Him, He knew us—our misery, our madness, and our wickedness. When we wept bitterly in despairing repentance and saw Him only as a judge and ruler, He saw us as His dearly beloved brothers, and His heart yearned for us. He never mistook His chosen, but always regarded them as the objects of His boundless love. "The Lord knows those who are His" is just as true of the prodigals feeding pigs in the distant field as it is of the children seated around the table.

Yet how tragic it was that we did not recognize our royal Brother, and from that ignorance sprang a multitude of sins! We withheld our hearts from Him and gave Him no room in our affections. We doubted Him and placed no trust in His words. We rebelled against Him and offered Him no loving devotion. The Sun of Righteousness shone forth, yet we could not see Him. Heaven came down to earth, but earth did not recognize it. Praise God, those days are behind us! Yet even now, what we know of Jesus is so little compared to what He knows of us. We have only begun to learn of Him, but He knows us completely. It is a mercy that the ignorance is not on His side, for then our case would be hopeless. He will never say to us, "I never knew you"; instead, He will acknowledge our names on the day of His appearing, and meanwhile He will reveal Himself to us in a way He never does to the world.

m.verse: And God saw that the light was good, and He separated the light from the darkness.
paras: Light is surely good, since it sprang from that decree of goodness: "Let there be light." We who enjoy it should be far more grateful for it than we are, seeing more of God in it and through it. Physical light was said by Solomon to be sweet, but gospel light is infinitely more precious, for it reveals eternal realities and nourishes our immortal souls. When the Holy Spirit gives us spiritual light and opens our eyes to behold the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ, we see sin in its true colors and ourselves in our true condition. We see the Most Holy God as He reveals Himself, the plan of mercy as He sets it forth, and the world to come as the Word describes it. Spiritual light shines with many beams and varied colors; but whether they are knowledge, joy, holiness, or life, all are divinely good. If the light we receive is so good, what must the Source of light Himself be? And how glorious must be the place where He unveils Himself! O Lord, since light is so good, give us more of it—and more of Yourself, the true Light.

No sooner does a good thing appear in the world than a separation becomes necessary. Light and darkness have no fellowship; God has divided them, so let us not confuse them. Children of light must have no fellowship with the deeds, doctrines, or deceptions of darkness. The children of the day must be sober, upright, and bold in their Lord's work, leaving the works of darkness to those who will dwell in it forever. Our churches should, through biblical discipline, divide the light from the darkness, and we must do the same by our distinct separation from the world. In our judgment, actions, hearing, teaching, and friendships, we must distinguish between the precious and the worthless, maintaining the great distinction that the Lord established on the world's first day. O Lord Jesus, be our light all through this day, for Your light is the light of men.

e.verse: And God saw that the light was good...
paras: This morning we considered the goodness of the light and the Lord's dividing it from the darkness; now we notice the special eye the Lord has for the light. "God saw the light"—He looked upon it with delight, gazed upon it with pleasure, and saw that it "was good." If the Lord has given you light, dear reader, He looks upon that light with special, loving interest. It is dear to Him not only as His own handiwork, but because it is like Himself, for "He is light." It is sweet for the believer to know that God's eye tenderly watches over the work of grace He has begun. He never loses sight of the treasure He has placed in our jars of clay. Sometimes we cannot see the light, but God always sees the light, and that is far better than our seeing it. It is better for the judge to see my innocence than for me to think I see it. It brings great comfort to know that I am one of God's people—but whether I know it or not, if the Lord knows it, I am still safe. This is the foundation: "The Lord knows those who are His."

You may be sighing and groaning because of the sin living within you, mourning over your darkness; yet the Lord sees "light" in your heart, for He has placed it there, and all the cloudiness and gloom of your soul cannot hide your light from His gracious eye. You may have sunk low into depression or even despair; but if your soul has any longing for Christ, and if you are seeking to rest in His finished work, God sees the "light." He not only sees it, but He also preserves it in you: "I, the LORD, am its keeper." This is a precious thought to those who, after anxious self-examination and striving, feel their own complete inability to preserve themselves. The light He preserves by His grace will one day shine with the splendor of noonday and the fullness of eternal glory. The light within us is the dawn of eternal day.

m.verse: Cast all your anxiety on Him, because He cares for you.
paras: It is a wonderful way to soothe our sorrow when we can truly say, "He cares for me!" Christian, do not bring dishonor on your faith by constantly wearing a worried look; come, cast your burden upon your Lord. You are staggering beneath a weight your Father does not even feel. What seems to you a crushing load would be to Him only like dust on the scales. Nothing is so sweet as to

Lie passive in God's hands,
And know no will but His.

O child of suffering, be patient! God has not overlooked you in His providence. He who feeds the sparrows will also provide everything you need. Do not sit down in despair; hope on, hope always! Take up the weapons of faith against a sea of troubles, and by standing firm you will see an end to your distress. There is One who cares for you. His eye is fixed on you, His heart beats with compassion for your sorrow, and His almighty hand will bring you the help you need. The darkest cloud will scatter in showers of mercy; the blackest night will give way to the morning. If you belong to His family, He will bind up your wounds and heal your broken heart. Do not doubt His grace because of your trials, but believe that He loves you just as much in seasons of trouble as in times of joy. What a peaceful and quiet life you could live if you would leave the providing to the God of providence! With a little oil in a jar and a handful of flour in a bowl, Elijah survived the famine, and you will do the same. If God cares for you, why do you need to be weighed down with anxiety? Can you trust Him with your soul, but not with your body? He has never refused to carry your burdens; He has never collapsed beneath their weight. Come, then, my soul! Put away your anxious fretting, and place all your concerns into the hands of a gracious God.

e.verse: ...The hand of the LORD was upon me in the evening...
paras: In the way of judgment this may be so; and if it is, let it be my duty to consider the reason for such a trial, and heed the rod and the One who has appointed it. I am not the only one humbled and convicted in the quiet hours of the night; let me submit willingly to the affliction and strive to benefit from it. Yet the hand of the Lord may also be felt in another way—strengthening the soul and lifting the spirit toward eternal realities. Oh, that in this sense I may feel the Lord dealing with me! An awareness of God's presence living within us carries the soul toward heaven as on eagles' wings. At such times we are filled to the brim with spiritual joy, forgetting the cares and sorrows of this earth. The invisible world draws near, and the visible realm loses its hold on us; the body waits like a servant at the foot of the hill, while the spirit worships upon the summit in the presence of the Lord.

Oh, that a sacred season of communion with God may be granted to me this evening! The Lord knows how deeply I need it. My spiritual strength fades, my sinful desires rage, my faith is weak, and my devotion is cold—all of these are reasons why His healing hand should be laid upon me. His hand can cool the heat of my burning forehead and calm the pounding of my anxious heart. That glorious right hand which formed the world can renew my mind; that untiring hand which upholds the pillars of the earth can sustain my spirit; that loving hand which holds all the saints can protect and cherish me; and that mighty hand which shatters the enemy can subdue my sins. Why should I not feel that hand touching me this evening? Come, my soul, approach your God with this powerful plea: that Jesus' hands were pierced for your redemption! Then you will surely feel that same hand upon you which once touched Daniel and set him upon his knees that he might see the visions of God.

m.verse: For to me, to live is Christ...
paras: The believer did not always live for Christ. He began to do so when God the Holy Spirit convicted him of sin, and when by grace he was brought to see the dying Savior making propitiation for his guilt. From the moment of that new, heavenly birth, a person begins to live for Christ. Jesus is to believers the pearl of great price, for Whom we are willing to part with all that we have. He has so completely won our love that our hearts beat for Him alone; for His glory we would live, and in defense of His gospel we would die. He is the pattern of our life, and the model after which we would sculpt our character. Paul's words mean far more than most people realize; they imply that the aim and purpose of his life was Christ—indeed, his very life was Jesus. In the words of an ancient saint, he ate, drank, and slept eternal life. Jesus was his very breath, the soul of his soul, the heart of his heart, and the life of his life.

Can you say, as a professing Christian, that you live up to this reality? Can you honestly say that for you to live is Christ? Your work—are you doing it for Christ? Is it not done for self-promotion and family advantage? Do you ask, "Is that a bad motive?" For the Christian, it is. He professes to live for Christ; how can he live for any other goal without committing spiritual adultery? There are many who practice this principle to some degree; but who would dare to say that he has lived entirely for Christ as the apostle did? Yet this alone is the true life of a Christian—its source, its sustenance, its shape, and its goal, all gathered up in one name: Christ Jesus. Lord, accept me; I offer myself to You here and now, praying to live only in You and for You. Let me be like the ox standing between the plow and the altar—ready to work or to be sacrificed; and let my motto be: "Ready for either."

e.verse: My sister, my bride...
paras: Notice the tender titles with which the heavenly Solomon, with intense affection, addresses His bride, the church: "My sister—one near to Me by ties of human nature, sharing the same feelings and experiences. My bride—nearest and dearest, united to Me by the tenderest bonds of love; My sweet companion, part of My very self. My sister by My incarnation, which makes Me bone of your bone and flesh of your flesh; My bride by heavenly betrothal, in which I have joined you to Myself in righteousness. My sister, whom I knew of old and over whom I watched from her earliest infancy; My bride, chosen from among all women, embraced by arms of love, and promised to Me forever." See how true it is that our royal Kinsman is not ashamed of us, for He dwells with obvious delight on this twofold relationship. We have the word "my" twice in our text, as if Christ lingered with deep joy over His possession of His church.

"His delight was in the sons of men," because those sons of men were His own chosen ones. He, the Shepherd, sought the sheep because they were His sheep; He came "to seek and to save the lost" because what was lost belonged to Him long before it was lost to itself or lost to Him. The church is the exclusive possession of her Lord; no one else may claim a partnership or presume to share her love. Jesus, Your church delights to have it so! Let every believing soul drink comfort from these wells. Soul, Christ is near to you in ties of kinship; Christ is dear to you in the bonds of marriage union, and you are dear to Him. Behold, He grasps both of your hands in His own, saying, "My sister, My bride." Take note of these two sacred bonds by which your Lord holds you with such a firm grasp that He neither can nor ever will let you go. Do not be slow, beloved, to return the holy flame of His love!

m.verse: ...The iniquity of the holy things...
paras: What a veil is lifted by these words, and what a revelation is made! It will be humbling and profitable for us to pause a moment and look upon this solemn sight. Consider the iniquities of our public worship: its hypocrisy, formality, lukewarmness, irreverence, wandering thoughts, and forgetfulness of God—what a full measure we find there! Consider our work for the Lord: its rivalry, selfishness, carelessness, negligence, and unbelief—what a mass of defilement is there! Consider our private devotions: their laxity, coldness, neglect, drowsiness, and vanity—what a heap of dead earth is there! If we examined ourselves more closely, we would find this iniquity to be far greater than it appears at first glance.

Dr. Payson, writing to his brother, said: "My church, as well as my heart, closely resembles the garden of the sluggard; and what is worse, I find that many of my desires for the improvement of both spring from pride, vanity, or laziness. I look at the weeds covering my garden and breathe out a heartfelt wish that they were uprooted. But why? What prompts the wish? It may be so that I can walk outside and say to myself, 'How orderly my garden is kept!' This is pride. Or it may be so that my neighbors will look over the wall and say, 'How beautifully your garden flourishes!' This is vanity. Or I may wish for the destruction of the weeds simply because I am tired of pulling them up. This is laziness." So it is that even our desires for holiness may be tainted by corrupt motives. Beneath the greenest grass, worms hide; we do not have to look long to find them. How comforting is the truth that when the high priest bore the iniquity of the holy things, he wore upon his forehead the engraving: "HOLY TO THE LORD." And in the same way, while Jesus bears our sin, He presents before His Father's face not our unholiness, but His own perfect holiness. Oh, for grace to look upon our great High Priest with the eyes of faith!

e.verse: ...Your love is more delightful than wine.
paras: Nothing gives the believer as much joy as fellowship with Christ. He finds enjoyment, as others do, in the common mercies of life; he can rejoice both in God's gifts and in God's works. Yet in all of these separately—yes, even in all of them combined—he does not find such deep satisfaction as in the matchless person of his Lord Jesus. He possesses wine that no vineyard on earth ever produced; he has bread that all the grainfields of Egypt could never produce. Where can such sweetness be found as that which we have tasted in communion with our Beloved? In our eyes, the joys of this earth are little better than pods for pigs compared with Jesus, the heavenly manna. We would rather have one taste of Christ's love and a single sip of His fellowship than an entire world full of earthly pleasures.

What is straw compared to grain? What is imitation glass to a genuine diamond? What is a dream compared to glorious reality? What is earthly merriment at its very best compared to our Lord Jesus in His most humble state? If you know anything of the inner spiritual life, you will confess that our highest, purest, and most enduring joys must be the fruit of the tree of life, which is in the paradise of God. No natural spring produces such sweet water as that well of God opened by the soldier's spear. All earthly happiness is worldly and fleeting, but the comforts of Christ's presence are like Himself: heavenly. We can look back on our communion with Jesus and find no emptiness in it; there is no bitter sediment in this wine, and no dead flies in this perfume. The joy of the Lord is solid and lasting. Vanity has never touched it, but wisdom and experience testify that it stands the test of the years, and in time and eternity is worthy to be called "the only true delight." For nourishment, comfort, strength, and refreshment, no wine can rival the love of Jesus. Let us drink deeply of it this evening!

m.verse: ...I will be their God...
paras: Christian, here is everything you could ever require! To be truly happy, you need something that completely satisfies you; and is this not enough? If you can pour this promise into your cup, will you not say with David, "My cup overflows; I have more than my heart could wish"? When this is fulfilled—"I will be your God"—are you not the possessor of all things? Human desire is as insatiable as death, but He who fills all things in every way can satisfy it. Who can measure the capacity of our desires? Yet the immeasurable wealth of God can more than fill them to overflowing. I ask you, are you not complete when God is yours? Do you need anything besides God? Is not His all-sufficiency enough to satisfy you even if everything else should fail?

Yet you need more than quiet satisfaction; you desire rapturous delight. Come, my soul, here is music fit for heaven in your inheritance, for God is the Maker of heaven. Not all the music played on sweet wind instruments or drawn from vibrant strings can produce such melody as this sweet promise: "I will be their God." Here is a deep sea of bliss, a shoreless ocean of delight! Come, bathe your spirit in it; swim for an age, and you will find no shore; dive through eternity, and you will find no bottom: "I will be their God." If this does not make your eyes sparkle and your heart beat high with joy, then surely your soul is not in a healthy state. But you desire more than present delights—you long for something upon which you may set your hope. And what more could you hope for than the fulfillment of this great promise: "I will be their God"? This is the masterpiece of all the promises; enjoying it creates a heaven below, and will make a heaven above. Dwell in the light of your Lord, and let your soul always be captivated by His love. Enjoy the rich nourishment this promise provides for you. Live up to your privileges, and rejoice with inexpressible joy!

e.verse: Serve the LORD with gladness...
paras: Delight in serving God is a true mark of acceptance. Those who serve God with a downcast face because their duty is unpleasant to them are not serving Him at all; they offer an outward form of worship, but the life is missing. Our God requires no unwilling slaves to surround His throne; He is the Lord of the kingdom of love, and desires His servants to be clothed in the garments of joy. The angels of God serve Him with songs, not with groans; a murmur or a sigh would be mutiny in their ranks. Obedience that is not willing is actually disobedience; for the Lord looks at the heart, and if He sees that we serve Him out of compulsion rather than love, He will reject our offering. Service joined with cheerfulness is true heart-service. Take away joyful willingness from a Christian, and you have removed the very proof of his sincerity.

If a soldier is forced into battle, he is no patriot; but the one who marches into the conflict with flashing eyes and a radiant face, singing that it is an honor to lay down his life for his country, proves his genuine patriotism. Cheerfulness sustains our strength; we are strong in the joy of the Lord. It removes our difficulties. It is to our service what oil is to the wheels of a train. Without oil, the axle soon overheats and accidents happen; and if we lack holy cheerfulness to lubricate our wheels, our spirits will quickly be bogged down with weariness. The one who is cheerful in serving God proves that obedience is his natural element; he can sing:

Make me to walk in Your commands,
'Tis a delightful road.

Reader, let us ask this question: Do you serve the Lord with gladness? Let us show the people of this world—who imagine our faith to be mere slavery—that to us it is pure delight and joy! Let our gladness proclaim that we serve a wonderful Master.

m.verse: ...There is laid up for me the crown of righteousness...
paras: Doubting soul, you have often said, "I fear I will never enter heaven." Fear not! All the people of God will enter there. I love the memorable saying of a dying man who exclaimed: "I have no fear of going home; I have sent all ahead of me. God's finger is on the latch of my door, and I am ready for Him to enter!" "But," someone asked, "are you not afraid that you might miss your inheritance?" "No," he answered, "no! There is one crown in heaven that the angel Gabriel could never wear; it will fit no head but mine. There is one throne in heaven that the apostle Paul could never fill; it was made for me, and I will have it." O Christian, what a joyous thought: your inheritance is secure! "There remains a Sabbath rest for the people of God."

"Can I not forfeit it?" No! It is guaranteed. If I am a child of God, I cannot lose it. It is mine as securely as if I were already there. Come with me, believer, and let us stand upon the top of Nebo and view that good land, even Canaan. Do you see that narrow river of death glistening in the sunlight? And across it, do you see the spires of the eternal city? Do you see that pleasant country and all its joyful inhabitants? Know, then, that if you could fly across, you would see written upon one of its many dwelling places: "This is reserved for this very person, kept for him alone. He will be caught up to dwell forever with God." Poor, doubting believer, look upon this glorious inheritance—it is yours! If you believe in the Lord Jesus, if you have repented of your sin, and if your heart has been renewed, you are one of the Lord's people. There is a place reserved for you, a crown laid up for you, and a harp prepared especially for you. No one else will ever take your inheritance; it is kept in heaven for you, and before long you will possess it. For there will be no empty thrones in glory when all the chosen are gathered home!

e.verse: ...Yet in my flesh I will see God.
paras: Notice the focus of Job's reverent anticipation: "I will see God." He does not say, "I will see the saints"—though that will certainly bring unspeakable happiness—but, "I will see God." It is not, "I will see the pearly gates; I will gaze on the walls of jasper; I will look upon the crowns of gold," but "I will see God." This is the very essence of heaven; this is the joyful hope of every believer. It is their delight to see Him now by faith in His Word and in the sacred ordinances of His church. They love to behold Him in communion and prayer; but there in heaven they will have an open, unclouded vision, and seeing "Him as He is," they will be made completely like Him. Likeness to God—what more could we desire? And the direct sight of God—what could be better?

Some translate this passage, "Yet in my flesh I will see God," finding here a reference to Christ as the "Word made flesh," and that glorious beholding of Him which will be the crowning splendor of the last days. Whether that is so or not, it is certain that Christ will be the supreme object of our eternal vision, and we will never desire any joy beyond seeing Him. Do not imagine that this will be a narrow sphere for the mind to inhabit. It is indeed only one source of delight, but that single source is infinite. All His divine attributes will be endless subjects for contemplation; and since He is infinite in every aspect, there is no possibility of exhausting them. His works, His gifts, His love toward us, and His glory displayed in all His purposes and actions will provide a theme that is ever fresh and new. The patriarch looked forward to this vision of God as a deeply personal joy: "My eyes will behold Him, and not as a stranger." Grasp the reality of heaven's bliss; consider what it will mean to you: "Your eyes will see the King in His beauty." All earthly brightness fades and darkens as we look upon it, but here is a brightness that can never dim, and a glory that can never fade: "I will see God!"

m.verse: ...They have no root...
paras: My soul, examine yourself this morning in the light of this text. You have received the word with joy; your feelings have been stirred, and a vivid impression has been made. Yet remember: to receive the word in the ear is one thing, but to receive Jesus into your very soul is quite another. Superficial emotion is often accompanied by an inward hardness of heart, and an emotional impression is not always an enduring one. In the parable, the seed fell upon ground with a rocky bedrock covered only by a thin layer of soil. When the seed began to take root, its downward growth was blocked by the hard stone; therefore, it spent all its energy pushing its green shoot upward as high as it could. But lacking the deep moisture that roots provide, it withered away.

Is this my condition? Have I been making an outward display of religion without an inner spiritual life to match? Healthy growth takes place upward and downward at the same time. Am I rooted in sincere faithfulness and love for Jesus? If my heart remains unsoftened and uncultivated by grace, the good seed may sprout for a season, but it must ultimately wither, for it cannot flourish upon a rocky, unbroken, unsanctified heart. Let me dread a profession of faith as rapid in growth and as lacking in endurance as Jonah's plant. Let me count the cost of following Jesus. Above all, let me experience the living power of His Holy Spirit; then I will possess an abiding and enduring seed in my soul. If my heart remains as stubborn as it was by nature, the scorching sun of trial will beat down, and my hard heart will only intensify the heat upon the seed planted in such shallow soil. Then my religion will quickly die, and my despair will be terrible. Therefore, O heavenly Sower, plow my heart first, and then scatter Your truth within me, that I may bring forth a rich harvest for You!

e.verse: ...I have prayed for you...
paras: How encouraging is the thought of the Redeemer's unending intercession for us! When we pray, He pleads for us; and when we are not praying, He is still advocating our cause, shielding us from unseen dangers through His petitions. Notice the word of comfort spoken to Peter: "Simon, Simon, Satan has asked to sift all of you like wheat; but"—what? "Go and pray for yourself"? That would be good advice, but that is not what is written. Nor does He say, "I will keep you watchful, and so you will be preserved"—though that would be a great blessing. No, He says: "But I have prayed for you, that your faith will not fail."

We little realize how much we owe to our Savior's prayers. When we reach the heights of heaven and look back upon all the way the Lord our God has led us, how we will praise Him who, before the eternal throne, dismantled the wicked schemes Satan was working against us on earth! How we will thank Him because He never remained silent, but day and night pointed to the wounds in His hands and carried our names upon His priestly breastplate! Even before Satan began to tempt, Jesus anticipated him and entered a plea in heaven. Mercy outruns malice! Notice, He does not merely say, "Satan has desired to have you"—He stops Satan in his very desire, nipping it in the bud. He does not say, "I wanted to pray for you." No, He says: "I have prayed for you. I have already done it; I have gone to court and filed a counter-plea before any accusation could even be made!" O Jesus, what a comfort it is that You have pleaded our cause against our unseen enemies, dismantled their secret plots, and exposed their ambushes! Here is true ground for joy, gratitude, hope, and confidence.

m.verse: ...You belong to Christ...
paras: "You belong to Christ." You are His by divine gift, for the Father gave you to the Son; His by blood-bought purchase, for He paid the full price for your redemption; His by dedication, for you have consecrated yourself to Him; His by kinship, for you are called by His name and made one of His brothers and joint-heirs. Work diligently to show the world that you are the servant, the friend, and the bride of Jesus. When tempted to sin, reply: "I cannot do this great wickedness, for I belong to Christ." Eternal principles forbid the friend of Christ to sin. When dishonest wealth is within your reach, declare that you belong to Christ, and do not touch it. Are you facing difficulties and dangers? Stand firm in the evil day, remembering that you belong to Christ.

Are you placed where others sit idle, doing nothing? Rise to your work with all your strength; and when sweat beads on your forehead and you are tempted to slack off, cry out: "No, I cannot stop, for I belong to Christ! If I were not bought with blood, I might be like Issachar, lying down between two burdens; but I belong to Christ, and I cannot be idle!" When the alluring song of pleasure tempts you from the path of righteousness, reply: "Your music cannot charm me; I belong to Christ." When the cause of God calls upon you, give your possessions and your very self away, for you belong to Christ. Never contradict your profession of faith. Always be among those whose conduct is gracious, whose speech reflects the Nazarene, and whose life and conversation are so filled with the fragrance of heaven that everyone who sees you may know you are the Savior's, recognizing in you His features of love and His character of holiness. "I am a Roman citizen!" was an ancient boast that demanded integrity. How much more, then, should this be your supreme reason for holiness: "I belong to Christ!"

e.verse: ...There is more to be said on God's behalf.
paras: We ought not to seek publicity for our virtues or notoriety for our zeal; yet at the same time, it is a sin to constantly conceal what God has bestowed upon us for the good of others. A Christian is not meant to be a secluded village in a valley, but "a city on a hill"; he is not to be a lamp under a basket, but a lamp on a stand, giving light to all who are in the house. Quiet solitude is pleasant in its proper season, and modesty is certainly commendable; but concealing Christ within us can never be justified. Withholding truth that is precious to us is a wrong against our neighbor and an offense against God. If you have a naturally timid personality and a retiring disposition, be careful not to indulge this fearful tendency, lest you become useless to the church. In the name of Him who was not ashamed of you, push past your natural reluctance and tell others what Christ has revealed to you.

If you cannot speak with the voice of a trumpet, use a gentle whisper. If the pulpit is not your platform and the printing press does not carry your words on its wings, you can still say with Peter and John: "Silver or gold I do not have, but what I have I give you." Beside Sychar's well, speak to the Samaritan woman if you cannot preach a sermon on the mountainside. Proclaim the praises of Jesus in the house if you cannot speak in the temple; in the open field if not in the bustling marketplace; and within your own household if not before the great family of mankind. From the hidden springs within you, let refreshing streams of testimony flow forth to give drink to every passerby. Do not bury your talent; put it to work, and you will bring a rich return to your Lord and Master. Speaking for God brings refreshment to our own souls, encouragement to the saints, help to sinners, and great honor to the Savior. Speechless children bring sorrow to their parents. Lord, loosen the tongues of all Your children!

m.verse: Jehoshaphat built ships of Tarshish to go to Ophir for gold, but they never set sail, because they were wrecked at Ezion-geber.
paras: Solomon's ships had returned in safety, but Jehoshaphat's vessels never reached the land of gold. Providence prospers one person and frustrates the desires of another, in the very same business and at the very same harbor; yet the Great Ruler is just as good and wise in the storm as in the calm. May we have grace today, as we remember this text, to praise the Lord for ships wrecked at Ezion-geber just as we praise Him for ships laden with earthly blessings. Let us not envy those who are more successful, nor grumble at our losses as though we were singled out for special trial. Like Jehoshaphat, we may be deeply precious in the Lord's sight, even though our plans end in disappointment.

The hidden cause of Jehoshaphat's failure is well worth our attention, for it lies at the root of much of the suffering of the Lord's people: his alliance with a sinful family, his partnership with sinners. In 2 Chronicles 20:37, we read that the Lord sent a prophet to declare: "Because you have allied yourself with Ahaziah, the LORD has destroyed your works." This was fatherly discipline, and it seems to have been deeply profitable to him; for in the verse immediately following our morning's text, we find him refusing to let his servants sail in the same ships with those of the wicked king. Would to God that Jehoshaphat's experience might serve as a solemn warning to all the Lord's people to avoid being unequally yoked together with unbelievers! A life of sorrow is almost always the lot of those who unite themselves in marriage, or in any other voluntary bond, with people of the world. Oh, for such love to Jesus that, like Him, we may be holy, innocent, undefiled, and set apart from sinners! For if it is not so with us, we may expect to hear it often said: "The LORD has destroyed your works."

e.verse: ...And made the iron float.
paras: The axe head seemed hopelessly lost; and because it was borrowed, the reputation of the company of prophets was in danger, and the honor of their God was at stake. Yet contrary to all human expectation, the iron rose from the bottom of the stream and floated; for what is impossible with man is possible with God. Only a few years ago, I knew a believer in Christ who was called to undertake a work that far exceeded his own strength. It seemed so difficult that the mere thought of attempting it appeared absurd. Yet he was called to it, and his faith rose to meet the occasion. God honored his faith, unexpected help arrived, and the iron floated! Another child of God was in severe financial distress. He had ample resources to pay all his debts if only he could sell a certain part of his property, but a sudden crisis overtook him. He looked to friends in vain, but faith led him to the unfailing Helper; and behold, the crisis was averted, his path was cleared, and the iron floated! A third had to deal with a heartbreaking case of deep-seated rebellion. He had taught, corrected, warned, invited, and prayed, but all in vain. The old sinful nature was too strong for the young reformer; the stubborn heart would not yield. Then came a desperate agony of prayer, and before long a wonderful answer was sent from heaven: the hard heart was broken, and the iron floated!

Beloved reader, what is your desperate situation? What heavy burden do you carry this evening? Bring it here. The God of the prophets still lives, and He lives to help His saints. He will not let you lack any good thing. Trust in the LORD of Hosts! Approach Him, pleading the name of Jesus, and the iron will float; you too will see the hand of God working wonders for His people. According to your faith, so let it be done for you—and once again the iron will float!

m.verse: ...Mighty to save.
paras: By the words "to save," we understand the whole of the great work of salvation, from the first holy desire onward to complete sanctification. These words are "much in little"—indeed, all mercy is gathered in this one phrase. Christ is not only "mighty to save" those who repent, but He is able to grant repentance. He will bring to heaven those who believe; but moreover, He is mighty to give people new hearts and create faith within them. He is mighty to make the one who hates holiness love it, and to compel those who despised His name to bow the knee before Him.

Yet this is not all, for divine power is seen just as clearly in the work that follows. The life of a believer is a continuous series of miracles worked by "the Mighty God." The bush burns with fire, but is never consumed. He is mighty to keep His people holy after He has cleansed them, and to preserve them in His fear and love until He brings their salvation to completion in heaven. Christ's power does not consist in making a person a believer and then leaving him to fend for himself. Rather, He who began the good work in you will carry it on to completion! He who implants the first spark of life in a dead soul sustains that divine life, strengthening it until it breaks every bond of sin, and the soul rises from this earth, perfected in glory.

Believer, here is true encouragement! Are you praying for a loved one? Oh, do not give up your prayers, for Christ is "mighty to save." You are powerless to turn the rebel, but your Lord is Almighty. Take hold of that mighty arm and plead with Him to put forth His power. Does your own condition trouble you? Do not be afraid, for His grace is sufficient for you. Whether in beginning the work in others or completing it in you, Jesus is "mighty to save"—and the clearest proof of this is that He has already saved you! What a boundless mercy that you did not find Him mighty to destroy!

e.verse: ...Beginning to sink, cried out, "Lord, save me!"
paras: Sinking times are praying times for the Lord's servants. Peter neglected prayer as he stepped out on his daring walk, but when he began to sink, his danger turned him into a pleading beggar; and his cry, though late, was not too late. In hours of bodily pain and mental anguish, we find ourselves as naturally driven to prayer as a shipwrecked vessel is driven ashore by the waves. The fox flees to its den for safety; the bird flies to the woods for shelter; and in the same way, the suffering believer runs to the throne of grace for refuge. Heaven's great harbor of refuge is prayer; thousands of weather-beaten ships have found safe harbor there, and the moment a storm strikes, wisdom tells us to hoist every sail and head straight for port.

Short prayers are long enough. There were only three words in the cry Peter gasped out, but they were entirely sufficient for his need. It is not length, but sincerity and faith that matter. A deep sense of need is a wonderful teacher of brevity. If our prayers had fewer of the peacock feathers of pride and more wings of faith, they would be far better! Empty words are to devotion what chaff is to wheat. Precious things come in small packages; and all that is genuine prayer in many a long, rambling address could easily have been spoken in a plea as brief as Peter's.

Our desperate extremities are the Lord's greatest opportunities. The moment a sharp sense of danger wrings an anxious cry from our lips, the ear of Jesus hears; and with Him, the ear and the heart move together, and His hand is never slow to act. We may appeal to our Master only at the very last moment, but His swift hand makes up for all our delays with immediate, saving power. Are we nearly swallowed up by the turbulent waters of affliction? Then let us lift our souls to our Savior, confident that He will never allow us to perish. When we can do nothing, Jesus can do all things. Let us call upon His mighty aid, and all will be well!

m.verse: ...Do as You have promised.
paras: God's promises were never meant to be thrown aside like scrap paper; He intended them to be used. God's gold is not a miser's hoard; it is minted to be put to use in trade. Nothing pleases our Lord more than to see His promises put into circulation. He loves to see His children bring them before Him and say, "Lord, do as You have promised!" We glorify God when we plead His promises. Do you think God will be any poorer for giving you the riches He has promised? Do you imagine He will be any less holy for giving holiness to you? Do you dream that He will be any less pure for washing you from your sins? He has said: "Come now, let us reason together, says the LORD. Though your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as snow; though they are as red as crimson, they will become like wool."

Faith takes hold of the promise of pardon and does not hesitate, wondering, "This is a precious promise, but can it really be true?" Instead, it goes straight to the throne of grace with it and pleads: "Lord, here is Your promise—do as You have promised!" Our Lord replies: "Let it be done for you as you desire!" When a Christian grasps a promise, if he fails to bring it to God, he dishonors Him. But when he runs to the throne of grace and cries, "Lord, I have nothing to plead in my favor except this: You have promised it!" then his request will be granted. Our heavenly Banker delights to honor His own promissory notes. Never let the promise gather rust! Draw the sword of promise from its scabbard, and wield it with holy boldness. Do not imagine that God will be annoyed by your persistent reminding Him of His promises. He loves to hear the earnest cries of needy souls. It is His delight to bestow grace. He is more ready to hear than you are to ask. The sun never tires of shining, nor the spring of flowing. It is God's very nature to keep His promises; therefore, go at once to the throne of grace, praying: "Do as You have promised!"

e.verse: ...But I am a man of prayer.
paras: Lying tongues were actively attacking David's reputation, but he did not defend himself; he appealed his case to a higher court and pleaded before the great King Himself. Prayer is the safest response to words of hatred. The Psalmist did not pray in a half-hearted manner; he gave himself fully to it, pouring his whole heart and soul into prayer—straining every spiritual muscle, just as Jacob did when wrestling with the angel. In this way, and only in this way, will any of us prevail at the throne of grace. Just as a shadow has no power because it has no substance, so a prayer in which a person's true self is not thoroughly engaged with heartfelt urgency and fervent desire is completely powerless, for it lacks the vital life that gives it strength. "Fervent prayer," said an old preacher, "like a cannon aimed at the gates of heaven, makes them fly wide open." The common fault with most of us is our quickness to surrender to distractions. Our thoughts wander here and there, and we make little real progress toward our goal. Like liquid mercury, our minds will not hold together, but scatter in every direction. What a serious evil this is! It harms us, and worse still, it dishonors our God. What would we think of a petitioner who, while granted an audience with a king, began playing with a feather or chasing a fly?

Continual perseverance is clearly implied in the words of our text. David did not cry out once and then slip back into silence; his holy, persistent crying continued until it brought down the blessing. Prayer must never be an occasional pastime, but our daily work, our lifelong habit, and our true calling. Just as artists dedicate themselves to their craft and writers to their studies, so must we devote ourselves to prayer. We must be immersed in prayer as our native element, and so "pray without ceasing." Lord, teach us to pray so that we may become increasingly effective in our intercession!

m.verse: ..."I will help you," declares the LORD...
paras: This morning, let us hear the Lord Jesus speak personally to each one of us: "I will help you." "It is only a small thing for Me, your God, to help you. Consider what I have done already! What—not help you? Why, I bought you with My own blood! What—not help you? I died for you; and if I have done the greater work, will I not do the lesser? Help you? That is the least thing I will ever do for you; I have done far more, and I will do far more! Before the world began, I chose you. I established the covenant for you. I laid aside My glory and became a man for you; I gave up My life for you; and if I did all this, I will surely help you now. In helping you, I am only giving you what I have already purchased for you. If you needed a thousand times more help, I would give it to you; you ask for very little compared to what I am prepared to give. It may seem like much for you to need, but it is nothing for Me to bestow. Help you? Do not be afraid! If an ant came to the door of your granary asking for food, it would not bankrupt you to give him a handful of your wheat; and you are only a tiny creature at the door of My all-sufficiency. I will help you!"

O my soul, is this not enough? Do you need more strength than the omnipotence of the Triune God? Do you desire more wisdom than exists in the Father, more love than is revealed in the Son, or more power than is displayed in the working of the Spirit? Bring your empty pitcher here! Surely this well will fill it to the brim. Hurry, gather up all your needs and bring them here—your emptiness, your sorrows, and your weaknesses. Behold, this river of God is overflowing to supply you; what more could you possibly desire? Go forward, my soul, in this divine strength! The Eternal God is your helper!

Fear not, I am with you, oh, be not dismayed!
I, I am your God, and will still give you aid.

e.verse: ...The Messiah will be cut off...
paras: Blessed be His name, there was no cause of death in Him! Neither original sin nor actual sin had ever defiled Him, and therefore death had no rightful claim upon Him. No one could have taken His life from Him justly, for He had wronged no one; nor could anyone have taken His life by force unless He had willingly surrendered Himself to die. Yet behold: one sins, and Another suffers! Divine justice was offended by us, but found its complete satisfaction in Him. Rivers of tears, mountains of offerings, oceans of animal blood, and hills of burning incense could never have sufficed to take away sin. But Jesus was cut off for us, and the cause of divine wrath was cut off at once, for sin was put away forever! Here is wisdom, by which substitution—the sure and perfect way of atonement—was ordained! Here is condescension, which brought Messiah the Prince to wear a crown of thorns and die upon a cross! Here is love, which led the Redeemer to lay down His life for His enemies!

Yet it is not enough merely to admire the spectacle of the Innocent bleeding for the guilty; we must be certain of our own personal share in it. The specific purpose of the Messiah's death was the salvation of His church: do we have a share and a place among those for whom He gave His life as a ransom? Did the Lord Jesus stand as our representative? Are we healed by His wounds? It would be a dreadful thing indeed to fall short of a share in His sacrifice; it would have been far better for us had we never been born! Solemn as this question is, it is a joyous truth that it can be answered clearly and with complete certainty. To all who believe in Him, the Lord Jesus is an ever-present Savior, and upon them all the blood of reconciliation has been sprinkled. Let all who trust in the merit of the Messiah's death rejoice at every remembrance of Him, and let their holy gratitude lead them to wholehearted consecration to His cause.

m.verse: Then I looked and saw the Lamb standing on Mount Zion...
paras: The apostle John was privileged to look inside the gates of heaven, and in describing what he saw, he begins by declaring: "I looked, and saw the Lamb!" This teaches us that the supreme focus of contemplation in heaven is "the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world." Nothing else captured the apostle's attention so completely as the person of that Divine Being who has redeemed us by His blood. He is the theme of the songs of all glorified spirits and holy angels. Christian, here is joy for you: you have looked, and you have seen the Lamb! Through your tears, your eyes have seen the Lamb of God taking away your sins. Rejoice, then!

In a little while, when every tear has been wiped from your eyes, you will see the same Lamb exalted upon His throne. It is the joy of your heart to enjoy daily fellowship with Jesus now; and you will possess that same joy in far greater measure in heaven: you will enjoy the uninterrupted vision of His presence, and you will dwell with Him forever. "I looked, and saw the Lamb!" Why, that Lamb is heaven itself; for as godly Samuel Rutherford said, "Heaven and Christ are the same thing." To be with Christ is to be in heaven, and to be in heaven is to be with Christ. That prisoner of the Lord wrote tenderly in one of his glowing letters: "O my Lord Jesus Christ, if I could be in heaven without You, it would be a hell; and if I could be in hell and have You still, it would be a heaven to me, for You are all the heaven I want!" This is true, is it not, Christian? Does your soul not say the same?

Not all the harps above
Can make a heavenly place,
If God His dwelling should remove,
Or only hide His face.
All you need to make you blessed—supremely blessed—is simply "to be with Christ."

e.verse: One evening David got up from his bed and strolled around on the roof of the palace...
paras: At that hour David saw Bathsheba. We are never beyond the reach of temptation. Both at home and abroad, we are liable to meet with allurements to evil; the morning opens with peril, and the shadows of evening find us still in danger. Those whom God protects are well protected, but woe to anyone who ventures out into the world, or even dares to walk through his own house, unarmed. Those who consider themselves secure are more exposed to danger than anyone else. The armor-bearer of Sin is Self-confidence.

David should have been engaged in fighting the Lord's battles; instead, he lingered in Jerusalem and surrendered himself to luxurious ease, rising from his bed at twilight. Idleness and luxury are the devil's jackals, providing him with abundant prey. In stagnant waters foul creatures swarm, and neglected soil soon produces a dense tangle of thorns and briers. Oh, for the compelling love of Jesus to keep us active and useful! When I see the king of Israel sluggishly rising from his couch at the close of the day and falling immediately into temptation, let me take warning, and place holy watchfulness to guard the door!

Is it possible that the king had gone up to his rooftop for quiet devotion? If so, what a solemn warning never to consider any place, no matter how private, a sanctuary from sin! While our hearts are like dry tinder and sparks are so plentiful, we must use all diligence everywhere to prevent a blaze. Satan can climb rooftops and enter our private prayer rooms; and even if we could shut out that foul enemy, our own corrupt desires are enough to cause our ruin unless grace intervenes! Reader, beware of evening temptations! Do not assume you are safe: the sun has set, but sin is wide awake. We need a watchman for the night just as much as a guardian for the day. O blessed Spirit, keep us from all evil this night. Amen.

m.verse: There remains, then, a Sabbath rest for the people of God.
paras: How different the believer's condition in heaven will be from what it is here! Here he is born to struggle and endure weariness, but in that immortal land, fatigue is never known. Eager to serve his Master, he finds his physical strength unequal to his zeal; his constant cry is, "Help me to serve You, O my God!" If he is truly active, he will have much work—not too much for his will, but more than enough for his strength, so that he cries out: "I am not weary of the work, but I am weary in it!" Ah, Christian, this scorching day of weariness will not last forever. The sun is nearing the horizon; and it will rise again upon a brighter day than you have ever seen, in a land where the saints serve God day and night, and yet rest from their work.

Here on earth, rest is only partial; there in glory, it is complete. Here, the Christian is always restless, knowing that he has not yet arrived. There, all are at rest: they have reached the summit of the mountain; they have ascended to the presence of their God. Higher they cannot go! Ah, weary worker, think of what it will be to rest forever! Can you even fathom it? It is an eternal rest—a rest that "remains." Here, my finest joys have "mortal" written on their brow: my lovely flowers wither; my finest cups are drained to the dregs; my sweetest songbirds fall before the arrows of death; my brightest days fade into dark nights; and the rising tides of my joy subside into ebbs of grief. But there, everything is immortal: the harp never rusts, the crown never fades, the eye never dims, the voice never falters, the heart never wavers, and our resurrected being is completely immersed in infinite delight! Happy day, happy day, when mortality is swallowed up by life, and the eternal Sabbath begins!

e.verse: ...He explained to them what was written in all the Scriptures about Himself.
paras: The two disciples on the road to Emmaus enjoyed a most profitable journey. Their companion and teacher was the best of tutors—an Interpreter one of a thousand, in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. The Lord Jesus condescended to become a preacher of the gospel, and He was not ashamed to exercise His calling before an audience of only two people; nor does He refuse today to become the teacher of even a single soul. Let us seek the company of so excellent an Instructor; for until He has become for us wisdom from God, we will never be wise unto salvation.

This peerless Teacher chose the best of all books as His textbook. Although fully able to reveal brand-new truth, He preferred to expound the old. In His omniscience, He knew the most effective way of teaching; and by turning at once to Moses and the Prophets, He showed us that the surest path to wisdom is not speculation, reasoning, or reading human books, but meditation upon the Word of God. The quickest way to become spiritually rich in heavenly knowledge is to dig in this diamond mine, and to gather pearls from this celestial sea. When Jesus Himself sought to enrich others, He worked in the quarry of Holy Scripture.

That favored pair were led to consider the greatest of themes, for Jesus spoke of Jesus, and explained what was written in the Scriptures concerning Himself. Here diamond cut diamond, and what could be more magnificent? The Master of the house unlocked His own doors, welcomed the guests to His table, and set His own banquet before them. He who hid the treasure in the field guided the searchers to it Himself. Our Lord would naturally speak on the sweetest of subjects, and He could find none sweeter than His own person and work: with an eye to these we should always search the Word. Oh, for grace to study the Bible with Jesus as both our Teacher and our Lesson!

m.verse: ...I sought him, but did not find him.
paras: Tell me where you lost the company of Christ, and I will tell you the most likely place to find Him. Have you lost Christ in your private prayer room by holding back prayer? Then it is there you must seek and find Him. Did you lose Christ through sin? You will find Christ in no other way than by giving up that sin, and seeking by the Holy Spirit to put to death the earthly desire in which lust dwells. Did you lose Christ by neglecting the Scriptures? You must find Christ in the Scriptures. It is a true proverb: "Look for a thing where you dropped it; it is there." So look for Christ where you lost Him, for He has not gone away. But it is hard work to retrace your steps for Christ. Bunyan tells us that the pilgrim found the stretch of road back to the Arbor of Ease, where he lost his scroll, the hardest he had ever traveled. Traveling twenty miles forward is easier than going one mile back for lost assurance.

Take care, then, when you find your Master, to cling close to Him. But how is it that you lost Him? One would have thought you would never have parted with such a precious Friend, whose presence is so sweet, whose words are so comforting, and whose company is so dear to you! How is it that you did not watch Him every moment for fear of losing sight of Him? Yet, since you have let Him go, what a mercy that you are seeking Him, even though you mournfully groan, "Oh, that I knew where I might find Him!" Keep on seeking, for it is dangerous to be without your Lord. Without Christ, you are like a sheep without its shepherd, like a tree without water at its roots, like a withered leaf in the tempest—not bound to the tree of life. Seek Him with your whole heart, and He will be found by you; only devote yourself completely to the search, and truly, you will yet discover Him to your joy and gladness.

e.verse: Then He opened their minds to understand the Scriptures.
paras: The One whom we saw yesterday evening opening the Scriptures, we see here opening the human mind. In the first work He has many fellow workers, but in the second He stands alone. Many can bring the Scriptures to the mind, but the Lord alone can prepare the mind to receive the Scriptures. Our Lord Jesus differs from all other teachers: they reach the ear, but He instructs the heart; they deal with the outward letter, but He imparts an inward taste for the truth, by which we perceive its true flavor and spirit. The most uneducated people become ripe scholars in the school of grace when the Lord Jesus, by His Holy Spirit, unfolds the mysteries of the kingdom to them and grants that divine anointing by which they can behold the invisible. How happy we are if our minds have been enlightened and strengthened by the Master! How many people of profound learning remain ignorant of eternal things! They know the killing letter of revelation, but its life-giving spirit they cannot discern; a veil rests upon their hearts that the eyes of carnal reason cannot penetrate. Such was our condition only a short time ago: we who now see were once utterly blind; truth was to us like beauty in the dark—unnoticed and neglected. If it were not for the love of Jesus, we would have remained in utter ignorance to this very moment; for without His gracious opening of our understanding, we could no more have attained spiritual knowledge than an infant could climb the Pyramids, or an ostrich fly up to the stars. Jesus' College is the only school in which God's truth can truly be learned: other schools may teach us what is to be believed, but Christ's alone can teach us how to believe it. Let us sit at the feet of Jesus, and by heartfelt prayer call upon His blessed help, that our dull minds may be sharpened and our feeble understanding may grasp heavenly things.

m.verse: ...Abel was a keeper of sheep...
paras: As a shepherd, Abel consecrated his work to the glory of God and offered a blood sacrifice upon his altar, and the Lord looked with favor on Abel and his offering. This early type of our Lord is remarkably clear and vivid. Like the first streak of light that colors the east at dawn, it does not reveal everything, but it plainly shows the great fact that the sun is rising. As we see Abel—both a shepherd and a priest—offering an aroma pleasing to God, we discern our Lord, who brings before His Father a sacrifice upon which the Lord always looks with delight. Abel was hated by his brother—hated without cause; and just so was our Savior: the worldly, unregenerate man hated the accepted man in whom the Spirit of grace dwelt, and did not rest until his blood was shed. Abel fell, sprinkling his altar and sacrifice with his own blood, and in this he foreshadows the Lord Jesus, slain by the hostility of man while ministering as a priest before the Lord. "The good Shepherd lays down His life for the sheep." Let us weep over Him as we behold Him slain by the hatred of mankind, staining the horns of His altar with His own blood! Abel's blood speaks: "The Lord said to Cain, The voice of your brother's blood cries out to Me from the ground." But the blood of Jesus has a far mightier voice, and the message of its prevailing cry is not vengeance, but mercy. It is precious beyond all measure to stand at the altar of our good Shepherd, to see Him bleeding there as our sacrificed Priest, and then to hear His blood speaking peace to all His flock—peace in our conscience, peace between Jew and Gentile, peace between man and his offended Maker, and peace through all the ages of eternity for blood-bought souls. Abel is the first shepherd in order of time, but our hearts will forever place Jesus first in order of preeminence. You great Keeper of the sheep, we, the people of Your pasture, bless You with all our hearts when we see You slain for us!

e.verse: Turn my eyes away from worthless things; revive me with Your word.
paras: There are many different kinds of vanity. The fool's cap and bells, the laughter of the world, the dance, the music, and the intoxicating cup of the reckless—all these are plainly recognized as worthless pursuits; they wear their true name stamped clearly upon their forehead. Far more deceitful are those equally vain distractions: the worries of this life and the deceptiveness of wealth. A person can chase vanity just as truly in an accounting office as in a theater. If someone spends his whole life merely accumulating wealth, he spends his days in an empty illusion. Unless we follow Christ and make our God the supreme goal of our lives, we differ only in appearance from the most frivolous people on earth. It is obvious, then, how deeply we need the second petition of our text: "Revive me in Your way!" The Psalmist confesses that he feels dull, heavy, lethargic—practically dead. Perhaps, dear reader, you feel the very same way. We are often so sluggish that even the highest motives fail to awaken us, apart from the Lord Himself. What! Will hell not revive me? Can I ponder perishing sinners and still remain asleep? Will heaven not revive me? Can I think of the reward awaiting the righteous and still be cold? Will death not revive me? Can I consider dying and standing before my God, and still be lazy in my Master's service? Will Christ's love not compel me? Can I contemplate His precious wounds and sit at the foot of His cross without being stirred with fervent zeal? Sadly, it seems so! No mere reflection can kindle our hearts to true devotion; God Himself must do it—hence the urgent cry: "Revive me!" The Psalmist pours out his entire being in passionate prayer: his body and his soul unite in this petition. "Turn away my eyes," prays the body; "Revive me," cries the soul. This is a fitting prayer for every single day. O Lord, answer it for me this night.

m.verse: And so all Israel will be saved...
paras: When Moses sang at the Red Sea, it was his joy to know that all Israel was safe. Not a single drop of spray fell from that solid wall of water until the last Israelite of God's flock had safely planted his foot on the other side of the sea. Once that was done, the waters immediately rushed back into their rightful place, but not until then. Part of that ancient song declared: "In Your loving devotion You have led forth the people whom You have redeemed." In the end of time, when the elect sing the song of Moses the servant of God and of the Lamb, it will be the joyful boast of Jesus: "Of those You have given Me, I have lost none." In heaven there will not be a single vacant throne.

For all the chosen race
Shall meet around the throne,
Shall bless the guidance of His grace,
And make His glories known.
As many as God has chosen, as many as Christ has redeemed, as many as the Spirit has called, and as many as believe in Jesus will safely cross the dividing sea. We are not all safely ashore yet:

Part of the host have crossed the flood,
And part are crossing now.

The vanguard of the army has already reached the shore. We are marching through the depths; today we are pressing hard after our Leader into the very heart of the sea. Let us take heart: the rearguard will soon stand where the vanguard already rests; the last of the chosen ones will soon cross the sea, and then the triumphant song will resound when everyone is safe. But oh, if even one were absent—if a single member of His chosen family should be cast away—it would cause an everlasting discord in the song of the redeemed, and snap the strings of the harps of paradise, so that no music could ever be drawn from them again!

e.verse: And being very thirsty, Samson cried out to the LORD, “You have accomplished this great deliverance through Your servant. Must I now die of thirst...”
paras: Samson was thirsty and ready to die. This difficulty was totally different from any that the hero had ever met before. Merely having thirst quenched is nothing like so great a matter as being delivered from a thousand Philistines! Yet when the thirst was upon him, Samson felt that small present difficulty to be far more weighty than the great past danger out of which he had been so remarkably delivered. It is very common for God's people, when they have enjoyed a great deliverance, to find a little trouble too much for them. Samson slays a thousand Philistines and piles them up in heaps, and then faints for a little water! Jacob wrestles with God at Peniel and overcomes Omnipotence itself, and then walks away limping upon his hip!
