It is strange that there must always be a shrinking of the sinew whenever we win the day—as if the Lord must teach us our own littleness and our nothingness in order to keep us within bounds. Samson boasted loudly when he said, "I have slain a thousand men." But his boastful throat soon grew hoarse with thirst, and he turned to prayer. God has many ways of humbling His people. Dear child of God, if after receiving great mercy you are laid very low, your case is not an unusual one. When David had mounted the throne of Israel, he confessed, "I am weak this day, though anointed king." You must expect to feel weakest when you are enjoying your greatest triumphs. If God has accomplished great deliverances for you in the past, your present difficulty is only like Samson's thirst; the Lord will not let you faint, nor will He permit the daughters of the uncircumcised to triumph over you. The road of sorrow is the road to heaven, but there are wells of refreshing water all along the route. So, tested brother, cheer your heart with Samson's words, and rest assured that God will deliver you before long.

m.verse: Son of man, how does the wood of the vine surpass any other branch among the trees in the forest?
paras: These words are meant to humble God's people. They are called God's vine, but what are they by nature more than anyone else? Through God's goodness, they have become fruitful, having been planted in good soil; the Lord has trained them along the walls of the sanctuary, and they bring forth fruit to His glory. But what are they without their God? What are they without the continuous influence of the Spirit, producing fruitfulness in them? O believer, learn to cast away pride, seeing that you have no ground for it! Whatever you are, you have nothing that should make you proud. The more you possess, the deeper you are in debt to God; and you should never be proud of that which makes you a debtor. Consider your origin; look back to what you once were. Consider what you would have been were it not for divine grace. Look upon yourself as you are now: does your conscience not reproach you? Do your thousand wanderings not rise up before you, telling you that you are unworthy to be called His child? And if He has made you anything of value, are you not taught by this that it is grace alone that made you to differ? Great believer, you would have been a great sinner if God had not made you differ. You who are valiant for the truth would have been just as valiant for error if grace had not laid hold of you. Therefore, do not be proud! Though you possess a rich estate—a broad domain of grace—you once had not a single thing to call your own except your sin and misery. Oh, what strange infatuation that you, who have borrowed everything, should ever dream of exalting yourself! You are a dependent recipient of your Savior's generosity, possessing a life that would wither without fresh streams from Jesus—and yet you are proud? Shame on you, foolish heart!

e.verse: ...Does Job fear God for nothing?
paras: This was the wicked question of Satan concerning that upright man of old, but there are many in our own day concerning whom it might justly be asked. They love God after a fashion simply because He prospers them; but if things went ill with them, they would abandon all their boasted faith in God. If they can clearly see that since the time of their supposed conversion worldly affairs have gone prosperously with them, then they will love God in their poor, carnal way; but if they endure adversity, they rebel against the Lord. Their love is the love of the banquet table, not of the Host; a love for the cupboard, not for the Master of the house. As for the true Christian, he expects to receive his reward in the life to come, and to endure hardship in this present world. The promise of the old covenant is prosperity, but the promise of the new is adversity. Remember Christ's words: "Every branch in Me that bears not fruit"—what? "He prunes it, that it may bring forth more fruit!" If you bear fruit, you will have to endure affliction. "Alas!" you say, "that is a terrible prospect." But this affliction works out such precious results that the Christian who is the subject of it must learn to rejoice in tribulations; because just as his tribulations abound, so his consolations abound through Christ Jesus. Rest assured: if you are a child of God, you will be no stranger to the rod. Sooner or later, every bar of gold must pass through the refining fire. Fear not, but rather rejoice that such fruitful seasons are in store for you; for in them you will be weaned from earth and made fit for heaven. You will be delivered from clinging to the present, and led to long for those eternal things that are so soon to be revealed to you. When you feel that as regards the present life you truly serve God for nothing, you will then rejoice in the infinite reward of the future.

m.verse: ...I have exalted one chosen from the people.
paras: Why was Christ chosen out of the people? Speak, my heart, for heart-thoughts are best! Was it not that He might be able to be our Brother, in the blessed tie of kindred blood? Oh, what a relationship exists between Christ and the believer! The believer can say: "I have a Brother in heaven; I may be poor, but I have a Brother who is rich and reigns as King, and will He allow me to be in need while He is upon His throne? Oh, no! He loves me; He is my Brother." Believer, wear this blessed truth like a necklace of diamonds around the neck of your memory; put it like a golden ring on the finger of your recollection, and use it as the King's own royal seal, stamping the petitions of your faith with confidence of success. He is a Brother born for adversity: treat Him as such.

Christ was also chosen out of the people that He might know our needs and sympathize with us. "He was tempted in every way, just as we are, yet without sin." In all our sorrows we have His tender sympathy. Temptation, pain, disappointment, weakness, weariness, poverty—He knows them all, for He has personally felt them all. Remember this, Christian, and let it comfort you. However difficult and painful your road may be, it is marked by the footsteps of your Savior; and even when you reach the dark valley of the shadow of death and the deep waters of the swelling Jordan, you will find His footprints there. Wherever we go, He has been our forerunner; every burden we must carry was once laid upon the shoulders of Immanuel.

His way was much rougher and darker than mine;
Did Christ, my Lord, suffer, and shall I repine?
Take courage! Royal feet have left a blood-red track upon the road, and consecrated the thorny path forever.

e.verse: ...We will praise Your love more than wine...
paras: Jesus will not let His people forget His love. If all the love they have enjoyed should ever be forgotten, He will visit them with fresh love. "Do you forget My cross?" says He. "I will cause you to remember it; for at My table I will manifest Myself anew to you. Do you forget what I did for you in the council-chamber of eternity? I will remind you of it, for you will need a Counselor, and you will find Me ready at your call." Mothers do not let their children forget them. If a boy has gone to Australia and does not write home, his mother writes: "Has John forgotten his mother?" Then there comes back a tender letter, which proves that the gentle reminder was not in vain. So it is with Jesus: He says to us, "Remember Me," and our response is, "We will praise Your love." We will remember Your love and its matchless history! It is as ancient as the glory which You had with the Father before the world began. We remember, O Jesus, Your eternal love when You became our divine Surety, and betrothed us to Yourself. We remember the love that conceived the sacrifice of Yourself—the love that, until the fullness of time, pondered that sacrifice and longed for the hour of which it was written of You in the scroll of the book: "Behold, I have come!" We remember Your love, O Jesus, as it was revealed to us in Your holy life, from the manger of Bethlehem to the garden of Gethsemane. We follow You from the cradle to the grave—for every word and deed of Yours was pure love—and we rejoice in Your love, which death could never extinguish; Your love which shone resplendent in Your resurrection. We remember that burning fire of love that will never let You remain silent until all Your chosen ones are safely gathered home, until Zion is glorified, and Jerusalem is established upon her everlasting foundations of light and love in heaven.

m.verse: Surely He will deliver you from the snare of the fowler...
paras: God delivers His people from the snare of the fowler in two senses: from it, and out of it. First, He delivers them from the snare—He does not let them enter it; and secondly, if they should be caught in it, He delivers them out of it. The first promise is the most precious to some; the second is the best to others.

"He will deliver you from the snare." How? Trouble is often the means by which God delivers us. God knows that our backsliding will soon end in our destruction, and He in mercy sends the rod. We say, "Lord, why is this?" not knowing that our trouble has been the means of delivering us from far greater evil. Many have been saved from ruin by their sorrows and their crosses; these have frightened the birds away from the net. At other times, God keeps His people from the snare of the fowler by giving them great spiritual strength, so that when tempted to do evil they say, "How can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?" But what a blessed thing it is that if the believer should, in an evil hour, come into the net, God will bring him out of it! O backslider, be cast down, but do not despair. Wanderer though you have been, hear what your Redeemer says: "Return, O backsliding children; I will have mercy upon you." But you say you cannot return, for you are a captive. Then listen to the promise: "Surely He will deliver you from the snare of the fowler." You will yet be brought out of all the evil into which you have fallen; and though you will never cease to repent of your ways, yet He who has loved you will not cast you away. He will receive you, and give you joy and gladness, that the bones which He has broken may rejoice. No bird of paradise will die in the fowler's net.

e.verse: ...Martha was distracted by all the preparations to be made...
paras: Her fault was not that she served: the role of a servant well becomes every Christian. "I serve" should be the motto of all the princes of the royal family of heaven. Nor was it her fault that she had much serving to do. We cannot do too much for Christ. Let us do all that we possibly can; let head, and heart, and hands all be engaged in the Master's service. It was no fault of hers that she was busy preparing a feast for the Master. Happy Martha, to have the privilege of entertaining so blessed a Guest; and happy, too, to have the devoted spirit to throw her whole heart so warmly into the task! Her fault was that she grew distracted by all her preparations, so that she forgot Him, and only remembered the service. She allowed service to override communion, and so presented one duty stained with the blood of another. We ought to be Martha and Mary in one: we should do much service, and enjoy much communion at the same time. For this we need abundant grace. It is far easier to serve than to commune. Joshua never grew weary while fighting with the Amalekites; but Moses, on the top of the mountain in prayer, needed two helpers to sustain his hands. The more spiritual the exercise, the sooner we tire in it. The choicest fruits are the hardest to grow; the most heavenly graces are the most difficult to cultivate. Beloved, while we must never neglect outward duties, which are good in themselves, we must also see to it that we enjoy living, personal fellowship with Jesus. See to it that sitting at the Savior's feet is not neglected, even under the shallow excuse of serving Him. The first requirement for our soul's health, the first for His glory, and the first for our usefulness, is to abide in constant communion with the Lord Jesus, ensuring that the vital spirituality of our faith is maintained above everything else in the world.

m.verse: I will make known the LORD’s loving devotion and His praiseworthy acts, because of all that the LORD has done for us...
paras: And can you not do this? Are there no mercies you have personally experienced? What though you are gloomy now, can you forget that blessed hour when Jesus met you and said, "Come unto Me"? Can you not remember that rapturous moment when He snapped your fetters, dashed your chains to the earth, and said, "I came to break your bonds and set you free"? Or if the love of your betrothal is forgotten, there must surely be some precious milestone along the road of life not quite overgrown with moss, on which you can read a happy memorial of His mercy toward you! Did you never endure an illness like the one you suffer now, and did He not restore you? Were you never poor before, and did He not supply your needs? Were you never in distress before, and did He not deliver you? Arise! Go to the river of your experience, pull up a few reeds, and weave them into an ark in which your infant faith may float safely upon the stream. Do not forget what your God has done for you: open the book of your remembrance, and consider the days of old. Can you not remember the hill Mizar? Did the Lord never meet with you at Mount Hermon? Have you never climbed the Delectable Mountains? Have you never been helped in your hour of need? No, I know you have! Go back, then, a little way to the choice mercies of yesterday; and though all may seem dark now, light up the lamps of the past. They will shine through the darkness, and you will trust in the Lord until the day breaks and the shadows flee away. "Remember, O Lord, Your compassion and Your loving devotion, for they are from of old."

e.verse: Do we, then, nullify the law by this faith? Certainly not! Instead, we uphold the law.
paras: When the believer is adopted into the Lord's family, his relationship to the old Adam and the law ceases at once; he is now under a new rule and a new covenant. Believer, you are God's child; it is your first duty to obey your heavenly Father. You have nothing to do with a servile spirit: you are not a slave, but a child. Inasmuch as you are a beloved child, you are bound to obey your Father's faintest wish and the least intimation of His will. Does He command you to observe a sacred ordinance? It is at your peril that you neglect it, for you will be disobeying your Father. Does He tell you to reflect the image of Jesus? Is it not your joy to do so? Does Jesus tell you, "Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect"? Then not because the law commands, but because your Savior enjoins, you will strive to be perfect in holiness. Does He command His saints to love one another? Do it, not because the law says, "Love your neighbor," but because Jesus says, "If you love Me, keep My commandments"; and this is the commandment He has given you: "Love one another." Are you told to help the poor? Do it, not because charity is a burden you dare not shirk, but because Jesus teaches, "Give to the one who asks you." Does the Scripture say, "Love the Lord your God with all your heart"? Look at that command and answer: "O commandment, Christ has fulfilled you already! I have no need to fulfill you for my salvation, but I rejoice to offer wholehearted obedience to you because God is my Father now, and He has a rightful claim upon me which I will never dispute." May the Holy Spirit make your heart obedient to the compelling power of Christ's love, that your prayer may be: "Direct my steps in the path of Your commandments, for in it I delight." Grace is the mother and nurse of holiness, never the apologist for sin.

m.verse: ...Your heavenly Father...
paras: God's people are doubly His children: they are His offspring by creation, and they are His sons by adoption in Christ. Therefore, they are privileged to call Him, "Our Father in heaven." Father! Oh, what a precious word that is! Here is authority: "If I am a Father, where is My honor?" If you are sons, where is your obedience? Here is affection blended with authority—an authority that never provokes rebellion, and an obedience that is most cheerfully rendered, which would not be withheld even if it could be. The obedience that God's children offer to Him must be a loving obedience. Do not go about the service of God like slaves driven to a taskmaster's work, but run in the way of His commands because it is your Father's way. Present your bodies as instruments of righteousness, because righteousness is your Father's will, and His will should be the joy of His child. Father! Here is a kingly attribute so sweetly veiled in love that the King's crown is forgotten in the King's face, and His scepter becomes, not a rod of iron, but a silver scepter of mercy—the scepter indeed seems almost forgotten in the tender hand of Him who wields it! Father! Here is honor and love. How great is a Father's love for His children! That which friendship cannot do, and mere benevolence will not attempt, a Father's heart and hand will gladly do for His sons. They are His offspring; He must bless them. They are His children; He must show Himself strong in their defense. If an earthly father watches over his children with unceasing love and care, how much more does our heavenly Father? Abba, Father! The soul that can say this has uttered sweeter music than cherubim or seraphim can ever reach. There is heaven in the depth of that word—Father! There is all I can ask, all my needs can require, all my desires can seek. I have all in all for all eternity when I can say, "Father!"

e.verse: ...All who heard it were amazed at what the shepherds said to them.
paras: We must not cease to wonder at the great marvels of our God. It would be very difficult to draw a dividing line between holy wonder and real worship; for when the soul is overwhelmed with the majesty of God's glory, though it may not express itself in song, or even utter its voice with bowed head in humble prayer, yet it silently adores. Our incarnate God is to be worshipped as "the Wonderful." That God should consider His fallen creature, man, and instead of sweeping him away with the broom of destruction, should Himself undertake to be man's Redeemer and to pay his ransom price, is marvelous indeed! But to each believer, redemption is most marvelous as he views it in relation to himself. It is a miracle of grace indeed that Jesus should forsake the thrones and royal dignities above, to suffer in shame and humiliation below for you. Let your soul lose itself in wonder, for wonder is in this way a very practical emotion. Holy wonder will lead you to grateful worship and heartfelt thanksgiving. It will produce within you a godly watchfulness; you will be afraid to sin against such extraordinary love as this. Feeling the presence of the mighty God in the gift of His dear Son, you will take off your sandals from your feet, because the place where you stand is holy ground. You will be moved at the same time to a glorious hope: if Jesus has done such marvelous things on your behalf, you will feel that heaven itself is not too great for your expectation. Who can be astonished at anything, when he has once been astonished at the manger and the cross? What is there wonderful left to marvel at after one has seen the Savior? Dear reader, it may be that from the quietness and solitude of your life, you are scarcely able to imitate the shepherds of Bethlehem, who recounted what they had seen and heard; but you can, at least, complete the circle of the worshippers before the throne, by wondering at what God has done.

m.verse: From His fullness we have all received...
paras: These words declare to us that there is an inexhaustible fullness in Christ. There is a fullness of essential Deity, for "in Him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead in bodily form." There is a fullness of perfect manhood, for in Him that divine nature was bodily revealed. There is a fullness of atoning power in His blood, for "the blood of Jesus Christ, His Son, cleanses us from all sin." There is a fullness of justifying righteousness in His life, for "there is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus." There is a fullness of prevailing power in His intercession, for "He is able to save completely those who come to God through Him, since He always lives to intercede for them." There is a fullness of victory in His death, for through death He destroyed the one who held the power of death, that is, the devil. There is a fullness of triumph in His resurrection, for by it "He has given us new birth into a living hope." There is a fullness of glory in His ascension, for "when He ascended on high, He led captives in His train and gave gifts to men." There is a fullness of blessings of every kind: a fullness of grace to pardon, of grace to regenerate, of grace to sanctify, of grace to preserve, and of grace to bring us to perfection. There is a fullness for every season: a fullness of comfort in affliction, and a fullness of guidance in prosperity. There is a fullness of every divine attribute—of wisdom, of power, of love—a boundless ocean which it would be impossible to survey, much less to fathom. "For God was pleased to have all His fullness dwell in Him." Oh, what a fullness must this be, from which we all receive! A river of grace must surely flow without end when the fountain springs up as free, as rich, and as full as ever! Come, believer, and have all your needs supplied; ask abundantly, and you will receive abundantly, for this fullness is infinite, and is treasured up where every needy soul may reach it—in Jesus, Immanuel, God with us.

e.verse: But Mary treasured up all these things and pondered them in her heart.
paras: In the response of this blessed woman, we witness the active engagement of three great faculties of her soul: her memory—she kept all these things; her affections—she kept them in her heart; and her intellect—she pondered them. Thus her memory, affection, and understanding were all reverently engaged with the wondrous truths she had heard. Beloved, remember what you have heard concerning your Lord Jesus, and what He has accomplished for your soul. Make your heart a golden urn of manna to preserve the sacred memory of that heavenly bread on which you have fed in days gone by. Let your memory treasure up everything about Christ that you have felt, known, or believed, and then let your deepest affections hold Him fast forever. Love the person of your Lord! Bring forth the alabaster jar of your heart, even though it be broken, and let all the precious fragrance of your devotion pour over His pierced feet. Let your intellect also be exercised upon the Lord Jesus. Meditate deeply upon what you read: do not merely skim the surface, but plunge into the depths. Do not be like the swallow that merely touches the water with its wing, but like the fish that dives into the deepest wave. Abide with your Lord: do not let Him be to you like a passing traveler who stays only for a night, but urge Him, saying, "Stay with us, for the day is nearly spent!" Hold Him fast, and do not let Him go! The word "ponder" means to weigh. Prepare the scales of holy contemplation. Yet where are the balances that can ever weigh the Lord Christ? "He lifts up the islands like fine dust"—who can weigh Him? "He weighs the mountains on the scales"—in what balance shall we weigh Him? If your understanding cannot fully comprehend Him, let your heart apprehend Him; and if your mind cannot encompass the Lord Jesus in the grasp of reason, let your soul embrace Him in the arms of love!

m.verse: ...perfect in Christ.
paras: Do you not feel in your own soul that perfection is not in you? Does not every day teach you that? Every tear that trickles from your eye weeps "imperfection"; every harsh word from your lips mutters "imperfection." You have looked into your own heart too often to dream for a moment of any perfection in yourself. Yet amid this sad consciousness of imperfection, here is comfort for you: you are "perfect in Christ Jesus!" In the sight of God, you are "complete in Him"; even now you are "accepted in the Beloved."

There is a second perfection, yet to be realized, which is sure to all the seed. Is it not delightful to look forward to the time when every stain of sin will be removed from the believer, and he will be presented faultless before the throne, without spot or wrinkle or any such blemish? The Church of Christ will then be so pure that not even the eye of Omniscience will detect a spot or blemish in her; so holy and so glorious that Hart did not go beyond the truth when he said—

With my Savior's garments on,
Holy as the Holy One.

Then we will know, and taste, and feel the happiness of this vast but short sentence: "Complete in Christ." Not until then will we fully comprehend the heights and depths of the salvation of Jesus. Does your heart not leap for joy at the thought of it? Dark with sin though you are, you will one day be white as snow; stained though you are, you will be clean. Oh, it is a marvelous salvation, this! Christ takes a worm and transforms it into an angel; Christ takes a dark and deformed creature and makes it clean, radiant in His glory, peerless in His beauty, and fit to be the companion of seraphs. O my soul, stand and admire this blessed truth of perfection in Christ!

e.verse: The shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all they had heard and seen, which was just as the angel had told them.
paras: What was the subject of their praise? They praised God for what they had heard—for the good tidings of great joy that a Savior was born to them. Let us copy them; let us also raise a song of thanksgiving that we have heard of Jesus and His salvation. They also praised God for what they had seen. There is the sweetest music: what we have experienced, what we have felt within, what we have made our own—"the things concerning the King." It is not enough merely to hear about Jesus: hearing may tune the harp, but the fingers of living faith must awaken the melody. If you have seen Jesus with the God-given sight of faith, allow no cobwebs to gather upon the strings of your harp, but awake your harp and lyre to sound the praises of sovereign grace! One reason they praised God was the agreement between what they had heard and what they had seen. Observe the last sentence: "Just as the angel had told them." Have you not found the gospel in your own experience to be exactly what the Bible said it would be? Jesus promised to give you rest—have you not enjoyed the sweetest peace in Him? He said that you would have joy, comfort, and life through believing in Him—have you not received all these? Are His ways not ways of pleasantness, and all His paths paths of peace? Surely you can say with the queen of Sheba, "The half was not told me!" I have found Christ far sweeter than His servants ever said He was. I looked upon His likeness as they painted it, but it was a mere rough sketch compared with Himself; for the King in His beauty outshines all imaginable loveliness. Surely what we have seen keeps pace with, indeed far exceeds, what we have heard. Let us, then, glorify and praise God for a Savior so precious and so satisfying!

m.verse: ...what is unseen...
paras: In our Christian pilgrimage it is well, for the most part, to be looking forward. Forward lies the crown, and onward is the goal. Whether for hope, for joy, for consolation, or for the rekindling of our love, the future must always be the grand focus for the eye of faith. Looking into the future, we see sin cast out, the body of sin and death destroyed, the soul made perfect, and fit to be a partaker of the inheritance of the saints in light. Looking further still, the believer's enlightened eye can see death's river passed, the gloomy stream safely forded, and the hills of light attained on which stands the celestial city. He sees himself enter within the pearly gates, hailed as more than a conqueror, crowned by the hand of Christ, embraced in the arms of Jesus, glorified with Him, and seated beside Him on His throne, even as He overcame and sat down with the Father on His throne! The contemplation of this future may well dispel the darkness of the past and the gloom of the present. The joys of heaven will surely compensate for all the sorrows of earth. Hush, hush, my doubts! Death is only a narrow stream, and you will soon have crossed it. Time, how short—eternity, how long! Death, how brief—immortality, how endless! It seems as though I even now taste the clusters of Eshcol, and drink from the well within the gate. The road is so very short! I will soon be there.

When the world my heart is rending
With its heaviest storm of care,
My glad thoughts to heaven ascending
Find a refuge from despair.
Faith's bright vision will sustain me
Till life's pilgrimage is past;
Fears may vex and troubles pain me,
I shall reach my home at last.

e.verse: ...the dove returned to him in the evening...
paras: Blessed be the Lord for another day of mercy, even though I am now weary with its work. To the Preserver of men I lift my song of gratitude! The dove found no resting place outside the ark, and therefore returned to it; and my soul has learned yet more fully than ever this day that there is no lasting satisfaction to be found in earthly things—God alone can give true rest to my spirit. As to my business, my possessions, my family, and my accomplishments, these are all well enough in their place, but they can never satisfy the longings of my immortal nature. "Return to your rest, O my soul, for the Lord has been good to you." It was at the quiet evening hour, when the gates of the day were closing, that with weary wing the dove came back to her master: O Lord, enable me this evening to return to Jesus! She could not bear to spend the night hovering over a restless wasteland, nor can I endure to be away from Jesus even for another hour—He who is the rest of my heart and the home of my spirit. She did not merely alight upon the roof of the ark; she came inside to him. Even so would my longing spirit look into the secret counsel of the Lord, penetrate to the heart of truth, enter within the veil, and reach my Beloved in truth. To Jesus I must come; short of the nearest and sweetest fellowship with Him, my longing spirit cannot rest. Blessed Lord Jesus, be with me, reveal Yourself, and abide with me throughout the night, so that when I awake I may still be with You. I observe that the dove brought in her beak a freshly plucked olive leaf—the memorial of the past day and a promise of the future. Have I no joyful record to bring home? No pledge and guarantee of loving devotion yet to come? Yes, my Lord, I offer You my grateful praise for tender mercies that have been new every morning and fresh every evening; and now, I pray You, reach out Your hand and take Your dove into Your bosom!

m.verse: As soon as you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, move quickly...
paras: The members of Christ's Church should be very prayerful, always seeking the anointing of the Holy One to rest upon their hearts, that the kingdom of Christ may come, and that His will may "be done on earth as it is in heaven." But there are times when God seems especially to favor Zion; such seasons ought to be to His people like "the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees." We ought then to be doubly prayerful, doubly earnest, pleading more fervently at the throne of grace than has been our custom. Action must then be prompt and vigorous. The tide is flowing—now let us pull manfully for the shore! Oh, for Pentecostal outpourings and Pentecostal work! Christian, in your own soul there are times when you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees. You feel a special power in prayer; the Spirit of God gives you joy and gladness; the Scripture is opened to your heart; the promises are applied; you walk in the light of God's countenance; you experience a special freedom in devotion and a closer communion with Christ than has been your custom. Now, at such joyful periods, when you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, is the time to stir yourself! Now is the time to put away every evil habit, while the Spirit helps your weaknesses. Spread your sail; but remember what you sometimes sing:

I can only spread the sail;
You, You must breathe the auspicious gale!

Only be sure you have the sail hoisted. Do not miss the heavenly breeze for lack of preparation. Seek help from God, that you may be more earnest in duty when made stronger in faith; that you may be more constant in prayer when you have greater freedom at the throne; and that you may be holy in all your speech and conduct while you live in closer fellowship with Christ.

e.verse: In Him we were also chosen as God’s own...
paras: When Jesus gave Himself for us, He gave us all the rights and privileges that belong to Him; so that now, although as eternal God He possesses essential rights to which no creature may ever dare lay claim, yet as Jesus the Mediator, the federal Head of the covenant of grace, He has no heritage apart from us. All the glorious consequences of His obedience unto death are the shared riches of all who are in Him, and on whose behalf He accomplished the divine will. See: He enters into glory, but not for Himself alone, for it is written, "where Jesus our forerunner has entered on our behalf." Does He stand in the presence of God? "He appears in the presence of God for us." Consider this, believer: you have no right to heaven in yourself; your entire right lies in Christ. If you are pardoned, it is through His blood; if you are justified, it is through His righteousness; if you are sanctified, it is because He has been made by God your sanctification; if you are kept from falling, it is because you are preserved in Christ Jesus; and if you are perfected at last, it will be because you are complete in Him. Thus Jesus is magnified, for all is in Him and through Him; thus the inheritance is made sure to us, for it is obtained in Him; thus each blessing is all the sweeter, and heaven itself the brighter, because it is Jesus our Beloved in whom we have obtained it all. Where is anyone who can calculate our divine portion? Weigh the riches of Christ on scales and His wealth in balances, and only then attempt to count the treasures that belong to the saints! Reach the bottom of Christ's ocean of joy, and only then hope to fathom the bliss that God has prepared for those who love Him. Step beyond the boundaries of Christ's possessions, and only then dream of a limit to the glorious inheritance of the elect: "All things are yours... and you belong to Christ, and Christ belongs to God."

m.verse: ...The LORD Our Righteousness.
paras: It will always bring a Christian the greatest calm, quiet, rest, and peace to reflect upon the perfect righteousness of Christ. How often are the saints of God downcast and sad! I do not think they ought to be; nor do I think they would be if they could only keep their perfection in Christ continually in view. There are some who are always talking about their corruptions, the depravity of the heart, and the innate evil of the soul. This is entirely true; but why not go a step further and remember that we are "perfect in Christ Jesus"? It is no wonder that those who dwell upon their own corruption wear such downcast looks; but surely if we remember that "Christ has become for us righteousness," we will be of good cheer! Even though troubles afflict me, though Satan assault me, and though there may be many things to experience before I reach heaven, all these are provided for in the covenant of divine grace. There is nothing lacking in my Lord; Christ has done it all! On the cross He said, "It is finished!" And if it is finished, then I am complete in Him, and can rejoice with an inexpressible and glorious joy: "not having a righteousness of my own that comes from the law, but that which is through faith in Christ—the righteousness that comes from God on the basis of faith." You will not find on this side of heaven a holier people than those who receive into their hearts the doctrine of Christ's righteousness. When the believer says, "I live on Christ alone; I rest solely on Him for salvation; and I believe that, however unworthy, I am still saved in Jesus," then there rises up as a motive of gratitude this thought: "Shall I not live for Christ? Shall I not love Him and serve Him, seeing that I am saved by His merits?" "For Christ's love compels us... that those who live should no longer live for themselves, but for Him who died for them." If saved by imputed righteousness, we will greatly value imparted righteousness.

e.verse: ...Ahimaaz ran by way of the plain and outran the Cushite.
paras: Running is not everything; there is much in the path we select. A swift foot over hill and down dale will not keep pace with a slower traveler upon level ground. How is it with my spiritual journey? Am I toiling up the hill of my own works and down into the ravines of my own humiliations and resolutions, or do I run along the plain way of "Believe and live"? How blessed it is to wait upon the Lord by faith! The soul runs without weariness and walks without fainting in the way of believing. Christ Jesus is the way of life, and He is a plain way, a pleasant way, a way suited for the tottering feet and feeble knees of trembling sinners. Am I found in this way, or am I chasing after another track that ritual or human philosophy promises me? I read of the way of holiness that the traveler, though a fool, will not err in it: have I been delivered from proud reason and brought as a little child to rest in Jesus' love and blood? If so, by God's grace I will outrun the strongest runner who chooses any other path! This truth I may remember to my profit in my daily cares and needs. It will be my wisest course to go at once to my God, and not to wander in a roundabout manner to this friend and that. He knows my needs and can relieve them; to whom should I go but to Himself by the direct appeal of prayer and the plain argument of the promise? "Straightforward makes the best runner." I will not linger with the servants, but hasten directly to their Master.

In reading this passage, it strikes me that if men vie with one another in earthly matters and one outruns the other, I ought to be in solemn earnestness so to run that I may obtain the prize! Lord, help me to prepare my mind for action, and may I press forward toward the goal for the prize of the heavenly calling of God in Christ Jesus!

m.verse: They will sing of the ways of the LORD...
paras: The time when Christians begin to sing in the ways of the Lord is when they first lose their burden at the foot of the cross. Not even the songs of the angels seem so sweet as that first song of rapture that gushes from the inmost soul of a forgiven child of God. You know how John Bunyan describes it: he says that when poor Pilgrim lost his burden at the cross, he gave three great leaps and went on his way singing:

Blest cross! blest sepulcher! blest rather be
The Man who there was put to shame for me!

Believer, do you remember the day when your fetters fell off? Do you remember the place where Jesus met you and said, "I have loved you with an everlasting love; I have blotted out your transgressions like a cloud, and your sins like a thick cloud; they will never be mentioned against you again forever"? Oh, what a sweet season it is when Jesus takes away the agonizing guilt of sin! When the Lord first pardoned my sin, I was so joyful that I could scarcely refrain from dancing! I thought on my walk home from the house where I had been set at liberty that I must tell the very stones in the street the story of my deliverance. So full was my soul of joy that I wanted to tell every snowflake falling from heaven of the wondrous love of Jesus, who had blotted out the sins of one of the chief of rebels! But it is not only at the beginning of the Christian life that believers have reason for song: as long as they live, they discover fresh cause to sing in the ways of the Lord; and their experience of His constant loving devotion leads them to declare, "I will bless the Lord at all times; His praise will continually be in my mouth." See to it, my brother, that you magnify the Lord this day!

Long as we tread this desert land,
New mercies shall new songs demand.

e.verse: ...Your love to me was extraordinary...
paras: Come, dear readers, let each one of us speak for himself of the wonderful love, not of Jonathan, but of Jesus. We will not relate merely what we have been told, but the things that we have personally tasted and touched of the love of Christ. Your love to me, O Jesus, was extraordinary when I was a stranger wandering far from You, fulfilling the desires of the flesh and of the mind. Your love restrained me from committing the sin that leads to death, and preserved me from self-destruction. Your love held back the axe when divine Justice cried, "Cut it down! Why should it clutter the ground?" Your love drew me into the wilderness, stripped me there, and made me feel the heavy guilt of my sin and the crushing burden of my iniquity. Your love spoke so tenderly to me when I was deeply dismayed: "Come to Me, and I will give you rest." Oh, how matchless was Your love when, in a single moment, You washed my sins away, and made my polluted soul—stained with the guilt of my birth and blackened by the grime of my transgressions—to be white as the driven snow, and pure as the finest wool! How You displayed Your love when You whispered in my ear, "I am yours, and you are Mine." Kind were those gentle words when You said, "The Father Himself loves you"; and passing sweet were the moments when You revealed to me the deep love of the Spirit! Never will my soul forget those secret chambers of communion where You unveiled Yourself to me. Moses had his cleft in the rock, where he saw the trailing glory of his God; and we, too, have had our clefts in the rock, where we have beheld the full splendor of the Godhead in the person of Christ! Did David remember the haunts of the wild goats, the land of Jordan, and the heights of Hermon? We, too, can remember sacred places dear to memory, equal to these in blessedness. Precious Lord Jesus, give us a fresh drink of Your wondrous love to begin this month with! Amen.

m.verse: ...without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.
paras: This is the voice of unalterable truth. In none of the Jewish ceremonies were sins, even symbolically, removed without the shedding of blood. In no case and by no means can sin ever be pardoned without an atonement. It is clear, then, that there is no hope for me outside of Christ; for there is no other sacrifice worth a thought as an atonement for sin. Am I, then, believing in Him? Is the blood of His atonement truly applied to my soul? All men stand on the same level in their desperate need of Him. Even if we are exceptionally moral, generous, amiable, or patriotic, the rule will never be altered to make an exception for us. Sin will give way to nothing less potent than the blood of Him whom God has set forth as a propitiation. What a boundless blessing that there is this one way of pardon! Why should we ever seek another?

People of merely formal religion cannot understand how we can rejoice that all our sins are forgiven for Christ's sake. Their works, their prayers, and their rituals afford them very poor comfort; and well may they be uneasy, for they are neglecting the one great salvation, attempting to obtain forgiveness without blood. My soul, sit down and behold the justice of God as bound to punish sin; see that punishment fully executed upon your Lord Jesus, and fall down in humble joy to kiss the pierced feet of Him whose blood has made atonement for you! When conscience is aroused, it is utterly useless to flee to subjective feelings or inward evidences for comfort: that is a habit we learned in the Egypt of our legal bondage. The only true remedy for a guilty conscience is a sight of Jesus suffering on the cross. "The life of all flesh is its blood," says the law, and we may rest assured that Christ's blood is the very life of faith, of joy, and of every holy grace!

Oh, how sweet to view the flowing
Of my Savior's precious blood;
With divine assurance knowing
He has made my peace with God!

e.verse: ...(These names are from ancient records.)
paras: Yet they are not so ancient as those precious truths that are the delight of our souls! Let us for a moment recount them, counting them over as misers count their gold. The sovereign choice of the Father, by which He elected us to eternal life before the earth began, is a matter of vast antiquity, since no human mind can conceive a beginning for it. We were chosen in Christ before the foundation of the world. Everlasting love accompanied that choice; for it was no cold act of divine will by which we were set apart, but the deepest affections of the Father were engaged. He loved us from the very beginning. Here is a theme for daily contemplation! The eternal purpose to redeem us from our foreseen ruin, to cleanse and sanctify us, and at last to glorify us, is of infinite antiquity, running side with immutable love and absolute sovereignty. The covenant of grace is ever described as everlasting; and Jesus, the divine Surety, had His goings forth from of old: He pledged Himself in sacred suretyship long before the first stars began to shine, and in Him the elect were ordained to eternal life. Thus, in the divine decree, a blessed covenant union was established between the Son of God and His chosen people, which will remain the eternal rock of their safety when time shall be no more. Is it not well to be familiar with these ancient truths? Is it not tragic that they are so neglected and even rejected by the majority of professing Christians? If men knew more of their own depravity, would they not be far more ready to adore distinguishing grace? Let us both admire and adore tonight, as we sing:

m.verse: Therefore, brothers, we have an obligation...
paras: As God's creatures, we are all debtors to Him: to obey Him with all our body, soul, and strength. Having broken His commandments, as we all have, we are debtors to His justice, and we owe Him a vast debt that we are unable to pay. But of the Christian it can be said that he does not owe God's justice anything, for Christ has paid the debt His people owed; for this reason the believer owes all the more to love. I am a debtor to God's grace and forgiving mercy; but I am no debtor to His justice, for He will never charge me with a debt already paid. Christ said, "It is finished!" and by that He meant that whatever His people owed was wiped away forever from the book of remembrance. Christ, to the uttermost, has satisfied divine justice: the account is settled; the certificate of debt is nailed to the cross; the receipt is given, and we are debtors to God's justice no longer. Yet because we are not debtors to our Lord in that legal sense, we become ten times greater debtors to God than we would have been otherwise. Christian, pause and ponder for a moment! What a debtor you are to divine sovereignty! How much you owe to His unselfish love, for He gave His own Son that He might die for you! Consider how much you owe to His forgiving grace, that after ten thousand offenses He loves you just as infinitely as ever. Consider what you owe to His power: how He has raised you from your death in sin; how He has preserved your spiritual life; how He has kept you from falling; and how, though a thousand enemies have beset your path, you have been able to hold firmly on your way. Consider what you owe to His immutability: though you have changed a thousand times, He has not changed once. You are as deeply in debt as you could possibly be to every attribute of God. To God you owe yourself and all that you have: present yourself as a living sacrifice, for it is only your reasonable service.

e.verse: Tell me... where do You pasture Your sheep? Where do You rest them at midday...
paras: These words express the desire of the believer for Christ, and his longing for present communion with Him. Where do You pasture Your flock? In Your house? I will go, if I may find You there. In private prayer? Then I will pray without ceasing. In the Word? Then I will read it diligently. In Your ordinances? Then I will walk in them with all my heart. Tell me where You pasture Your sheep, for wherever You stand as the Shepherd, there will I lie down as a sheep; for none but You can supply my need. I cannot be satisfied to remain apart from You. My soul hungers and thirsts for the refreshment of Your presence. "Where do You rest them at midday?" for whether at dawn or at noon, my only rest must be where You are and where Your beloved flock rests. My soul's rest must be a grace-given rest, and can only be found in You. Where is the shadow of that rock? Why should I not rest beneath it? "Why should I be like a veiled wanderer beside the flocks of Your companions?" You have companions—why should I not be one? Satan tells me I am unworthy; but I have always been unworthy, and yet You have loved me long; therefore my unworthiness cannot be a barrier to my having fellowship with You now. It is true that I am weak in faith and prone to fall, but my very weakness is the reason why I should always be where You pasture Your flock, that I may be strengthened and preserved in safety beside the still waters. Why should I turn aside? There is no reason why I should, but there are a thousand reasons why I should not, for Jesus beckons me to come. If He withdrew Himself for a little season, it was only to make me prize His presence more. Now that I am grieved and distressed at being away from Him, He will lead me once again to that sheltered nook where the lambs of His fold are shielded from the scorching sun.

m.verse: ...as the LORD loves the Israelites...
paras: Believer, look back through all your experience, and remember the way by which the LORD your God has led you in the wilderness, and how He has fed and clothed you every day—how He has borne with your stubborn ways, how He has put up with all your grumblings and all your longings after the meat pots of Egypt, how He has split open the rock to supply you, and fed you with manna that came down from heaven. Think of how His grace has been sufficient for you in all your troubles, how His blood has secured pardon for you in all your sins, and how His rod and His staff have comforted you. When you have thus looked back upon the love of the Lord, then let faith survey His love in the future; for remember that Christ's covenant and blood contain far more than blessings in the past. He who has loved you and pardoned you will never cease to love and pardon. He is the Alpha, and He will be the Omega also: He is first, and He will be last. Therefore, consider: when you pass through the valley of the shadow of death, you need fear no evil, for He is with you. When you stand in the cold waters of Jordan, you need not fear, for death cannot separate you from His love; and when you enter into the mysteries of eternity, you need not tremble, "For I am convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor principalities, neither things present nor things to come, nor powers, neither height nor depth, nor any other created thing, will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord." Now, soul, is not your love refreshed? Does not this make you love Jesus? Does not a flight through the boundless realms of the atmosphere of divine love set your heart ablaze and compel you to delight yourself in the LORD your God? Surely, as we meditate on the love of the Lord, our hearts burn within us, and we long to love Him more.

e.verse: ...These will be your refuge from the avenger of blood.
paras: It is said that in the land of Canaan, the cities of refuge were so arranged that anyone might reach one of them within half a day at the most. Even so the word of our salvation is near us: Jesus is an ever-present Savior, and the way to Him is short; it requires only a simple renunciation of our own merit, and a laying hold of Jesus to be our all in all. With regard to the roads leading to the city of refuge, we are told that they were carefully maintained: every river was bridged, and every obstruction was removed, so that the fugitive who fled might find an easy passage to the city. Once a year the elders traveled along the roads to inspect their condition, so that nothing might hinder the flight of anyone, or cause him through delay to be overtaken and slain. How graciously the promises of the gospel remove every stumbling block from the way! Wherever there were crossroads or turnings, signposts were erected with the clear inscription upon them: "To the city of refuge!" This is a vivid picture of the road to Christ Jesus. It is no roundabout road of the law; it is no complicated obeying of this, that, and the other command; it is a straight and open road: "Believe, and live." It is a road so difficult that no self-righteous man can ever tread it, yet so easy that every sinner who truly knows himself to be a sinner may find his way by it to heaven. No sooner did the manslayer reach the outer boundaries of the city than he was safe; it was not necessary for him to pass deep within the walls, for the surrounding pasturelands themselves were sufficient protection. Learn from this that if you do but touch the hem of Christ's garment, you will be made whole; if you only lay hold upon Him with "faith like a mustard seed," you are safe.

A little genuine grace ensures
The death of all our sins.
Only waste no time; do not linger along the way, for the avenger of blood is swift of foot, and it may be that he is at your very heels at this quiet evening hour.

m.verse: ...the Father has sent His Son to be the Savior of the world.
paras: It is a sweet thought that Jesus Christ did not come forth without His Father's permission, authority, consent, and assistance. He was sent by the Father, that He might be the Savior of mankind. We are too prone to forget that, while there are distinctions among the persons of the Trinity, there are no distinctions of honor. We too frequently ascribe the glory of our salvation, or at least the depths of its benevolence, more to Jesus Christ than to the Father. This is a very great mistake. What if Jesus came? Did not His Father send Him? If He spoke wondrously, did not His Father pour grace into His lips, that He might be an able minister of the new covenant? He who knows the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit as he ought to know Them, never sets one above another in his love; he sees Them at Bethlehem, at Gethsemane, and on Calvary, all equally engaged in the work of salvation. O Christian, have you placed your confidence in the Man Christ Jesus? Have you placed your reliance solely on Him? And are you united with Him? Then believe that you are united to the God of heaven. Since to the Man Christ Jesus you are a brother and hold the closest fellowship, you are linked through this with God the Eternal, and "the Ancient of Days" is your Father and your Friend. Have you ever considered the depth of love in the heart of the LORD, when God the Father equipped His Son for the great enterprise of mercy? If not, let this be your meditation today: The Father sent Him! Contemplate this theme. Think how Jesus works what the Father wills. In the wounds of the dying Savior see the love of the great I AM. Let every thought of Jesus be also connected with the eternal, ever-blessed God, for "it pleased the LORD to crush Him; He has put Him to grief."

e.verse: At that time Jesus declared...
paras: This is a remarkable way to begin a verse—"At that time Jesus answered," or declared in response. If you look at the context, you will not see that anyone had asked Him a question, or that He was in conversation with any human being. Yet it is written: "Jesus answered and said, I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth." When someone answers, he answers a person who has been speaking to him. Who, then, had spoken to Christ? His Father. Yet there is no outward record of it, and this should teach us that Jesus enjoyed unbroken communion with His Father, and that God spoke into His heart so frequently, so continually, that it was not an unusual circumstance to be recorded. It was the daily habit and life of Jesus to talk with God. As Jesus was in this world, so are we; let us therefore learn the lesson that this simple statement concerning Him teaches us. May we likewise have silent fellowship with the Father, so that we may often answer Him; and though the world knows not to whom we speak, may we be responding to that secret voice unheard by any other ear, which our own ear, opened by the Spirit of God, recognizes with joy. God has spoken to us; let us speak to God—either to set our seal that God is true and faithful to His promise, or to confess the sin of which the Spirit of God has convicted us, or to acknowledge the mercy that God's providence has bestowed, or to give hearty assent to the great truths that God the Holy Spirit has opened to our understanding. What a privilege is intimate communion with the Father of our spirits! It is a secret hidden from the world, a joy with which even the dearest friend does not interfere. If we would hear the whispers of God's love, our ear must be cleansed and tuned to listen to His voice. This very evening may our hearts be in such a state that when God speaks to us, we, like Jesus, may be prepared at once to answer Him.

m.verse: Pray in the Spirit at all times...
paras: What multitudes of prayers we have offered from the first moment we ever learned to pray! Our first prayer was a cry for ourselves: we asked that God would have mercy upon us and blot out our sin. He heard us. Yet when He had blotted out our sins like a thick cloud, we found we had still more prayers to offer for ourselves. We have had to pray for sanctifying grace, for constraining and restraining grace; we have been led to plead for a fresh assurance of faith, for the comforting application of the promise, for deliverance in the hour of temptation, for help in the time of duty, and for relief in the day of trial. We have been compelled to go to God for our souls as constant beggars, asking for everything. Bear witness, children of God, that you have never been able to obtain anything for your souls elsewhere. All the bread your soul has eaten has come down from heaven, and all the water it has drunk has flowed from the living Rock—Christ Jesus the Lord. Your soul has never grown rich in itself; it has always been dependent upon the daily bounty of God; and therefore your prayers have ascended to heaven for a range of spiritual mercies well-nigh infinite. Your needs were innumerable, and therefore the divine supplies have been infinitely great; your prayers have been as varied as the mercies have been countless. Have you not good reason, then, to say, "I love the LORD, for He heard my voice and my plea for mercy"? For as your prayers have been many, so also have been God's answers to them. He has heard you in the day of trouble, has strengthened you, and helped you, even when you dishonored Him by trembling and doubting at the mercy seat. Remember this, and let it fill your heart with gratitude to God, who has so graciously heard your poor, feeble prayers: "Bless the LORD, O my soul, and forget not all His benefits!"

e.verse: ...pray for each other...
paras: As an encouragement cheerfully to offer intercessory prayer, remember that such prayer is the sweetest God ever hears, for the intercession of Christ is of this very character. In all the incense that our Great High Priest now places into the golden censer, there is not a single grain for Himself. His intercession is the most acceptable of all supplications—and the more our prayer resembles Christ's, the sweeter it will be. Thus, while petitions for ourselves are graciously accepted, our pleadings for others—containing more of the fruit of the Spirit, more love, more faith, and more brotherly kindness—will be, through the precious merits of Jesus, the sweetest offering we can present to God, the very choice portion of our sacrifice. Remember also that intercessory prayer is powerfully effective. What wonders it has accomplished! The Word of God teems with its marvelous deeds. Believer, you hold a mighty instrument in your hands: use it well, use it constantly, use it with faith, and you will surely be a benefactor to your brothers. When you have the King's ear, speak to Him on behalf of the suffering members of His body. When you are privileged to draw very near to His throne, and the King says to you, "Ask, and I will give you whatever you desire," let your petitions be not for yourself alone, but for the many who stand in need of His aid. If you have grace at all and are not an intercessor, that grace must be as small as a mustard seed. You have just enough grace to float your soul clear of the quicksand, but you have no deep flood of grace; otherwise, you would carry in your joyous vessel a weighty cargo of the needs of others, and you would bring back from your Lord rich blessings for them, which, but for you, they might never have obtained:

Oh, let my hands forget their skill,
My tongue be silent, cold, and still,
This bounding heart forget to beat,
If I forget the mercy seat!

m.verse: Arise and depart...
paras: The hour is approaching when the message will come to us, as it comes to all: "Arise, and go forth from the home in which you have lived, from the city in which you have carried on your business, from your family, from your friends. Arise, and take your final journey." And what do we know of the journey? And what do we know of the country to which we are bound? A little we have read of it, and something has been revealed to us by the Spirit; but how little do we know of the realms of the future! We know that there is a dark and stormy river called Death; yet God bids us cross it, promising to be with us. And after death, what comes? What world of wonders will open upon our astonished sight? What scene of glory will be unfolded to our view? No traveler has ever returned to tell. Yet we know enough of the heavenly land to make us welcome our summons there with joy and gladness. The journey of death may be dark, but we may go forth on it fearlessly, knowing that God is with us as we walk through the gloomy valley, and therefore we need fear no evil. We will be departing from all we have known and loved here, but we will be going to our Father's house—to our Father's home where Jesus is—to that royal city that has foundations, whose architect and builder is God. This will be our final relocation, to dwell forever with Him whom we love, in the midst of His people, in the presence of God. Christian, meditate much on heaven: it will help you to press on, and to forget the toil of the way. This valley of tears is only the pathway to the better country; this world of woe is but the steppingstone to a world of bliss.

Prepare us, Lord, by grace divine,
For Your bright courts on high;
Then bid our spirits rise, and join
The chorus of the sky.

e.verse: ...heard a loud voice from heaven saying, “Come up here”...
paras: Without considering these words in their prophetical connection, let us regard them as the invitation of our great Forerunner to His sanctified people. In due time there will be heard a loud voice from heaven to every believer, saying, "Come up here." This should be to the saints the subject of joyful anticipation. Instead of dreading the time when we shall leave this world to go home to the Father, we should be longing for the hour of our emancipation. Our song should be—

My heart is with Him on His throne,
And ill can brook delay;
Each moment listening for the voice,
"Rise up and come away."

We are not called down to the grave, but up to the skies. Our heaven-born spirits should long for their native air. Yet the celestial summons should be the object of our patient waiting. Our God knows best when to bid us, "Come up here." We must not wish to anticipate the appointed time of our departure. I know that fervent love will make us cry,

O Lord of hosts, the waves divide,
And land us all in heaven;

but patience must have its perfect work. God ordains with perfect wisdom the most fitting time for the redeemed to remain below. Surely, if there could be regrets in heaven, the saints might mourn that they did not live longer here to do more good. Oh, for more sheaves for my Lord's barn! More jewels for His crown! But how can this be, unless there is more work to do? True, there is the other side of it: living so briefly, our sins are the fewer; but oh, when we are wholeheartedly serving God, and He grants us to scatter precious seed and reap a hundredfold, we would even say it is well for us to remain where we are. Whether our Master shall say "Go" or "Stay," let us be equally well pleased, so long as He favors us with His presence.

m.verse: ...you are to give Him the name Jesus...
paras: When a person is dear, everything connected with him becomes dear for his sake. Thus, so precious is the person of the Lord Jesus in the estimation of all true believers, that they consider everything about Him to be inestimable beyond all price. "All Your robes are fragrant with myrrh and aloes and cassia," said David, as though the very garments of the Savior were so sweetened by His person that he could not help but love them. Certain it is that there is not a spot where that hallowed foot has trodden, there is not a word that those blessed lips have uttered, nor a thought that His loving Word has revealed, which is not precious to us beyond all price. And this is equally true of the names of Christ: they are all sweet in the believer's ear. Whether He is called the Husband of the church, her Bridegroom, her Friend; whether He is styled the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world—the King, the Prophet, or the Priest—every title of our Master: Shiloh, Immanuel, Wonderful, the Mighty Counselor—every name is like the honeycomb dripping with honey, and luscious are the drops that flow from it. Yet if there is one name sweeter than any other in the believer's ear, it is the name of Jesus. Jesus! It is the name that moves the harps of heaven to melody! Jesus! The life of all our joys! If there is one name more charming, more precious than another, it is this name. It is woven into the very fabric of our hymnody. Many of our hymns begin with it, and scarcely any that are worth anything end without it. It is the sum total of all delights! It is the music with which the bells of heaven ring: a song in a single word; an ocean in comprehension, though a drop in brevity; a matchless oratorio in two syllables; a gathering up of the hallelujahs of eternity in five letters!

Jesus, I love Your charming name,
'Tis music to my ear.

e.verse: ...He will save His people from their sins.
paras: Many people, if they are asked what they understand by salvation, will reply, "Being saved from hell and taken to heaven." This is one result of salvation, but it is not a tenth of what is contained in that great blessing. It is true that our Lord Jesus Christ does redeem all His people from the wrath to come; He saves them from the fearful condemnation that their sins had brought upon them; but His triumph is far more complete than this. He saves His people "from their sins." Oh, sweet deliverance from our worst foes! Where Christ works a saving work, He casts Satan from his throne and will not let him be master any longer. No one is a true Christian if sin reigns in his mortal body. Sin will be in us—it will never be utterly expelled until the spirit enters glory—but it will never have dominion. There will be a striving for dominion—a conflict against the new law and the new spirit that God has implanted—but sin will never gain the upper hand so as to be absolute monarch of our nature. Christ will be Master of the heart, and sin must be put to death. The Lion of the tribe of Judah will prevail, and the dragon will be cast out. Professing Christian! Is sin subdued in you? If your life is unholy, your heart is unchanged; and if your heart is unchanged, you are an unsaved person. If the Savior has not sanctified you, renewed you, given you a hatred of sin and a love of holiness, He has done nothing in you of a saving character. The grace that does not make a man better than others is a worthless counterfeit. Christ saves His people, not in their sins, but from them. "Without holiness no one will see the Lord." "Let everyone who names the name of Christ depart from iniquity." If not saved from sin, how shall we hope to be counted among His people? Lord, save me now from all evil, and enable me to honor my Savior!

m.verse: So David inquired of the LORD...
paras: When David made this inquiry, he had just fought the Philistines and gained a notable victory. The Philistines came up in great hosts, but by the help of God, David easily put them to flight. Notice, however, that when they came a second time, David did not go up to fight them without inquiring of the Lord. Once he had been victorious, and he might have said, as many have in similar circumstances: "I shall be victorious again; I may be quite sure that if I have conquered once, I shall triumph yet again. Why should I wait to seek at the Lord's hands?" Not so with David! He had gained one battle by the strength of the Lord; he would not venture upon another until he had secured the same. He inquired, "Shall I go up against them?" and he waited until God's sign was given. Learn from David to take no step without God. Christian, if you would know the path of duty, take God for your compass; if you would steer your ship through the dark billows, put the helm into the hand of the Almighty. Many a rock might be escaped if we would let our Father take the helm; many a shoal or quicksand we might well avoid if we would submit to His sovereign will to choose and to command. As the Puritan said, "As sure as ever a Christian carves for himself, he'll cut his own fingers"—this is a great truth. Said another old divine, "He that goes before the cloud of God's providence goes on a fool's errand"—and so he does! We must watch where God's providence leads us; and if providence delays, wait until providence comes. He who goes before providence will be very glad to run back again. "I will instruct you and teach you in the way you should go," is God's promise to His people. Let us, then, take all our perplexities to Him, and say, "Lord, what do You want me to do?" Leave not your room this morning without inquiring of the Lord.

e.verse: ...lead us not into temptation...
paras: What we are taught to seek or shun in prayer, we should equally pursue or avoid in daily action. Most earnestly, therefore, should we avoid temptation, seeking to walk so guardedly in the path of obedience that we may never tempt the devil to tempt us. We are not to plunge into the thicket in search of the lion: dearly might we pay for such presumption! This lion may cross our path or leap upon us from the brush, but we have no business hunting him. He who encounters him, even though he wins the day, will find it a grueling struggle. Let the Christian pray that he may be spared the encounter. Our Savior, who had full experience of what temptation meant, thus earnestly admonished His disciples: "Pray that you may not enter into temptation."

Yet do what we will, we will be tempted; hence the petition, "Deliver us from evil," or from the evil one. God had one Son without sin, but He has no son without temptation. The natural man is born to trouble as the sparks fly upward, and the Christian is born to temptation just as certainly. We must constantly remain on guard against Satan, because, like a prowling thief, he gives no warning of his approach. Believers who have gained experience in the ways of Satan know that there are certain seasons when he will most probably attack, just as at certain times of the year bleak winds may be expected; thus the Christian is put on double guard by the prospect of danger, and that danger is averted by preparing to meet it. Prevention is far better than cure: it is better to be so well armed that the devil will not dare to attack you, than to endure the perils of the battle, even though you emerge victorious. Pray this evening, first, that you may not be tempted; and next, that if temptation is permitted, you may be delivered from the evil one.

m.verse: ...I know how to abound...
paras: There are many who know how to live humbly who have not yet learned how to abound. When they are set upon the pinnacle of success, their heads grow dizzy and they are ready to fall. The Christian far more frequently disgraces his profession in prosperity than in adversity. It is a perilous thing to be prosperous: the crucible of affliction is often a far less severe trial to the believer than the refining pot of prosperity. Oh, what leanness of soul and neglect of spiritual realities have been brought on through the very mercies and bounties of God! Yet this is by no means inevitable, for the apostle tells us that he knew how to abound. When he possessed much, he knew how to use it: abundant grace enabled him to bear abundant prosperity. When his vessel carried a full sail, it was ballasted with deep humility, and so he navigated safely. It requires more than human skill to carry the brimming cup of earthly joy with a steady hand; yet Paul had mastered that divine art, for he declares: "In any and every situation I have learned the secret of being filled and being hungry." It is a divine lesson to know how to be filled; for the Israelites were filled once, but while the meat was still between their teeth, the wrath of God struck them. Many have clamored for earthly mercies merely that they might indulge their own desires. Abundance of food has often bred pride and indulgence of spirit. When we enjoy much of God's providential goodness, it too often happens that we have but little of God's grace, and meager gratitude for the blessings we have received. We are filled and we forget God: satisfied with earth, we are content to live without heaven. Rest assured, it is far harder to know how to be full than it is to know how to be hungry—so strong is the natural tendency toward pride and neglect of God. See to it, then, that you ask in your prayers that God would teach you how to be filled.

Let not the gifts Your love bestows
Estrange our hearts from You.

e.verse: I have blotted out your transgressions like a cloud, and your sins like a mist. Return to Me, for I have redeemed you.
paras: Attentively observe THE INSTRUCTIVE COMPARISON: our sins are like a cloud. As clouds are of many shapes and shades, so are our transgressions. As clouds obscure the light of the sun and darken the landscape beneath, so do our sins hide from us the light of God's face and cause us to sit in the shadow of death. They are earth-born things that rise from the miry depths of our nature; and when collected until their measure is full, they threaten us with storm and tempest. Alas, that unlike natural clouds, our sins bring us no refreshing showers, but rather threaten to deluge us with a fiery flood of destruction! O black clouds of sin, how can it be fair weather with our souls while you remain?

Let our joyful eye dwell upon THE REMARKABLE ACT of divine mercy—"blotting out." God Himself appears upon the scene, and in sovereign goodness, instead of displaying His anger, He reveals His grace. He at once and forever effectively removes our guilt and ruin, not by blowing away the cloud, but by blotting it out of existence once for all. Against the justified man no sin remains: the great transaction of the cross has eternally removed his transgressions from him. On Calvary's summit the great deed, by which the sin of all the chosen was forever put away, was completely and gloriously accomplished.

Practically let us obey THE GRACIOUS COMMAND: "Return to Me." Why should pardoned sinners live at a distance from their God? If we have been forgiven all our sins, let no legalistic fear withhold us from the boldest access to our Lord. Let backslidings be bemoaned, but let us not persevere in them. To the greatest possible nearness of communion with the Lord, let us, in the power of the Holy Spirit, strive mightily to return. O Lord, this night restore us!

m.verse: ...they took note that these men had been with Jesus.
paras: A Christian should be a striking likeness of Jesus Christ. You have read biographies of Christ, beautifully and eloquently written, but the best life of Christ is His living biography, written out in the words and actions of His people. If we were what we profess to be and what we ought to be, we would be living portraits of Christ—yes, such striking likenesses of Him that the world would not have to examine us for hours together and say, "Well, there seems to be somewhat of a resemblance"; but they would, upon the first glance, exclaim: "He has been with Jesus! He has been taught by Him; he is like Him; he has caught the very spirit of the holy Man of Nazareth, and he works it out in his daily life and everyday actions!" A Christian should be like Christ in his boldness. Never blush to own your faith; your profession will never disgrace you—take care that you never disgrace it. Be like Jesus, very valiant for your God. Imitate Him in your loving spirit: think kindly, speak kindly, and act kindly, that men may say of you, "He has been with Jesus." Imitate Jesus in His holiness. Was He zealous for His Father? So be you: continually go about doing good. Let no time be wasted—it is far too precious. Was He self-denying, never seeking His own interest? Be the same. Was He devout? Be fervent in your prayers. Did He show deference to His Father's will? So submit yourselves to Him. Was He patient? Learn so to endure. And best of all, as the highest portraiture of Jesus, strive to forgive your enemies as He did; and let those sublime words of your Master, "Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do," continually echo in your ears. Forgive as you hope to be forgiven. Heap burning coals on the head of your foe by your kindness to him. Returning good for evil, remember, is godlike. Be godlike, then; and in all ways and by all means, so live that everyone may say of you, "He has been with Jesus."

e.verse: ...You have abandoned your first love.
paras: Ever to be remembered is that best and brightest of hours, when we first saw the Lord, lost our heavy burden, received the scroll of promise, rejoiced in full salvation, and went on our way in peace. It was springtime in the soul: the winter was past; the mutterings of Sinai's thunders were hushed; the flashes of its lightning were seen no more; God was beheld as reconciled; the law threatened no vengeance, and divine justice demanded no punishment. Then the flowers appeared in our heart; hope, love, peace, and patience sprang from the soil; the hyacinth of repentance, the snowdrop of pure holiness, the crocus of golden faith, and the daffodil of early love all adorned the garden of the soul.
