His vast benevolence must, from the very nature of things, have afforded Him the deepest possible delight, for benevolence is joy. There were a few remarkable seasons when this joy manifested itself openly: "At that time Jesus rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said, 'I praise You, Father, Lord of heaven and earth.'" Christ had His songs, though it was night with Him; though His face was marred, and His countenance had lost the luster of earthly happiness, yet sometimes it was lit up with a matchless splendor of unparalleled satisfaction, as He thought upon the recompense of the reward, and in the midst of the congregation sang His grateful praise to God.

In this, the Lord Jesus is a blessed picture of His church on earth. At this hour the church expects to walk in sympathy with her Lord along a thorny road; through much tribulation she is forcing her way to the crown. To bear the cross is her office, and to be scorned and counted an alien by her mother's children is her lot; and yet the church has a deep well of joy, of which none can drink but her own children. There are stores of wine, and oil, and grain, hidden in the midst of our Jerusalem, upon which the saints of God are evermore sustained and nurtured; and sometimes, as in our Savior's case, we have our seasons of intense delight, for "There is a river whose streams make glad the city of our God." Exiles though we are, we rejoice in our King; yes, in Him we exceedingly rejoice, while in His glorious name we set up our banners.

m.verse: ... Are you betraying the Son of Man with a kiss?
paras: “The kisses of an enemy are deceitful.” Let me be on my guard when the world puts on a loving face, for it will, if possible, betray me as it did my Master, with a kiss. Whenever a man is about to stab religion, he usually professes very great reverence for it. Let me beware of the sleek-faced hypocrisy which is armor-bearer to heresy and infidelity. Knowing the deceitfulness of unrighteousness, let me be wise as a serpent to detect and avoid the designs of the enemy. The young man, lacking understanding, was led astray by the seductive kiss of the strange woman: may my soul be so graciously instructed throughout all this day, that "the flattering speech" of the world may have no effect upon me. Holy Spirit, let me not, a poor frail son of man, be betrayed with a kiss!

But what if I should be guilty of the same accursed sin as Judas, that son of perdition? I have been baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus; I am a member of His visible Church; I sit at the communion table: all these are so many kisses of my lips. Am I sincere in them? If not, I am a base traitor. Do I live in the world as carelessly as others do, and yet make a profession of being a follower of Jesus? Then I must expose religion to ridicule, and lead men to speak evil of the holy name by which I am called. Surely if I act thus inconsistently I am a Judas, and it would be far better for me never to have been born. Dare I hope that I am clear in this matter? Then, O Lord, keep me so. O Lord, make me sincere and true. Preserve me from every false way. Never let me betray my Savior. I do love You, Jesus, and though I often grieve You, yet I desire to abide faithful even to death. O God, forbid that I should be a high-soaring professor of faith, and then fall at last into the lake of fire, because I betrayed my Master with a kiss.

e.verse: ... the Son of Man.
paras: How constantly our Master used the title, the "Son of Man!" If He had chosen, He might always have spoken of Himself as the Son of God, the Everlasting Father, the Wonderful, the Counselor, the Prince of Peace; but behold the lowliness of Jesus! He prefers to call Himself the Son of Man. Let us learn a lesson of humility from our Savior; let us never court great titles nor proud degrees. There is here, however, a far sweeter thought. Jesus loved manhood so much that He delighted to honor it; and since it is a high honor, and indeed the greatest dignity of manhood, that Jesus is the Son of Man, He is accustomed to display this name, that He may as it were hang royal stars upon the breast of manhood, and show forth the love of God to Abraham's seed. Son of Man—whenever He spoke that word, He shed a halo round the head of Adam's children. Yet there is perhaps a more precious thought still. Jesus Christ called Himself the Son of Man to express His oneness and sympathy with His people. He thus reminds us that He is the One whom we may approach without fear. As a man, we may take to Him all our griefs and troubles, for He knows them by experience; in that He Himself has suffered as the "Son of Man," He is able to help and comfort us. All hail, You blessed Jesus! Inasmuch as You are evermore using the sweet name which acknowledges that You are a brother and a near kinsman, it is to us a dear token of Your grace, Your humility, Your love.

Oh see how Jesus trusts Himself
To our frail childish love,
As though by His free ways with us
Our earnestness to prove!
His sacred name a common word
On earth He loves to hear;
There is no majesty in Him
Which love may not come near.

m.verse: ... If you are looking for Me, let these men go.
paras: Mark, my soul, the care which Jesus manifested even in His hour of trial, toward the sheep of His hand! The ruling passion is strong in death. He resigns Himself to the enemy, but He interposes a word of power to set His disciples free. As to Himself, like a sheep before her shearers He was silent and opened not His mouth, but for His disciples' sake He speaks with Almighty energy. Here is love—constant, self-forgetting, faithful love. But is there not far more here than is to be found upon the surface? Have we not the very soul and spirit of the atonement in these words? The Good Shepherd lays down His life for the sheep, and pleads that they must therefore go free. The Surety is bound, and justice demands that those for whom He stands a substitute should go their way. In the midst of Egypt's bondage, that voice rings as a word of power, "Let these go their way." Out of the slavery of sin and Satan the redeemed must come. In every cell of the dungeons of Despair, the sound is echoed, "Let these go their way," and forth come Despondency and Much-afraid. Satan hears the well-known voice, and lifts his foot from the neck of the fallen; and Death hears it, and the grave opens her gates to let the dead arise. Their way is one of progress, holiness, triumph, glory, and none shall dare to stay them in it. No lion shall be on their way, neither shall any ravenous beast go up on it. "The hind of the morning" has drawn the cruel hunters upon Himself, and now the most timid roes and hinds of the field may graze at perfect peace among the lilies of His love. The thundercloud has burst over the cross of Calvary, and the pilgrims of Zion shall never be smitten by the bolts of vengeance. Come, my heart, rejoice in the freedom which your Redeemer has secured for you, and bless His name all the day, and every day.

e.verse: ... when He comes in His Father’s glory with the holy angels.
paras: If we have been partakers with Jesus in His shame, we shall be sharers with Him in the luster which shall surround Him when He appears again in glory. Are you, beloved one, with Christ Jesus? Does a vital union knit you to Him? Then you are today with Him in His shame; you have taken up His cross, and gone with Him outside the camp bearing His reproach; you shall doubtless be with Him when the cross is exchanged for the crown. But judge yourself this evening; for if you are not with Him in the regeneration, neither shall you be with Him when He shall come in His glory. If you start back from the dark side of communion, you shall not understand its bright, its happy hour, when the King shall come, and all His holy angels with Him. What! Are angels with Him? And yet He did not take on the nature of angels—He took up the seed of Abraham. Are the holy angels with Him? Come, my soul, if you are indeed His own beloved, you cannot be far from Him. If His friends and His neighbors are called together to see His glory, what do you think if you are married to Him? Shall you be distant? Though it be a day of judgment, yet you cannot be far from that heart which, having admitted angels into intimacy, has received you into union. Has He not said to you, O my soul, "I will betroth you to Me in righteousness, and in judgment, and in lovingkindness"? Have not His own lips declared it, "I am married to you, and My delight is in you"? If the angels, who are only friends and neighbors, shall be with Him, it is abundantly certain that His own beloved Hephzibah, in whom is all His delight, shall be near to Him, and sit at His right hand. Here is a morning star of hope for you, of such exceeding brilliance, that it may well light up the darkest and most desolate experience.

m.verse: ... Then all the disciples deserted Him and fled.
paras: He never deserted them, but they, in cowardly fear for their lives, fled from Him in the very beginning of His sufferings. This is but one instructive instance of the frailty of all believers if left to themselves; they are but sheep at the best, and they flee when the wolf comes. They had all been warned of the danger, and had promised to die rather than leave their Master; and yet they were seized with sudden panic, and took to their heels. It may be that I, at the opening of this day, have braced up my mind to bear a trial for the Lord's sake, and I imagine myself to be certain to exhibit perfect fidelity; but let me be very watchful of myself, lest having the same evil heart of unbelief, I should depart from my Lord as the apostles did. It is one thing to promise, and quite another to perform. It would have been to their eternal honor to have stood at Jesus' side right manfully; they fled from honor; may I be kept from imitating them! Where else could they have been so safe as near their Master, who could presently call for twelve legions of angels? They fled from their true safety. O God, let me not play the fool also. Divine grace can make the coward brave. The smoking flax can flame forth like fire on the altar when the Lord wills it. These very apostles, who were timid as hares, grew to be bold as lions after the Spirit had descended upon them, and even so the Holy Spirit can make my faint-hearted spirit brave to confess my Lord and witness for His truth.

What anguish must have filled the Savior as He saw His friends prove so faithless! This was one bitter ingredient in His cup; but that cup is drained dry; let me not put another drop in it. If I forsake my Lord, I shall crucify Him afresh, and put Him to an open shame. Keep me, O blessed Spirit, from an end so shameful.

e.verse: ... even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their master’s table.
paras: This woman gained comfort in her misery by thinking GREAT THOUGHTS OF CHRIST. The Master had talked about the children's bread: "Now," she reasoned, "since You are the Master of the table of grace, I know that You are a generous host, and there is sure to be an abundance of bread upon Your table; there will be such an abundance for the children that there will be crumbs to drop on the floor for the dogs, and the children will fare none the worse because the dogs are fed." She thought Him One who kept so good a table that all that she needed would only be a crumb in comparison; yet remember, what she wanted was to have the demon cast out of her daughter. It was a very great thing to her, but she had such a high esteem of Christ, that she said, "It is nothing to Him; it is but a crumb for Christ to give." This is the royal road to comfort. Great thoughts of your sin alone will drive you to despair; but great thoughts of Christ will pilot you into the haven of peace.

"My sins are many, but oh! It is nothing to Jesus to take them all away. The weight of my guilt presses me down as a giant's foot would crush a worm, but it is no more than a grain of dust to Him, because He has already borne its curse in His own body on the tree. It will be but a small thing for Him to give me full remission, although it will be an infinite blessing for me to receive it." The woman opens her soul's mouth very wide, expecting great things of Jesus, and He fills it with His love. Dear reader, do the same. She confessed what Christ laid at her door, but she laid fast hold upon Him, and drew arguments even out of His hard words; she believed great things of Him, and she thus overcame Him. SHE WON THE VICTORY BY BELIEVING IN HIM. Her case is an instance of prevailing faith; and if we would conquer like her, we must imitate her tactics.

m.verse: ... to know this love that surpasses knowledge ...
paras: The love of Christ in its sweetness, its fullness, its greatness, its faithfulness, surpasses all human comprehension. Where shall language be found which shall describe His matchless, His unparalleled love toward the children of men? It is so vast and boundless that, as the swallow merely skims the surface of the water, and dives not into its depths, so all descriptive words but touch the surface, while depths immeasurable lie beneath. Well might the poet say,
O love, you fathomless abyss!

for this love of Christ is indeed measureless and fathomless; none can attain to it. Before we can have any right idea of the love of Jesus, we must understand His previous glory in its height of majesty, and His incarnation upon the earth in all its depths of shame. But who can tell us the majesty of Christ? When He was enthroned in the highest heavens He was very God of very God; by Him were the heavens made, and all their heavenly host. His own almighty arm upheld the spheres; the praises of cherubim and seraphim perpetually surrounded Him; the full chorus of the hallelujahs of the universe unceasingly flowed to the foot of His throne: He reigned supreme above all His creatures, God over all, blessed forever. Who can tell His height of glory then? And who, on the other hand, can tell how low He descended? To be a man was something; to be a man of sorrows was far more; to bleed, and die, and suffer—these were much for Him who was the Son of God; but to suffer such unparalleled agony—to endure a death of shame and desertion by His Father, this is a depth of condescending love which the most inspired mind must utterly fail to fathom. Here is love! And truly it is love that "surpasses knowledge." Oh, let this love fill our hearts with adoring gratitude, and lead us into practical manifestations of its power.

e.verse: ... I will accept you as a pleasing aroma.
paras: The merits of our great Redeemer are as a sweet aroma to the Most High. Whether we speak of the active or passive righteousness of Christ, there is an equal fragrance. There was a sweet aroma in His active life by which He honored the law of God, and made every precept to glitter like a precious jewel in the pure setting of His own person. Such, too, was His passive obedience, when He endured with unmurmuring submission hunger and thirst, cold and nakedness, and at length sweat great drops of blood in Gethsemane, gave His back to those who struck Him, and His cheeks to those who plucked out His beard, and was fastened to the cruel wood, that He might suffer the wrath of God in our behalf. These two things are sweet before the Most High; and for the sake of His doing and His dying, His substitutionary sufferings and His vicarious obedience, the Lord our God accepts us. What a preciousness must there be in Him to overcome our want of preciousness! What a pleasing aroma to put away our offensive stench! What a cleansing power in His blood to take away sin such as ours! And what glory in His righteousness to make such unacceptable creatures to be accepted in the Beloved! Mark, believer, how sure and unchanging must be our acceptance, since it is in Him! Take care that you never doubt your acceptance in Jesus. You cannot be accepted without Christ; but, when you have received His merit, you cannot be unaccepted. Notwithstanding all your doubts, and fears, and sins, Jehovah's gracious eye never looks upon you in anger; though He sees sin in you, in yourself, yet when He looks at you through Christ, He sees no sin. You are always accepted in Christ, are always blessed and dear to the Father's heart. Therefore lift up a song, and as you see the smoking incense of the merit of the Savior coming up, this evening, before the sapphire throne, let the incense of your praise go up also.

m.verse: Although He was a Son, He learned obedience from what He suffered.
paras: We are told that the Captain of our salvation was made perfect through suffering; therefore we who are sinful, and who are far from being perfect, must not wonder if we are called to pass through suffering too. Shall the Head be crowned with thorns, and shall the other members of the body be rocked upon the dainty lap of ease? Must Christ pass through seas of His own blood to win the crown, and are we to walk to heaven dryshod in silver slippers? No, our Master's experience teaches us that suffering is necessary, and the true-born child of God must not, and would not, escape it even if he could. But there is one very comforting thought in the fact of Christ's "being made perfect through suffering"—it is that He can have complete sympathy with us. "We do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses." In this sympathy of Christ we find a sustaining power. One of the early martyrs said, "I can bear it all, for Jesus suffered, and He suffers in me now; He sympathizes with me, and this makes me strong." Believer, lay hold of this thought in all times of agony. Let the thought of Jesus strengthen you as you follow in His steps. Find a sweet and abiding support in His sympathy; and remember that to suffer is an honorable thing—to suffer for Christ is glory. The apostles rejoiced that they were counted worthy to do this. Just so far as the Lord shall give us grace to suffer for Christ, to suffer with Christ, just so far does He honor us. The jewels of a Christian are his afflictions. The regalia of the kings whom God has anointed are their troubles, their sorrows, and their griefs. Let us not, therefore, shun being honored. Let us not turn aside from being exalted. Griefs exalt us, and troubles lift us up. "If we endure, we shall also reign with Him."

e.verse: ... I called Him, but He did not answer.
paras: Prayer sometimes lingers, like a petitioner at the gate, until the King comes forth to fill her lap with the blessings that she seeks. The Lord, when He has bestowed great faith, has often been known to test it by long delays. He has suffered His servants' voices to echo in their ears as from a brazen sky. They have knocked at the golden gate, but it has remained immovable, as though it were rusted upon its hinges. Like Jeremiah, they have cried, "You have covered Yourself with a cloud, so that no prayer can pass through." Thus have true saints continued long in patient waiting without reply, not because their prayers were not vehement, nor because they were unaccepted, but because it so pleased Him who is a Sovereign, and who gives according to His own good pleasure. If it pleases Him to bid our patience exercise itself, shall He not do as He wills with His own? Beggars must not be choosers either as to time, place, or form. But we must be careful not to take delays in prayer for denials: God's long-dated promises will be punctually honored; we must not suffer Satan to shake our confidence in the God of truth by pointing to our unanswered prayers. Unanswered petitions are not unheard. God keeps a file for our prayers—they are not blown away by the wind; they are treasured in the King's archives. There is a registry in the court of heaven where every prayer is recorded. Tried believer, your Lord has a tear-bottle in which the costly drops of your sacred grief are stored, and a book in which your holy groanings are numbered. Soon your suit shall prevail. Can you not be content to wait a little while? Will not your Lord's time be better than your time? Soon He will appear with comfort to your soul's joy, and make you put away the sackcloth and ashes of long waiting, and put on the scarlet and fine linen of full fruition.

m.verse: ... and He was numbered with the transgressors.
paras: Why did Jesus permit Himself to be enrolled among sinners? This wonderful condescension was justified by many powerful reasons. In such a character He could the better become their advocate. In some trials there is an identification of the counselor with the client, nor can they be looked upon in the eye of the law as apart from one another. Now, when the sinner is brought to the bar, Jesus appears there Himself. He stands to answer the accusation. He points to His side, His hands, His feet, and challenges Justice to bring anything against the sinners whom He represents; He pleads His blood, and pleads so triumphantly, being numbered with them and having a part with them, that the Judge proclaims, "Let them go their way; deliver them from going down into the pit, for He has found a ransom." Our Lord Jesus was numbered with the transgressors in order that they might feel their hearts drawn toward Him. Who can be afraid of One who is written in the same list with us? Surely we may come boldly to Him, and confess our guilt. He who is numbered with us cannot condemn us. Was He not put down in the transgressor's list that we might be written in the red roll of the saints? He was holy, and written among the holy; we were guilty, and numbered among the guilty; He transfers His name from yonder list to this black indictment, and our names are taken from the indictment and written in the roll of acceptance, for there is a complete transfer made between Jesus and His people. All our estate of misery and sin Jesus has taken; and all that Jesus has comes to us. His righteousness, His blood, and everything that He has He gives us as our dowry. Rejoice, believer, in your union to Him who was numbered among the transgressors; and prove that you are truly saved by being manifestly numbered with those who are new creatures in Him.

e.verse: Let us examine and test our ways, and turn back to the LORD.
paras: The spouse who fondly loves her absent husband longs for his return; a long protracted separation from her lord is a semi-death to her spirit: and so with souls who love the Savior much, they must see His face; they cannot bear that He should be away upon the mountains of Bether, and no more hold communion with them. A reproaching glance, an uplifted finger will be grievous to loving children, who fear to offend their tender father, and are only happy in his smile. Beloved, it was so once with you. A text of Scripture, a threatening, a touch of the rod of affliction, and you went to your Father's feet, crying, "Show me why You contend with me?" Is it so now? Are you content to follow Jesus afar off? Can you contemplate suspended communion with Christ without alarm? Can you bear to have your Beloved walking contrary to you, because you walk contrary to Him? Have your sins separated between you and your God, and is your heart at rest? Oh, let me affectionately warn you, for it is a grievous thing when we can live contentedly without the present enjoyment of the Savior's face. Let us strive to feel what an evil thing this is—little love to our own dying Savior, little joy in our precious Jesus, little fellowship with the Beloved! Hold a true spiritual fast in your souls, while you sorrow over your hardness of heart. Do not stop at sorrow! Remember where you first received salvation. Go at once to the cross. There, and there only, can you get your spirit quickened. No matter how hard, how insensible, how dead we may have become, let us go again in all the rags and poverty and defilement of our natural condition. Let us clasp that cross, let us look into those languid eyes, let us bathe in that fountain filled with blood—this will bring back to us our first love; this will restore the simplicity of our faith, and the tenderness of our heart.

m.verse: ... and by His stripes we are healed.
paras: Pilate delivered our Lord to the lictors to be scourged. The Roman scourge was indeed a most dreadful instrument of torture. It was made of the sinews of oxen, and sharp bones were interwoven here and there among the sinews; so that every time the terrible lash came down, these pieces of bone inflicted fearful lacerations, and tore off the quivering flesh from the bone. The Savior was, no doubt, bound to the column, and thus beaten. He had been beaten before; but this beating by the Roman lictors was probably the most severe of His flagellations. My soul, stand here in holy awe and weep over His poor, bruised, and stricken body.

Believer in Jesus, can you gaze upon Him without tears, as He stands before you the mirror of agonizing love? He is at once fair as the lily for innocence, and red as the rose with the crimson of His own blood. As we feel the sure and blessed healing which His stripes have wrought in us, does not our heart melt at once with love and grief? If ever we have loved our Lord Jesus, surely we must feel that affection glowing now within our bosoms.

See how the patient Jesus stands,
Insulted in His lowest case!
Sinners have bound the Almighty's hands,
And spit in their Creator's face.
With thorns His temples gored and gashed
Send streams of blood from every part;
His back with knotted scourges lashed,
But sharper scourges tear His heart.

We would gladly go to our chambers and weep; but since our business calls us away, we will first pray our Beloved to print the image of His bleeding self upon the tablets of our hearts all the day, and at nightfall we will return to commune with Him, and sorrow that our sin should have cost Him so dear.

e.verse: And Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth and spread it out for herself on a rock. From the beginning of the harvest until the rain from heaven poured down on the bodies, she did not allow the birds of the air to rest on them by day, nor the beasts of the field by night.
paras: If the love of a woman to her slain sons could make her prolong her mournful vigil for so long a period, shall we weary of considering the sufferings of our blessed Lord? She drove away the birds of prey, and shall not we chase from our meditations those worldly and sinful thoughts which defile both our minds and the sacred themes upon which we are occupied? Away, you birds of evil wing! Leave the sacrifice alone! She bore the scorching heat of summer, the night dews and the rains, unsheltered and alone. Sleep was chased from her weeping eyes: her heart was too full for slumber. Behold how she loved her children! Shall Rizpah thus endure, and shall we shrink at the first little inconvenience or trial? Are we such cowards that we cannot bear to suffer with our Lord? She chased away even the wild beasts, with courage unusual in her sex, and will not we be ready to encounter every foe for Jesus' sake? These her children were slain by other hands than hers, and yet she wept and watched: what ought we to do who have by our sins crucified our Lord? Our obligations are boundless, our love should be fervent, and our repentance thorough. To watch with Jesus should be our business, to protect His honor our occupation, to abide by His cross our solace. Those ghastly corpses might well have terrified Rizpah, especially by night, but in our Lord, at whose cross-foot we are sitting, there is nothing revolting, but everything attractive. Never was living beauty so enchanting as a dying Savior. Jesus, we will watch with You yet awhile, and do You graciously unveil Yourself to us; then we shall not sit beneath sackcloth, but in a royal pavilion.

m.verse: Let Him kiss me with the kisses of His mouth ...
paras: For several days we have been dwelling upon the Savior's passion, and for some little time to come we shall linger there. In beginning a new month, let us seek the same desires after our Lord as those which glowed in the heart of the elect spouse. See how she leaps at once to Him; there are no prefatory words; she does not even mention His name; she is in the heart of her theme at once, for she speaks of Him who was the only "Him" in all the world to her. How bold is her love! It was great condescension which permitted the weeping penitent to anoint His feet with spikenard—it was rich love which allowed the gentle Mary to sit at His feet and learn of Him—but here, love, strong and fervent love, aspires to higher tokens of regard, and closer signs of intimate fellowship. Esther trembled in the presence of Ahasuerus, but the spouse in the joyful liberty of perfect love knows no fear. If we have received the same free spirit, we also may ask the like. By kisses we suppose to be intended those varied manifestations of affection by which the believer is made to enjoy the love of Jesus. The kiss of reconciliation we enjoyed at our conversion, and it was sweet as honey dropping from the comb. The kiss of acceptance is still warm on our brow, as we know that He has accepted our persons and our works through rich grace. The kiss of daily, present communion, is that which we pant after to be repeated day after day, till it is changed into the kiss of reception, which removes the soul from earth, and the kiss of consummation which fills it with the joy of heaven. Faith is our walk, but fellowship sensibly felt is our rest. Faith is the road, but communion with Jesus is the well from which the pilgrim drinks. O Lover of our souls, be not distant to us; let the lips of Your blessing meet the lips of our asking; let the lips of Your fullness touch the lips of our need, and at once the kiss of holy communion will be granted.

e.verse: ... it is time to seek the LORD ...
paras: This month of April is said to derive its name from the Latin verb aperio, which signifies to open, because all the buds and blossoms are now opening, and we have arrived at the gates of the flowery year. Reader, if you are yet unsaved, may your heart, in accord with the universal awakening of nature, be opened to receive the Lord. Every blossoming flower warns you that it is time to seek the Lord; be not out of tune with nature, but let your heart bud and bloom with holy desires. Do you tell me that the warm blood of youth leaps in your veins? Then, I entreat you, give your vigor to the Lord. It was my unspeakable happiness to be called in early youth, and I could gladly praise the Lord every day for it. Salvation is priceless, let it come when it may, but oh! An early salvation has a double value in it. Young men and maidens, since you may perish before you reach your prime, "It is time to seek the Lord." You who feel the first signs of decay, quicken your pace: that hollow cough, that hectic flush, are warnings which you must not trifle with; with you it is indeed time to seek the Lord. Did I observe a little gray mingled with your once luxurious tresses? Years are stealing on apace, and death is drawing nearer by hasty marches; let each return of spring arouse you to set your house in order. Dear reader, if you are now advanced in life, let me entreat and implore you to delay no longer. There is a day of grace for you now—be thankful for that, but it is a limited season and grows shorter every time that clock ticks. Here in this silent chamber, on this first night of another month, I speak to you as best I can by paper and ink, and from my inmost soul, as God's servant, I lay before you this solemn warning, "It is time to seek the Lord." Slight not that word; it may be your last call from destruction, the final syllable from the lip of grace.

m.verse: But Jesus gave no answer, not even to a single charge ...
paras: He had never been slow of speech when He could bless the sons of men, but He would not say a single word for Himself. "No one ever spoke like this Man," and never man was silent like Him. Was this singular silence the index of His perfect self-sacrifice? Did it show that He would not utter a word to stay the slaughter of His sacred person, which He had dedicated as an offering for us? Had He so entirely surrendered Himself that He would not interfere in His own behalf, even in the minutest degree, but be bound and slain an unstruggling, uncomplaining victim? Was this silence a type of the defenselessness of sin? Nothing can be said in palliation or excuse of human guilt; and, therefore, He who bore its whole weight stood speechless before His judge. Is not patient silence the best reply to a gainsaying world? Calm endurance answers some questions infinitely more conclusively than the loftiest eloquence. The best apologists for Christianity in the early days were its martyrs. The anvil breaks a host of hammers by quietly bearing their blows. Did not the silent Lamb of God furnish us with a grand example of wisdom? Where every word was occasion for new blasphemy, it was the line of duty to afford no fuel for the flame of sin. The ambiguous and the false, the unworthy and mean, will before long overthrow and confute themselves, and therefore the true can afford to be quiet, and finds silence to be its wisdom. Evidently our Lord, by His silence, furnished a remarkable fulfillment of prophecy. A long defense of Himself would have been contrary to Isaiah's prediction: "He was led like a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is silent, so He did not open His mouth." By His quiet He conclusively proved Himself to be the true Lamb of God. As such we salute Him this morning. Be with us, Jesus, and in the silence of our heart, let us hear the voice of Your love.

e.verse: ... He will see His offspring, He will prolong His days, and the good pleasure of the LORD will prosper in His hand.
paras: Plead for the speedy fulfillment of this promise, all you who love the Lord. It is easy work to pray when we are grounded and bottomed, as to our desires, upon God's own promise. How can He that gave the word refuse to keep it? Immutable veracity cannot demean itself by a lie, and eternal faithfulness cannot degrade itself by neglect. God must bless His Son, His covenant binds Him to it. That which the Spirit prompts us to ask for Jesus, is that which God decrees to give Him. Whenever you are praying for the kingdom of Christ, let your eyes behold the dawning of the blessed day which draws near, when the Crucified shall receive His coronation in the place where men rejected Him. Courage, you that prayerfully work and toil for Christ with success of the very smallest kind, it shall not be so always; better times are before you. Your eyes cannot see the blissful future: borrow the telescope of faith; wipe the misty breath of your doubts from the glass; look through it and behold the coming glory. Reader, let us ask, do you make this your constant prayer? Remember that the same Christ who tells us to say, "Give us this day our daily bread," had first given us this petition, "Hallowed be Your name; Your kingdom come; Your will be done, on earth as it is in heaven." Let not your prayers be all concerning your own sins, your own wants, your own imperfections, your own trials, but let them climb the starry ladder, and get up to Christ Himself, and then, as you draw near to the blood-sprinkled mercy seat, offer this prayer continually, "Lord, extend the kingdom of Your beloved Son." Such a petition, fervently presented, will elevate the spirit of all your devotions. Mind that you prove the sincerity of your prayer by diligently striving to promote the Lord's glory.

m.verse: ... and the soldiers took Him away.
paras: He had been all night in agony; He had spent the early morning at the hall of Caiaphas; He had been hurried from Caiaphas to Pilate, from Pilate to Herod, and from Herod back again to Pilate; He had, therefore, very little strength left, and yet neither nourishment nor rest was granted Him. They were eager for His blood, and therefore led Him out to die, heavily laden with the cross. O sorrowful procession! The daughters of Jerusalem may well weep. My soul, you must weep as well.

What do we learn here as we see our blessed Lord led forth? Do we not perceive that truth which was foreshadowed by the scapegoat? Did not the high priest bring the scapegoat and place both his hands upon its head, confessing the sins of the people, so that those sins might be laid upon the goat and removed from the people? Then the goat was led away by a suitable man into the wilderness, carrying away the sins of the people, so that even if they were searched for, they could never be found. Now we see Jesus brought before the priests and rulers, who pronounce Him guilty; God Himself imputes our sins to Him: "the LORD has laid on Him the iniquity of us all"; "He was made sin for us"; and, as the substitute for our guilt, bearing our sin upon His shoulders as represented by the cross, we see the great Scapegoat led away by the appointed officers of justice. Beloved, can you feel assured that He carried your sin? As you look at the cross upon His shoulders, does it represent your sin? There is one way by which you can tell whether He carried your sin or not. Have you laid your hand upon His head, confessed your sin, and trusted in Him? Then your sin does not rest upon you; it has all been transferred by blessed imputation to Christ, and He bears it on His shoulder as a load heavier than the cross.
Do not let this picture fade until you have rejoiced in your own deliverance and worshipped the loving Redeemer upon Whom your iniquities were laid.

e.verse: We all like sheep have gone astray, each one has turned to his own way; and the LORD has laid upon Him the iniquity of us all.
paras: Here is a confession of sin common to all the elect people of God. They have all fallen, and therefore, in one united chorus, they all say, from the first who entered heaven to the last who shall enter there, "We all like sheep have gone astray." The confession, while thus unanimous, is also personal and specific: "Each one has turned to his own way." There is a distinctive sinfulness about every one of these individuals; all are sinful, but each one with some special aggravating factor not found in anyone else. It is the true mark of genuine repentance that while it naturally joins with other penitents, it also stands completely alone. "Each one has turned to his own way" is a confession that each person had sinned against the light given specifically to himself, or sinned with compounding guilt that he did not see in others. This confession is unreserved; there is not a single word to weaken its force, nor a syllable offered by way of excuse. The confession is a total surrender of all claims to self-righteousness. It is the declaration of people who are consciously guilty—guilty under compounding circumstances, guilty without excuse: they stand with their weapons of rebellion broken to pieces, and cry, "We all like sheep have gone astray, each one has turned to his own way." Yet we hear no mournful lamentations accompanying this confession of sin; for the very next sentence turns it almost into a song: "The LORD has laid upon Him the iniquity of us all." It is the most solemn sentence of the three, but it overflows with heavenly comfort. How strange it is that where misery was concentrated, mercy reigned; where sorrow reached its climax, weary souls find rest! A bruised Savior brings healing to bruised hearts. See how the lowliest repentance gives way to joyful assurance through simply gazing at Christ upon the cross!

m.verse: God made Him who knew no sin to be sin on our behalf, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.
paras: Mourning Christian, why do you weep? Are you mourning over your own corruptions? Look to your perfect Lord, and remember that you are complete in Him; you are in God's sight as perfect as if you had never sinned. More than that, the Lord our Righteousness has placed a divine robe upon you, so that you possess more than human righteousness—you have the righteousness of God. To you who mourn because of indwelling sin and depravity, remember that none of your sins can condemn you. You have learned to hate sin; but you have also learned that sin is no longer charged to your account—it was laid upon Christ's head. Your standing is not in yourself; it is in Christ. Your acceptance is not in yourself, but in your Lord. You are as truly accepted by God today, with all your remaining weakness, as you will be when you stand before His throne, free from all corruption. Oh, I urge you, lay hold of this precious truth: perfection in Christ! For you are "complete in Him." With your Savior's robe upon you, you are as holy as the Holy One. "Who is there to condemn us? For Christ Jesus, who died, and more than that was raised to life, is at the right hand of God—and He is interceding for us." Christian, let your heart rejoice, for you are "accepted in the Beloved"—what do you have to fear? Let your face always wear a smile; live near your Master; live on the very borders of the Celestial City; for soon, when your appointed time has come, you will rise to where your Lord Jesus sits, and reign at His right hand. All this is yours because the divine Lord was made to be sin for us, who knew no sin, that we might become the righteousness of God in Him.

e.verse: ... Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD ...
paras: It is wonderfully good for our souls to rise above this present evil world to something nobler and better. The cares of this life and the deceitfulness of wealth are quick to choke everything good within us, leaving us fretful, despondent, and perhaps proud and carnal. It is well for us to cut down these thorns and briers, for heavenly seed sown among them is not likely to produce a harvest; and where can we find a better sickle to cut them down than communion with God and the things of His kingdom? In the valleys of Switzerland, many of the inhabitants are afflicted with bodily ailments and have a pale, sickly look, because the valley air is thick with damp vapors, stifling, and stagnant; but high up on the mountain, you find a hardy people who breathe the clean, fresh air that blows from the pure snows of the Alpine summits. It would be a great blessing if those who dwell in the valley could frequently leave their homes among the marshes and damp fogs to breathe the bracing air of the hills. It is to such a spiritual ascent that I invite you this evening. May the Spirit of God help us leave behind the mists of fear, the fevers of anxiety, and all the troubles that collect in this earthly valley, and ascend the mountains of anticipated joy and blessedness. May God the Holy Spirit cut the cords that hold us down, and help us climb! We sit too often like chained eagles bound to the rock, except that, unlike the eagle, we begin to love our chain, and would perhaps, if put to the test, be reluctant to have it broken. May God now give us grace, even if we cannot escape these chains in our body, to do so in our spirit; and leaving earthly cares, like servants, at the foot of the hill, may our soul, like Abraham, climb to the mountain peak, there to enjoy sweet communion with the Most High.

m.verse: ... they put the cross on him to carry behind Jesus.
paras: We see in Simon carrying the cross a picture of the work of the Church throughout all generations: she is the cross-bearer behind Jesus. Notice this, Christian: Jesus does not suffer so as to exempt you from suffering. He bears a cross, not that you may escape it, but that you may endure it. Christ delivers you from sin, but not from sorrow. Remember that, and expect to suffer.

Yet let us comfort ourselves with the thought that in our case, just as in Simon's, it is not our cross, but Christ's cross that we carry. When you are mistreated for your faith, or when following Christ brings the trial of cruel mocking upon you, remember that it is not your cross—it is Christ's cross. And how delightful it is to carry the cross of our Lord Jesus!

You carry the cross behind Him. You walk in blessed company; your path is marked with the footprints of your Lord. The imprint of His blood-stained shoulder is upon that heavy burden. It is His cross, and He goes before you as a shepherd goes before his sheep. Take up your cross daily, and follow Him.

Do not forget that you bear this cross in partnership. Some believe that Simon carried only one end of the cross, and not the whole burden. That is very possible; Christ may have carried the heavier portion, against the crossbeam, while Simon carried the lighter end. That is certainly true of you: you carry only the light end of the cross, while Christ has borne the crushing weight.

And remember that although Simon had to bear the cross for only a little while, it brought him lasting honor. In the same way, the cross we carry is only for a brief moment, and then we will receive the crown of glory. Surely we should love the cross, and instead of shrinking from it, hold it dear, knowing that it works out for us an eternal weight of glory far beyond all comparison.

e.verse: ... humility comes before honor.
paras: Humiliation of soul always brings a real and positive blessing with it. If we empty our hearts of self, God will fill them abundantly with His love. Whoever desires close communion with Christ should remember the word of the Lord: "This is the one I will esteem: he who is humble and contrite in spirit, who trembles at My word." Stoop down if you would climb to heaven. Do we not say of Jesus, "He descended that He might ascend"? So must you. You must grow downward in humility that you may grow upward in grace; for the sweetest fellowship with heaven is enjoyed by humble souls alone. God will deny no blessing to a thoroughly humbled spirit. "Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven," with all its boundless riches and treasures. The whole royal treasury of God is granted as a free gift to the soul that is humble enough to receive it without becoming proud. God blesses all of us to the fullest extent that is safe for Him to do. If you do not receive a coveted blessing, it is because it is not safe for you to have it. If our heavenly Father were to let your unhumbled spirit win a victory in His holy war, you would steal the crown for yourself, and upon meeting a fresh enemy, you would fall an easy victim; therefore you are kept low for your own enduring safety. When a person is sincerely humble, and never ventures to touch even a single grain of the praise that belongs to God alone, there is scarcely any limit to what God will do for him. Humility prepares our hearts to receive the grace of God, and fits us to deal effectively with our fellow men. True humility is a lovely flower that adorns any garden. It is a seasoning for every dish of life, bringing out the best in every circumstance. Whether in heartfelt prayer or joyful praise, whether in daily work or patient suffering, the genuine salt of humility can never be used in excess.

m.verse: Therefore let us go to Him outside the camp ...
paras: Jesus, bearing His cross, went out to suffer outside the gate. The Christian's reason for leaving the camp of worldly sin and religion is not out of a desire to be eccentric, but because Jesus did so; and the disciple must follow his Master. Christ was not of the world: His life and testimony were a continuous protest against conformity to the world. There was never such overflowing love for mankind as we find in Him; yet He remained separate from sinners. In the same way, Christ's people must go to Him. They must take their stand outside the camp as witnesses for the truth. They must be prepared to walk the narrow path. They must have bold, resolute, courageous hearts, loving Christ first of all, His truth next, and Christ and His truth far above all the world. Jesus calls His people to go outside the camp for their own sanctification. You cannot grow deeply in grace while conforming to the world. The life of separation may be a path of sorrow, but it is the highway of safety; and though this separated life may bring many heartaches and make every day a battle, it is a truly happy life after all. No joy can surpass that of the soldier of Christ: Jesus reveals Himself so graciously and gives such sweet refreshment that the warrior enjoys more peace in his daily struggle than others find in their hours of ease. The highway of holiness is the highway of communion. In this way we hope to win the crown, if by divine grace we faithfully follow Christ outside the camp. The crown of glory follows the cross of separation. A moment's shame will be richly rewarded with eternal honor, and a brief season of bearing witness will seem as nothing when we are forever with the Lord.

e.verse: ... in the name of the LORD I cut them off.
paras: Our Lord Jesus, by His death, did not purchase the right to only a part of us, but to the entire person. In His suffering, He intended our complete sanctification—spirit, soul, and body—so that in this threefold realm He Himself might reign supreme without a rival. It is the calling of the new nature given to us in regeneration to assert the rights of the Lord Jesus Christ. My soul, as a child of God, you must conquer every part of yourself that remains unsanctified; you must bring all your faculties and desires under the gracious scepter of Jesus' rule, and never rest satisfied until He who is King by purchase becomes also King by joyful coronation, reigning supreme within you. Since sin has no claim on any part of us, we engage in a righteous and noble warfare when we seek, in the name of God, to drive it out. O my body, you are a member of Christ: will I tolerate your subjection to the prince of darkness? O my soul, Christ has suffered for your sins and redeemed you with His most precious blood: will I allow your memory to become a storehouse of evil, or your passions to kindle the fires of sin? Will I surrender my judgment to be corrupted by error, or my will to be bound in the chains of iniquity? No, my soul, you belong to Christ, and sin has no claim on you.

Be courageous in this struggle, Christian! Do not be discouraged, as though your spiritual enemies could never be destroyed. You can overcome them—not in your own strength, for the weakest of them would be more than a match for you on your own, but you can and will overcome them through the blood of the Lamb. Do not ask, "How can I drive them out, since they are greater and stronger than I?" Instead, look to the Strong One for strength, wait humbly upon God, and the mighty God of Jacob will surely come to your rescue, so that you will sing of victory through His grace.

m.verse: How long, O men, will My honor be maligned? ...
paras: An instructive writer has compiled a mournful list of the honors that the blinded people of Israel awarded to their long-expected King.

(1.) They gave Him a procession of honor, in which Roman soldiers, Jewish priests, men, and women all took part, while He Himself bore His own cross. This is the triumph that the world awards to Him who comes to overthrow man's greatest foes. Derisive shouts were His only cheers, and cruel taunts His only songs of praise.

(2.) They presented Him with the wine of honor. Instead of a golden cup of generous wine, they offered Him the criminal's stupefying death draught, which He refused because He would keep His senses clear so that He might fully taste of death; and afterward, when He cried, "I thirst," they gave Him vinegar mixed with gall, thrust to His lips upon a sponge. Oh, what wretched, detestable hostility toward the King's Son!

(3.) He was provided with a guard of honor, who demonstrated their esteem for Him by gambling over His clothing, which they had seized as their plunder. Such was the bodyguard of the adored of heaven: a squad of four crude soldiers gambling at His feet.

(4.) A throne of honor was found for Him upon the bloody tree; no easier resting place would rebellious men grant to their sovereign Lord. The cross was, in fact, the full expression of the world's attitude toward Him: "There," they seemed to say, "You Son of God, this is the way God Himself would be treated if only we could reach Him."

(5.) His title of honor was nominally "King of the Jews," but the blinded nation openly rejected it, practically naming Him "King of criminals" by choosing Barabbas instead, and by placing Jesus in the place of greatest shame between two thieves. His glory was thus turned into shame by the sons of men; yet that same glory will forever gladden the eyes of saints and angels throughout all eternity.

e.verse: Deliver me from bloodguilt, O God, the God of my salvation, and my tongue will sing of Your righteousness.
paras: In this SOLEMN CONFESSION, it is encouraging to observe that David plainly names his sin. He does not call it manslaughter, nor speak of it as an oversight through which an unfortunate accident happened to a worthy man; instead, he calls it by its honest name: bloodguilt. He did not physically strike down the husband of Bathsheba, but it was planned in David's heart that Uriah should die, and before the Lord he stood as his murderer. Learn in confession to be completely honest with God. Do not give pleasant names to foul sins; call them whatever you like, they will smell no sweeter. What God sees them to be, strive to feel them to be, and with genuine openness of heart acknowledge their true character. Notice that David was deeply weighed down by the heinousness of his guilt. It is easy to utter words, but difficult to feel their weight. The fifty-first Psalm is the true portrait of a contrite spirit. Let us seek after that same brokenness of heart; for no matter how excellent our words may be, if our hearts do not recognize how truly deserving of judgment our sin is, we cannot expect to find forgiveness.

Our text contains A HEARTFELT PRAYER—it is addressed to the God of salvation. It is His divine prerogative to forgive; it is His very nature and office to save those who seek His face. Better still, the text calls Him the God of my salvation. Yes, blessed be His name! While I am coming to Him through Jesus' blood, I can already rejoice in the God of my salvation.

The psalmist ends with A COMMENDABLE VOW: if God will deliver him, he will sing—no, more than that, he will "sing aloud." Who could sing in any lesser way of such great mercy as this? But take note of the subject of the song—"YOUR RIGHTEOUSNESS." We must sing of the finished work of our precious Savior; and whoever knows the most of forgiving love will sing the loudest.

m.verse: For if men do these things while the tree is green, what will happen when it is dry?
paras: Among other interpretations of this thought-provoking question, the following is rich and full of solemn instruction: "If the innocent substitute for sinners suffers like this, what will happen when the sinner himself—the dry tree—falls into the hands of an angry God?" When God saw Jesus in the sinner's place, He did not spare Him; and when He finds the unregenerate without Christ, He will not spare them. Sinner, Jesus was led away by His enemies: so also will you be dragged away by demons to the place appointed for you. Jesus was forsaken by God; and if He, who was only a sinner by imputation, was forsaken, how much more will you be? "Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?" What an awful cry! But what will be your cry when you say, "O God! O God! Why have You forsaken me?" And the answer will come back: "Since you neglected all My counsel and wanted none of My reproof, I in turn will laugh at your calamity; I will mock when terror comes upon you." If God did not spare His own Son, how much less will He spare you! What lashes of burning wire will strike you when conscience accuses you with all its terrors! You who are richest, you who are most careless, you who are most self-righteous—who would want to stand in your place when God shall say, "Awake, O sword, against the man who rejected Me; strike him, and let him feel the punishment forever"? Jesus was spit upon by wicked men: sinner, what shame will be yours! We cannot summarize in a single word the vast weight of sorrow that converged upon the head of Jesus when He died for us; therefore, it is impossible to describe what oceans of grief must sweep over your soul if you die as you are right now. You may die in that state; you may die this very hour. By the agonies of Christ, by His wounds and by His precious blood, do not bring upon yourselves the wrath to come! Trust in the Son of God, and you will never perish.

e.verse: ... I will fear no evil, for You are with me ...
paras: Behold how independent of outward circumstances the Holy Spirit can make the Christian! What a radiant light can shine within us when all is dark outside! How steadfast, joyful, calm, and peaceful we can be, even when the world is shaken and the pillars of the earth give way! Even death itself, with all its terrors, has no power to silence the music of a believer's heart; rather, it makes that melody sweeter, clearer, and more heavenly, until the last service death can perform is to let the earthly song dissolve into the heavenly chorus, and temporary joy pass into eternal bliss! Let us place our confidence, then, in the blessed Spirit's power to comfort us. Dear reader, are you facing poverty? Do not fear; the divine Spirit can give you, in your need, a greater abundance than the rich possess in their wealth. You do not know what joys may be stored up for you in the humble cottage around which grace will plant the roses of contentment. Are you conscious of failing strength in your body? Do you anticipate long nights of weariness and days of pain? Oh, do not be downcast! That sickbed can become a throne of grace to you. You hardly know how every sharp pain that shoots through your body may serve as a refining fire to burn away your dross—a beam of glory lighting up the secret depths of your soul. Are your eyes growing dim? Jesus will be your light. Does your hearing begin to fail? The name of Jesus will be your soul's sweetest music, and His presence your supreme delight. Socrates used to say, "Philosophers can be happy without music"; but Christians can be far happier than philosophers when every outward source of joy is stripped away. In You, my God, my heart will triumph, whatever troubles may threaten from outside! By Your power, O blessed Spirit, my soul will be exceedingly glad, even if everything should fail me here below.

m.verse: A great number of people followed Him, including women who kept mourning and wailing for Him.
paras: Amid the unruly mob that hounded the Redeemer to His doom, there were some gracious souls whose bitter anguish found vent in wailing and lamentation—fitting music to accompany that march of sorrow. When in imagination my soul sees the Savior bearing His cross to Calvary, she joins the godly women and weeps with them; for there is truly cause for grief—a cause lying deeper than those mourning women knew. They bewailed innocence mistreated, goodness persecuted, love bleeding, and meekness about to die; but my heart has a far deeper and more bitter cause to mourn. My sins were the scourges that lacerated those blessed shoulders, and crowned with thorns those bleeding brows. My sins cried, "Crucify Him! Crucify Him!" and laid the cross upon His gracious shoulders. His being led forth to die is sorrow enough for one eternity; but that I was His murderer is infinitely more grief than one poor fountain of tears can express.

Why those women loved and wept is not hard to guess; yet they could not have had greater reasons for love and grief than my heart has. Nain's widow saw her son restored—but I myself have been raised to newness of life. Peter's mother-in-law was cured of fever—but I of the greater plague of sin. Out of Mary Magdalene seven demons were cast—but a whole legion out of me. Mary and Martha were favored with visits—but He dwells with me. His mother bore His body—but He is formed in me, the hope of glory. In no way behind those holy women in debt, let me not fall behind them in gratitude or sorrow.

Love and grief my heart dividing,
With my tears His feet I'll lave—
Constant still in heart abiding,
Weep for Him who died to save.

e.verse: ... Your gentleness exalts me.
paras: These words may well be translated, "Your goodness has made me great." David gratefully ascribed all his greatness not to his own goodness, but to the goodness of God. "Your providence" is another valid reading; and providence is nothing less than divine goodness in action. Goodness is the bud of which providence is the flower, or goodness is the seed of which providence is the harvest. Some render it, "Your help," which is only another word for providence—providence being the faithful ally of the saints, helping them in the service of their Lord. Or again, "Your humility has made me great." "Your condescension" may serve as a comprehensive translation, combining all these thoughts, including that of divine humility. God's willingness to make Himself small is the very cause of our being made great. We are so frail and small that if God were to manifest His greatness without condescension, we would be crushed beneath His feet; but God, who must stoop even to view the skies and bend low to see what angels do, turns His gaze lower still: He looks upon the humble and contrite, and makes them great. There are yet other translations, such as the Septuagint, which reads, "Your discipline"—Your fatherly correction—"has made me great"; while the ancient Aramaic paraphrase reads, "Your word has increased me." Yet the central truth remains the same: David ascribes all his greatness to the condescending goodness of his Father in heaven. May this same praise echo in our hearts tonight as we cast our crowns at Jesus' feet and cry, "Your gentleness has made me great!" How marvelous has been our experience of God's gentleness! How gentle have been His corrections! How gentle His forbearance! How gentle His teachings! How gentle the drawings of His love! Meditate upon this theme, believer. Let gratitude be awakened, let humility be deepened, and let love be rekindled before you fall asleep tonight.

m.verse: ... the place called The Skull ...
paras: The hill of comfort is the hill of Calvary; the house of consolation is built with the wood of the cross; the temple of heavenly blessing is founded upon the rock split open by the spear that pierced His side. No scene in all sacred history gladdens the soul like the tragedy of Calvary.

Is it not strange, the darkest hour
That ever dawned on sinful earth,
Should touch the heart with softer power,
For comfort, than an angel's mirth?
That to the Cross the mourner's eye should turn,
Sooner than where the stars of Bethlehem burn?

Light springs forth from the midday darkness of Golgotha, and every herb of the field blooms sweetly beneath the shadow of that once-accursed tree. In that place of thirst, grace has opened a fountain that flows continually with water pure as crystal, each single drop capable of healing the woes of mankind. You who have passed through seasons of spiritual conflict will confess that it was not on Olivet that you found comfort, nor on the heights of Sinai, nor on Tabor; but Gethsemane, Gabbatha, and Golgotha have brought true consolation to your soul. The bitter herbs of Gethsemane have taken away the bitterness of your life; the scourge of Gabbatha has driven away your cares, and the groans of Calvary bring us comfort rich and rare. We never could have known Christ's love in all its heights and depths if He had not died; nor could we fathom the Father's deep affection if He had not given His Son to die. The common mercies of daily life all sing of love, just as the seashell whispers of the deep sea from which it came; but if we desire to hear the full music of the ocean itself, we must look not at everyday blessings, but at the sacred work accomplished at the crucifixion. Whoever desires to know love, let him go to Calvary and behold the Man of Sorrows die.

e.verse: ... an angel of the God to whom I belong and whom I serve stood beside me ...
paras: A fierce tempest and long darkness, together with the imminent danger of shipwreck, had plunged the ship's crew into desperate distress; yet one man alone among them remained completely calm, and by his words the rest took courage. Paul was the only man on board who had the heart to say, "Men, take courage!" There were veteran Roman soldiers on board and experienced sailors, and yet their Jewish prisoner possessed more courage than them all. He had a secret Friend who sustained his heart. The Lord Jesus dispatched a heavenly messenger to whisper words of comfort in the ear of His faithful servant; therefore, he wore a radiant face and spoke like a man at peace.

If we fear the Lord, we may expect timely divine interventions when our circumstances are at their worst. Angels are not kept away from us by raging storms, nor hindered by the darkness. Seraphs consider it no humiliation to visit the humblest members of the heavenly family. If angelic visits seem few and far between in ordinary times, they will be frequent in our nights of storm and tossing. Earthly friends may abandon us when we are under pressure, but our fellowship with the heavenly messengers will only grow richer; and strengthened by words of love brought to us from the throne by way of Jacob's ladder, we will be strong to accomplish great things for God. Dear reader, is this an hour of deep distress for you? Then ask for His personal, tailored help. Jesus is the Angel of the covenant, and if His presence is sought from the heart, it will never be denied. What that presence brings in joy and courage, those well remember who, like Paul, have had an angel of God stand beside them in a night of storm, when anchors could no longer hold and the rocks were dangerously near.

O angel of my God, be near,
Amid the darkness hush my fear;
Loud roars the wild tempestuous sea,
Your presence, Lord, shall comfort me.

m.verse: I am poured out like water, and all my bones are disjointed.
paras: Did earth or heaven ever behold a sadder spectacle of suffering! In soul and body, our Lord felt Himself to be as weak as water poured out upon the ground. The placing of the cross into its socket had jolted Him with terrible violence, straining every ligament, agonizing every nerve, and disjointing all His bones. Burdened by His own weight, the exalted Sufferer felt the agony increasing with every passing moment of those six long hours. His sense of faintness and utter exhaustion was overpowering, while in His own consciousness He became a mass of misery and overwhelming pain. When Daniel beheld his great vision, he described what he felt: "No strength was left in me; my face turned deathly pale, and I was helpless." How much more faint must our greater Prophet have been when He beheld the dreadful vision of God's wrath and felt its full weight in His own soul! For us, suffering such as our Lord endured would have been unendurable, and merciful unconsciousness would have come to our relief; but in His case, He was wounded and felt the sword; He drained the cup and tasted every single drop.

O King of Grief! (a title strange, yet true
To Thee of all kings only due)
O King of Wounds! how shall I grieve for Thee,
Who in all grief preventest me!

As we kneel before our ascended Savior's throne, let us remember the path by which He prepared it as a throne of grace for us. Let us in spirit drink of His cup, so that we may be strengthened for our own hour of sorrow whenever it may come. In His physical body every member suffered, and so it must be in His spiritual body; but just as His body came forth unharmed through all His griefs into resurrection glory and power, so also His mystical body will pass through the furnace without even the smell of smoke upon it.

e.verse: Consider my affliction and trouble, and take away all my sins.
paras: It is well with us when prayers about our sorrows are joined with pleas concerning our sins—when, under the chastening hand of God, we are not entirely consumed by our pain, but remember our offenses against Him. It is also good to take both sorrow and sin to the very same place. It was to God that David carried his grief, and it was to God that he confessed his sin. Observe, then: we must take our sorrows to God. Even your smallest sorrows you may cast upon Him, for He counts the very hairs of your head; and your greatest griefs you may commit to Him, for He holds the ocean in the hollow of His hand. Go to Him, whatever your present trouble may be, and you will find Him both able and willing to relieve you. But we must take our sins to God as well. We must carry them to the cross, so that the blood of Christ may cover them, purging away their guilt and breaking their defiling power.

The central lesson of this text is that we must go to the Lord with our sorrows and our sins in the right spirit. Notice that all David asks concerning his sorrow is, "Consider my affliction and trouble"; but his next petition is far more urgent, definite, and direct—"Take away all my sins." Many sufferers would have reversed it: "Remove my affliction and my pain, and merely look at my sins." But David does not pray that way. He cries, "Lord, as for my affliction and my pain, I will not dictate to Your wisdom. Look upon them; I leave them entirely to You. I would be glad to have my pain removed, but do as You will. As for my sins, Lord, I know what must be done: they must be forgiven; I cannot bear to lie under their curse for a single moment." A Christian counts sorrow far lighter in the scale than sin: he can endure that his troubles continue, but he cannot bear the crushing burden of his transgressions.

m.verse: ... My heart is like wax; it melts away within me.
paras: Our blessed Lord experienced a terrible sinking and melting of soul. "A man’s spirit can endure sickness, but who can bear a broken spirit?" Deep depression of spirit is the most grievous of all trials; everything else seems like nothing in comparison. The suffering Savior might well cry to His God, "Do not be far from Me," for above all other seasons a person needs God when his heart is melted within him under the weight of grief. Believer, come near the cross this morning, and humbly adore the King of glory, who was once brought far lower in mental distress and inward agony than any one of us; and notice His fitness to be our faithful High Priest, who is able to sympathize with our weaknesses. Especially let those among us whose sadness springs directly from the loss of a conscious sense of our Father's love enter into intimate communion with Jesus. Let us not give way to despair, since through this very dark room the Master has walked before us. Our souls may sometimes long, faint, and thirst even to agony to behold the light of the Lord's countenance; at such times let us anchor our souls in the sweet reality of our great High Priest's sympathy. Our tiny drops of sorrow may well be forgotten in the boundless ocean of His griefs; but how high our love ought to rise! Come in, O strong and deep love of Jesus, like the sea at high tide: cover all my powers, drown all my sins, wash away all my cares, and lift up my earth-bound soul, carrying it straight to my Lord's feet. There let me lie, a broken shell washed ashore by His love, having no merit or value of my own, only venturing to whisper that if He will bend His ear to me, He will hear within my heart the faint echoes of the vast ocean of His own love, which has brought me where it is my joy to rest, even at His feet forever.

e.verse: ... near the king’s garden ...
paras: The mention of the king's garden by Nehemiah brings to mind the paradise that the King of kings prepared for Adam. Sin has utterly ruined that fair dwelling of delights, driving out the children of men to cultivate the ground, which brings forth thorns and briers to them. My soul, remember the fall, for it was your fall. Weep bitterly that the Lord of love was so shamefully wronged by the father of the human race, of which you are an undeserving member. Behold how wild beasts and demons now haunt this earth, which was once a garden of pure delights.

Look at another King's garden, which the King waters with His bloody sweat—Gethsemane, whose bitter herbs are far sweeter to renewed souls than even Eden's luscious fruits. There the destructive work of the serpent in the first garden was undone; there the curse was lifted from the earth and borne by the woman's promised seed. My soul, ponder deeply the agony and the passion; go to the garden of the olive press, and behold your great Redeemer rescuing you from your fallen condition. This is the garden of gardens indeed, in which the soul may see both the guilt of sin and the power of divine love—two sights that surpass all others.

Is there no other King's garden? Yes, my heart, you are, or ought to be, just such a garden. How do your flowers flourish? Does any choice fruit appear? Does the King walk within and rest in the quiet bowers of your spirit? Let me see that the plants are tended and watered, and that the destructive foxes are driven out. Come, Lord, and let the heavenly wind blow at Your coming, that the fragrance of Your garden may spread abroad. Nor must I forget the King's garden of the church. O Lord, send prosperity to it! Rebuild her walls, nourish her plants, ripen her fruits, and from the vast wilderness reclaim the barren waste, making of it "a King's garden."

m.verse: My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh ...
paras: Myrrh may well be chosen as a symbol of Jesus on account of its preciousness, its perfume, its pleasantness, its healing, preserving, and disinfecting qualities, and its close connection with sacrifice. But why is He compared to "a bundle of myrrh"? First, for abundance. He is not a mere drop of it; He is a full casket. He is not a sprig or flower of it, but a whole bundle. There is enough in Christ for all my necessities; let me never hesitate to draw from Him. Our Beloved is compared to a "bundle" again, for variety: for in Christ there is not only the one thing necessary, but in "Him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead bodily"—everything we could ever need is in Him. Consider Jesus in His different offices, and you will see a marvelous variety—Prophet, Priest, King, Husband, Friend, Shepherd. View Him in His life, death, resurrection, ascension, and second coming; see Him in His virtue, gentleness, courage, self-denial, love, faithfulness, truth, and righteousness—everywhere He is a treasury of preciousness. He is a "bundle of myrrh" for preservation—not loose myrrh scattered about, but myrrh safely kept in a casket. We must value Him as our greatest treasure; we must prize His words and His ordinances; and we must guard our thoughts and knowledge of Him under lock and key, so that the enemy may not steal anything from us. Moreover, Jesus is a "bundle of myrrh" for special distinction. This emblem speaks of distinguishing, sovereign grace. From before the foundation of the world, He was set apart for His people; and He gives forth His fragrance only to those who know how to enter into intimate communion with Him. Oh, blessed are the people whom the Lord has admitted into His secrets, and for whom He sets Himself apart! Truly happy are they who are led to say, "My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh!"

e.verse: He is to lay his hand on the head of the burnt offering, so it can be accepted on his behalf to make atonement for him.
paras: Our Lord's being made "sin for us" is set forth here by the deeply significant transfer of guilt to the sacrifice, performed by the elders of the people. The laying on of the hand was not a mere superficial touch, for in other passages of Scripture the original word carries the meaning of leaning heavily, as in the expression, "Your wrath lies heavily upon me" (Psalm 88:7). Surely this is the very essence and nature of true faith, which not only brings us into contact with the great Substitute, but teaches us to lean upon Him with all the crushing burden of our guilt. The LORD caused to fall upon the head of the Substitute all the offenses of His covenant people; yet each one of the redeemed is brought personally to ratify this solemn covenant act, when by grace he is enabled by faith to lay his hand upon the head of the "Lamb slain from before the foundation of the world." Believer, do you remember that joyful day when you first experienced pardon through Jesus the Sin-Bearer? Can you not make glad confession, and join with me in saying, "My soul recalls its day of deliverance with delight! Laden with guilt and filled with fears, I saw my Savior as my Substitute, and I laid my hand upon Him. Oh, how timidly at first! But courage grew and confidence deepened until I leaned my whole soul upon Him; and now it is my unceasing joy to know that my sins are no longer imputed to me, but laid upon Him. And just as with the debts of the wounded traveler, Jesus, like the Good Samaritan, has said of all my past and future failures, 'Put that on My account.'" Blessed discovery! Eternal comfort of a grateful heart!

My numerous sins transferred to Him,
Shall never more be found,
Lost in His blood's atoning stream,
Where every crime is drowned!

m.verse: All who see me mock me; they sneer and shake their heads:
paras: Mockery was a bitter element in our Lord's suffering. Judas mocked Him in the garden; the chief priests and scribes laughed Him to scorn; Herod treated Him with contempt; the servants and soldiers jeered at Him and brutally insulted Him; Pilate and his guards ridiculed His royalty; and on the cross all kinds of cruel jests and vile taunts were hurled at Him. Ridicule is always hard to bear, but when we are in intense pain it is so heartless, so cruel, that it cuts us to the quick. Imagine the Savior crucified, wracked with agony far beyond all human comprehension, and then picture that mocking crowd, shaking their heads and sneering in bitter contempt at one solitary, suffering Sufferer! Surely there must have been something more in the crucified One than they could see, or else such a vast crowd would not unanimously have honored Him with such fierce contempt. Was this not evil confessing, in the very hour of its apparent triumph, that after all it could do nothing more than mock that victorious goodness which was then reigning upon the cross? O Jesus, "despised and rejected by men," how could You die for those who treated You so cruelly? Here is love amazing, love divine—yes, love beyond all measure! We, too, despised You in the days before our regeneration, and even since our new birth we have too often enthroned the world in our hearts; yet You bled to heal our wounds, and died to give us life. Oh, that we could set You on a glorious high throne in the hearts of all people! We would sound Your praises over land and sea until all mankind adores You as universally as once they rejected You.

Your creatures wrong You, O Sovereign Good!
You are not loved, because not understood:
This grieves me most, that vain pursuits beguile
Ungrateful men, regardless of Your smile.

e.verse: Tell the righteous it will be well with them ...
paras: It is well with the righteous ALWAYS. If the Scripture had said, "Tell the righteous that it is well with him in his prosperity," we would have been thankful for so great a blessing, for prosperity is an hour of spiritual peril, and it is a gift from heaven to be delivered from its snares.
