Or if it had been written, "It is well with him when under persecution," we would have been thankful for so sustaining an assurance, for persecution is hard to bear; but when no specific season is mentioned, all times are included. God's promises must always be understood in their fullest sense. From the beginning of the year to its close, from the first gathering of evening shadows until the morning star shines, in every condition and under every circumstance, it shall be well with the righteous. It is so well with him that we could not imagine it to be better: he is well fed, feeding upon the flesh and blood of Jesus; he is well clothed, wearing the imputed righteousness of Christ; he is well sheltered, dwelling in God; he is well married, his soul knit in spiritual union to Christ; he is well provided for, for the Lord is his Shepherd; and he is well endowed, for heaven is his everlasting inheritance. It is well with the righteous—well upon divine authority, for the mouth of God speaks the comforting assurance. Beloved, if God declares that all is well, ten thousand demons may shout that it is ill, but we can laugh them all to scorn. Blessed be God for a faith that enables us to trust Him even when creation contradicts Him! The Word declares that it is well with you at all times, believer; therefore, if you cannot see it, let God's promise take the place of sight. Yes, believe it on divine authority far more firmly than if your own eyes and feelings confirmed it. The one whom God blesses is blessed indeed, and whatever His lips declare is truth most sure and steadfast.

m.verse: My God, my God, why have You forsaken me? ...
paras: Here we behold the Savior in the lowest depths of His sorrow. No other place so vividly displays the griefs of Christ as Calvary, and no moment at Calvary is so filled with agony as that in which His cry pierces the air: "My God, my God, why have You forsaken Me?" At this moment, extreme physical weakness was joined with acute mental anguish from the shame and public humiliation through which He had to pass; and to bring His grief to its darkest climax, He suffered spiritual agony surpassing all human expression, caused by the withdrawal of His Father's presence. This was the black midnight of His horror; then it was that He descended into the abyss of suffering. No human mind can enter into the full depth of these words. Some of us think at times that we could cry, "My God, my God, why have You forsaken me?" There are seasons when the brightness of our Father's smile is eclipsed by clouds and darkness; but let us remember that God never truly forsakes us. With us, it is only a temporary and apparent forsaking, but in Christ's case it was a terrible, real forsaking. We grieve at the slightest withdrawal of our Father's comforting presence; but who can measure the depth of agony caused by the actual turning away of God's face from His own beloved Son?

In our case, our cry is often prompted by unbelief; in His case, it was the utterance of an awful reality, for God had truly turned away from Him for a time. O distressed and trembling soul, you who once walked in the sunshine of God's face but are now in darkness, remember that He has not really abandoned you. God behind the clouds is as truly our God as when He shines forth in all the brightness of His grace. Yet since the mere thought that He has forsaken us causes such deep sorrow, what must the grief of the Savior have been when He cried out, "My God, my God, why have You forsaken Me?"

e.verse: ... shepherd them and carry them forever.
paras: God's people continually need lifting up. By nature they are weighed down and prone to sink. They have no wings of their own, or if they have, they are like the dove of old lying among the sheepfolds; they need divine grace to make them mount on wings shimmering with silver, and feathers of yellow gold. By nature, sparks fly upward, but the sinful hearts of men tend downward. O Lord, "lift them up forever!" David himself declared, "To You, O LORD, I lift up my soul," recognizing the constant need for other believers to be lifted up as well as himself. When you seek this blessing for your own soul, never forget to ask it for others. There are three ways in which God's people need to be lifted up. First, they need to be elevated in character. Lift them up, O Lord; do not let Your people live like the world! The whole world lies in the power of the evil one; lift them far above it! Worldly people chase after silver and gold, seeking their own pleasures and the gratification of their lusts; but Lord, lift Your people up above all these things, and keep them from being "muck-rakers," as John Bunyan called the man who was always scraping after earthly dust! Set their hearts upon their risen Lord and their heavenly inheritance. Second, believers need victory in spiritual conflict. In the day of battle, if they seem to stumble, O Lord, give them the victory. If the enemy's foot is on their neck for a moment, help them grasp the sword of the Spirit, and ultimately win the day. Lord, lift up Your children's spirits in the struggle; let them not sit in the dust, mourning without hope. Do not let the adversary torment them; but if they have been persecuted, like Hannah, let them sing of the mercy of a delivering God.
Finally, we may ask our Lord to lift them up at the last day! Lift them up by taking them home, raise their bodies from the tomb, and bring their souls to Your eternal kingdom in glory.

m.verse: ... the precious blood of Christ ...
paras: Standing at the foot of the cross, we behold hands, feet, and side, all pouring forth crimson streams of precious blood. It is "precious" because of its redeeming and atoning power. By it the sins of Christ's people are fully atoned for; they are redeemed from the curse of the law, reconciled to God, and made one with Him. Christ's blood is also "precious" in its cleansing power: it "cleanses from all sin." "Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be as white as snow." Through Jesus' blood there is not a single spot left upon any believer; no wrinkle or any such blemish remains. O precious blood, which makes us clean, washing away the stains of our deep iniquity, and enabling us to stand accepted in the Beloved, despite all the ways we have rebelled against our God! The blood of Christ is likewise "precious" in its preserving power. We are completely safe from the destroying angel beneath the sprinkled blood. Remember that it is God's sight of the blood which is the true reason we are spared. Here is comfort for us when the eye of our faith is dim, for God's eye remains unchanged. The blood of Christ is "precious" also in its sanctifying influence. The very same blood that justifies by taking away sin also works to revive the new nature, leading it forward to conquer sin and obey the commands of God. There is no motive for holiness so powerful as that which streams from the wounds of Jesus. And this blood is unspeakably precious because it possesses an overcoming power. It is written, "They overcame him by the blood of the Lamb." How could it be otherwise? Whoever fights with the precious blood of Jesus wields a weapon that can never know defeat. The blood of Jesus! Sin dies in its presence, death loses its sting, and heaven's gates are opened wide. By the blood of Jesus we will march on, conquering and to conquer, as long as we trust its saving power!

e.verse: ... his hands remained steady until the sun went down.
paras: So mighty was the prayer of Moses that everything depended upon it. The petitions of Moses defeated the enemy far more than the sword of Joshua. Yet both were necessary. In the spiritual conflict of the soul, strength and devotion, decision and prayer, courage and fervor, must join their forces, and all will be well. You must wrestle against your sin, but the greatest part of that wrestling must take place in private with God. Prayer, like the rod of Moses, holds up the token of the covenant before the Lord. That rod was the emblem of God's power working with Moses, the symbol of divine authority in Israel. Learn, pleading believer, to hold up the promise and the oath of God before Him. The Lord cannot deny His own declarations. Hold up the rod of promise, and you will receive what you ask.

Moses grew weary, and his friends came to assist him. When at any time your prayer begins to flag, let faith support one hand, and let holy hope lift up the other; then prayer, resting upon the Stone of Israel, the Rock of our salvation, will persevere and prevail. Beware of growing weary in devotion; if Moses felt it, who can escape? It is far easier to fight against sin in public than to pray against it in private. It is worth noting that Joshua never grew weary in the battle, but Moses did grow weary in prayer; for the more spiritual the endeavor, the more difficult it is for flesh and blood to sustain it. Let us pray, then, for special strength; and may the Spirit of God, Who helps us in our weakness, just as He provided help for Moses, enable us to keep our hands steady until the sun goes down—until the evening of life is past, and we awake to the rising of a better sun in that land where prayer is swallowed up in everlasting praise.

m.verse: ... to the sprinkled blood that speaks a better word than the blood of Abel.
paras: Reader, have you come to the blood of sprinkling? The question is not whether you have attained a knowledge of doctrine, or an observance of ceremonies, or a particular form of religious experience, but have you come to the blood of Jesus? The blood of Jesus is the lifeblood of all true godliness. If you have truly come to Jesus, we know how you came—the Holy Spirit graciously drew you there. You came to the blood of sprinkling with no merit of your own. Guilty, lost, and helpless, you came to take that blood, and that blood alone, as your everlasting hope. You came to the cross of Christ with a trembling and an aching heart; and oh, what a precious sound it was to hear the voice of the blood of Jesus! The dropping of His blood is like the music of heaven to repentant sinners on earth. We are full of sin, but the Savior bids us lift our eyes to Him, and as we gaze upon His streaming wounds, each drop of blood, as it falls, cries, "It is finished; I have made an end of sin; I have brought in everlasting righteousness." Oh, what sweet language from the precious blood of Jesus! If you have come to that blood once, you will come to it constantly. Your life will be defined by "looking to Jesus." Your whole conduct will be summed up in this: "coming to Him"—not to Whom I have come once in the past, but to Whom I am continually coming. If you have ever come to the blood of sprinkling, you will feel your need of coming to it every single day. Anyone who does not desire to wash in it daily has never washed in it at all. Believers always consider it their joy and privilege that this fountain remains open. Past experiences are questionable nourishment for Christians; only a present coming to Christ can give us joy and comfort. This morning let us sprinkle our doorposts afresh with blood, and then feast upon the Lamb, assured that the destroying angel will pass us by.

e.verse: ... Sir, we want to see Jesus.
paras: The worldly person's constant cry is, "Who will show us any good?" He seeks satisfaction in earthly comforts, pleasures, and riches. But the spiritually awakened sinner knows of only one true good: "Oh, that I knew where I might find Him!" When truly awakened to feel his guilt, if you could pour the gold of India at his feet, he would say, "Take it away; I want to find Him!" It is a blessed thing when a person brings his desires into focus, centering them on a single object. When someone has fifty different desires, his heart resembles a stagnant marsh, breeding disease and decay; but when all his desires are directed into a single channel, his heart becomes like a river of pure water, flowing swiftly to fertilize the fields. Blessed is the one who has one desire, if that desire is set upon Christ, even if it is not yet realized. If Jesus is the soul's supreme desire, it is a sure sign of divine grace at work within. Such a person will never be content with empty outward rituals. He will say, "I want Christ; I must have Him—mere external forms are of no use to me; I want Himself! Do not offer me these; you are offering an empty pitcher while I am dying of thirst. Give me living water, or I die! Jesus is my soul's desire. I want to see Jesus!"

Is this your condition, dear reader, at this moment? Do you have but one desire, and is that desire Christ? Then you are not far from the kingdom of heaven. Do you have only one wish in your heart, that you may be washed from all your sins in Jesus' blood? Can you truly say, "I would give all I have to be a Christian; I would give up everything I possess and hope for, if only I could know that I have a part in Christ"? Then, despite all your fears, take heart! The Lord loves you, and you will soon step out into the daylight, rejoicing in the freedom with which Christ sets us free.

m.verse: ... she tied the scarlet cord in the window.
paras: Rahab depended for her preservation upon the promise of the spies, whom she regarded as representatives of the God of Israel. Her faith was simple and firm, and it was marked by prompt obedience. To tie the scarlet cord in the window was a seemingly trivial act, but she did not dare to risk omitting it. Come, my soul, is there not a searching lesson here for you? Have you been attentive to all your Lord's will, even when some of His commands might appear non-essential? Have you observed, in His own appointed way, the two ordinances of believer's baptism and the Lord's Supper? To neglect them reveals a grievous lack of loving obedience in your heart. From now on, be blameless in all things, even down to the tying of a thread, if it has been commanded by your Lord.

This act of Rahab presents an even more solemn lesson. Have I trusted wholeheartedly in the precious blood of Jesus? Have I tied the scarlet cord, as with an unbreakable knot in my window, so that my faith can never be displaced? Can I look out toward the Dead Sea of my sins, or toward the heavenly Jerusalem of my hopes, without seeing the blood, and viewing everything in connection with its redeeming power? A passerby readily sees a cord of so vivid a color hanging from a window; and it will be well for me if my life makes the transforming power of the atonement evident to every onlooker. What is there to be ashamed of? Let men or demons mock if they will; the blood of Christ is my boast and my song! My soul, there is One Who will see that scarlet cord, even when through weakness of faith you cannot see it yourself: the LORD, the Avenger of sin, will see it and pass over you. The walls of Jericho collapsed, yet Rahab's house was on the wall and stood unshaken; my human nature is bound up with fallen humanity, and yet when judgment strikes the world, I will be completely secure. My soul, tie the scarlet cord in your window afresh, and rest in peace.

e.verse: ... You have said, “I will surely make you prosper ...”
paras: When Jacob was on the other side of the brook Jabbok, and Esau was approaching with four hundred armed men, he earnestly sought God's protection; and as his supreme argument he pleaded, "You have said, 'I will surely make you prosper.'" Oh, the unstoppable force of that plea! He was holding God to His own word: "You said." The attribute of God's faithfulness is a glorious horn of the altar for faith to lay hold of; but the specific promise, which embodies that faithfulness and applies it directly, is an even stronger anchor: "You said, 'I will surely make you prosper.'" Has He spoken, and will He not act? Has He promised, and will He not fulfill it? "Let God be true, though every man a liar." Will He not be faithful? Will He not keep His covenant? Will not every word that proceeds from His lips stand firm and be accomplished? Solomon, at the dedication of the temple, used this very same mighty plea: he asked God to remember the word He had spoken to his father David, and to bless that place. When an honorable man signs a promissory note, his character is at stake; he must pay the debt when the due date arrives, or else forfeit his reputation. It will never be said that God defaults on His commitments! The integrity of the Most High has never been questioned, and it never will be. He is punctual to the exact moment: He is never ahead of His time, and He is never late. Search God's Word from beginning to end, and compare it with the lived experience of His people; you will find that the two agree perfectly from first to last. Many an aged saint has affirmed with Joshua: "Not one word has failed of all the good promises the LORD your God gave you; every one has been fulfilled." If you possess a divine promise, you need not plead it with an "if"—you may urge it with bold assurance. The Lord intended to fulfill the promise, or He would never have given it. God does not speak merely to soothe us for a season with the intention of disappointing us in the end; whenever He speaks, He fully intends to do all that He has said.

m.verse: ... the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.
paras: No small miracle was performed in the tearing of so strong and thick a veil; yet it was not intended merely as a display of power—it teaches us many profound lessons. The ceremonial law was abolished, and like a worn-out garment, it was torn and laid aside. When Jesus died, the animal sacrifices were forever completed because all were fulfilled in Him; therefore, the place of their presentation was marked with an unmistakable sign of its end. That tear also unveiled the hidden things of the old covenant: the mercy seat could now be openly seen, and the glory of God shone forth above it. Through the death of our Lord Jesus, we have a clear revelation of God, for He was unlike Moses, who had to put a veil over his face. Life and immortality have been brought to light, and things kept hidden since the foundation of the world are made plain in Him. The annual Day of Atonement was permanently fulfilled. The atoning blood, which once every year had been sprinkled within the veil, was now offered once for all by our great High Priest, and the place of that symbolic ceremony was opened wide. No blood of bulls or goats is needed now, for Jesus has entered the Most Holy Place once for all with His own blood. Direct access to God is now granted to every believer in Christ Jesus. It is not merely a narrow opening through which we may catch a glimpse of the mercy seat; the tear extends completely from top to bottom. We may now come boldly to the throne of grace. Can we doubt that the opening of the Most Holy Place through our Lord's dying cry was a prophetic picture of the opening of the gates of paradise to all the saints through His suffering? Our crucified Lord holds the key of heaven: what He opens, no one can shut. Let us enter with Him into the heavenly realms and sit with Him there until all His enemies are made His footstool.

e.verse: ... the Amen ...
paras: The word "Amen" solemnly confirms what has been spoken; and Jesus is the great Confirmer. Unchanging and eternal, He is "the Amen" in all His promises. To the seeking sinner, take comfort in this truth: Jesus said, "Come to Me, all you who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest." If you come to Him, He will speak His "Amen" into your soul, and His promise will prove faithful to you. During His earthly ministry He declared, "A bruised reed He will not break." O troubled and brokenhearted seeker, if you come to Him, He will speak His "Amen" to you as well; and it will be as true in your heart as it has been in countless lives through generations past. Believer, is it not deeply comforting to know that not a single word from our Savior's lips has ever been retracted? The words of Jesus will remain steadfast when heaven and earth have passed away. If you grasp even half a promise, you will find it unfailingly true. Beware of that doubt which acts like a coin clipper, trimming away the edges of God's promises and robbing your soul of comfort.

Jesus is "Yes" and "Amen" in all His offices. He served as Priest to pardon and cleanse in the past, and He remains the "Amen" Priest today. He was King to rule and reign for His people and defend them with His mighty arm, and He is the "Amen" King forever unchanged. He was a Prophet of old to reveal good things to come, and His lips are sweet, overflowing with divine truth—He is the "Amen" Prophet. He is the "Amen" in the enduring value of His blood; He is the "Amen" in the perfection of His righteousness. That sacred robe will remain radiant and glorious when creation itself fades away. He is the "Amen" in every title He bears: your Husband, Who never seeks a divorce; your Friend, Who sticks closer than a brother; your Shepherd, Who walks with you through the valley of the shadow of death; your Help and your Deliverer; your Fortress and your High Tower; the Horn of your salvation, your confidence, your joy, your all in all, and your "Yes" and "Amen" in every season.

m.verse: ... so that by His death He might destroy him who holds the power of death ...
paras: Child of God, death has lost its sting, because the devil's power over it has been destroyed. Therefore, do not fear dying. Ask grace from God the Holy Spirit, that through an intimate knowledge and firm conviction of your Redeemer's death, you may be strengthened for that solemn hour. By living near the cross of Calvary, you can contemplate death with peace and welcome it with quiet joy when it arrives. It is sweet to die in the Lord; it is a covenant blessing to fall asleep in Jesus. Death is no longer an exile; it is a homecoming to the many mansions where our loved ones already dwell. The distance between glorified saints in heaven and struggling believers on earth may seem vast, but it is not. We are not far from home; a single moment will bring us there. The sail is spread; the soul is launched upon the deep waters. How long will the crossing take? How many wearying winds must beat against the sail before it is furled in the harbor of peace? How long must the soul be tossed upon the waves before it reaches the sea that knows no storm? Listen to the answer: "Away from the body and at home with the Lord." That ship has only just departed, yet it has already reached its haven! It barely spread its sails before it arrived. Like that boat of old on the Sea of Galilee, tossed by the storm until Jesus spoke, "Peace, be still!" and immediately it arrived at the shore. Do not imagine that a long expanse of time lies between the moment of death and the fullness of eternal glory. When eyes close on earth, they instantly open in heaven. The chariots and horses of fire do not linger on the road. What is there left for you to fear in death, child of God, since through the death of your Lord its curse and sting have been destroyed? Death has become a Jacob's ladder whose foot rests in the grave, while its top reaches straight into everlasting glory.

e.verse: ... fight the LORD’s battles.
paras: The chosen people of God are actively engaged in spiritual warfare on earth, with Jesus Christ as the Captain of their salvation. He has promised, "I am with you always, even to the end of the age." Listen to the shouts of battle! Let God's people stand firm in their ranks, and let no one's heart falter. It is true that the battle often appears to turn against us in our day, and unless the Lord Jesus wields His sword, we might wonder what will become of the church; yet let us take courage and stand firm like valiant soldiers. There has rarely been a time when the truth of the gospel seemed to hang more precariously in the balance, as relentless efforts seek to re-establish religious error and spiritual tyranny. We urgently need bold voices and strong hands to proclaim the timeless gospel for which martyrs bled and faithful confessors gave their lives. The Savior is present on earth by His Spirit; let this encourage our hearts! He stands in the very thick of the conflict, and therefore the outcome of the battle is never in doubt. While the conflict rages, what profound reassurance it gives to know that the Lord Jesus, serving as our great Intercessor, is pleading with prevailing power for His people! Anxious observer, do not fix your eyes only on the battlefield below, where you will be enveloped in blinding smoke and overwhelmed by garments rolled in blood. Lift your eyes upward to heaven where the Savior lives and pleads! For as long as He intercedes, the cause of God is secure. Let us fight with all our might as if everything depended upon our faithfulness, yet look up in faith, knowing that ultimate victory depends entirely upon Him.

Now, by the purity of Christian holiness, by the precious blood of the Savior's sacrifice, and by every sacred bond of love, we urge you who love Jesus: stand valiantly in this spiritual struggle for truth and righteousness, and for the honor and kingdom of your Lord! Move forward with courage, "for the battle is not yours, but God’s!"

m.verse: ... I know that my Redeemer lives ...
paras: The heart of Job's comfort lies in that personal word "my"—"my Redeemer"—and in the fact that the Redeemer lives. Oh, to lay hold of a living Christ! We must possess a personal claim in Him before we can truly enjoy Him. What is gold in the mine to me? Men are beggars in Peru, and beg for bread in California; it is the gold in my own purse that satisfies my needs by purchasing the bread I require. In the same way, of what value is a Redeemer who does not redeem me, or an avenger who will never stand up for my blood? Do not rest content until by faith you can say, "Yes, I cast myself upon my living Lord, and He is mine." You may hold Him with a trembling hand, half fearing it is presumption to say, "He lives as my Redeemer"; yet remember that if you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, that little faith entitles you to say it. Another word here expresses Job's strong confidence: "I know." To say, "I hope so" or "I trust so" brings comfort, and thousands in the fold of Jesus rarely get much further. But to reach the essence of consolation, you must say, "I know." "Ifs," "buts," and "maybes" are sure murderers of peace and comfort. Doubts are dreary things in times of sorrow—like wasps, they sting the soul! If I suspect that Christ is not mine, then vinegar is mingled with the gall of death; but if I know that Jesus lives for me, darkness is not dark, and even the night is light around me. Surely if Job, in those ancient ages before the coming of Christ, could say, "I know," we should speak with no less assurance. God forbid that our assurance should be presumption! Let us see that our evidences are sound, lest we build upon an ungrounded hope; yet let us not be satisfied with the mere foundation, for it is from the upper rooms that we get the widest view. A living Redeemer, truly mine, is joy unspeakable!

e.verse: ... is at the right hand of God ...
paras: He Who was once despised and rejected by men now occupies the exalted position of a beloved and honored Son. The right hand of God is the place of supreme majesty and favor. Our Lord Jesus is His people's representative. When He died for them, they received rest; when He rose again for them, they received liberty; and when He sat down at His Father's right hand, they were crowned with favor, honor, and dignity. The resurrection and exaltation of Christ is the elevation, the acceptance, and the eternal glorification of all His people, for He is their Head and Representative. His session at the right hand of God, then, represents the Father's full acceptance of our divine Surety, the welcoming of our Representative, and therefore the eternal acceptance of our own souls. Believer, see in this your complete deliverance from condemnation! "Who is there to condemn us?" Who can ever condemn those who are united to Jesus at the right hand of God?

The right hand is the place of power. Christ at the right hand of God possesses all authority in heaven and on earth. Who can prevail against a people whose Captain wields such sovereign might? O my soul, what can ever destroy you if Omnipotence is your helper? If the shield of the Almighty covers you, what weapon can harm you? Rest in complete security! If Jesus is your all-victorious King Who has crushed your enemies beneath His feet—if sin, death, and hell are all vanquished by Him, and you are represented in Him—it is impossible for you to be destroyed.

Jesus' tremendous name
Puts all our foes to flight:
Jesus, the meek, the angry Lamb,
A Lion in the fight.

By all hell's host withstood,
We all hell's host overthrow;
And conquering them through Jesus' blood,
We still to conquer go.

m.verse: God exalted Him ...
paras: Jesus, our Lord, once crucified, dead, and buried, now sits upon the throne of glory. The highest place that heaven can offer is His by undisputed right. It is sweet to remember that the exaltation of Christ in heaven is a representative exaltation. He is exalted at the Father's right hand; and though as God He possesses transcendent glories in which finite creatures cannot share, yet as our Mediator, the honors Jesus wears in heaven are the shared heritage of all His saints. How delightful it is to reflect upon the intimate union between Christ and His people! We are truly one with Him—members of His body—and His exaltation is our own. He will grant us to sit with Him on His throne, just as He overcame and sat down with His Father on His throne. He wears a crown, and He gives crowns to us as well; He possesses a throne, yet He is not content to occupy it alone: at His right hand stands His queen, adorned in the finest gold of Ophir. He will not be glorified without His bride! Look up to Jesus now, believer; let the eye of faith behold Him with many crowns upon His head, and remember that one day you will be like Him, for you will see Him as He is. You will not be infinite as He is, nor divine as He is, yet in your measure you will share the very same honors, and enjoy the same happiness and dignity that He possesses. Be content, then, to remain unknown for a little while, and to walk your path through the valleys of poverty or over the hills of affliction; for soon you will reign with Christ, for He has made us to be a kingdom and priests to God, and we will reign with Him forever. What a magnificent hope for the children of God! We have Christ as our glorious representative in the courts of heaven today, and soon He will return to receive us to Himself, that where He is, we may be also, beholding His glory and sharing His everlasting joy.

e.verse: You will not fear the terror of the night ...
paras: What is this terror? It may be the alarm of fire, the stealthy approach of thieves, imagined fears, or the sudden onset of illness and death. We live in a world of mortality and grief; therefore, we must expect troubles during the quiet watches of the night just as beneath the blazing heat of the noon sun. Yet this should never cause us to panic; for whatever the terror may be, God's promise is that the believer will not be afraid. Why should he? Or to make it personal: why should we? God our Father is with us, and He will remain near throughout every lonely hour. He is an almighty Watcher, a sleepless Guardian, and a faithful Friend. Nothing can happen apart from His sovereign direction, for even the powers of darkness are under His control. Darkness is never dark to Him. He has promised to be a wall of fire around His people, and who can break through such a divine defense? Worldly people may well be terrified, for they have an offended God above them, an accusing conscience within them, and a looming judgment beneath them; but we who rest in Jesus are delivered from all these through His abounding mercy. If we surrender to anxiety, we dishonor our Christian testimony and cause others to doubt the reality of living faith. We ought rather to be afraid of fear itself, lest we grieve the Holy Spirit through unbelief. Away, then, with dismal forebodings and groundless anxieties! God has not forgotten to be gracious, nor has He withheld His tender mercies. Night may settle upon your soul, but you need not be terrified, for the God of love never changes. Children of light may walk through darkness, but they are never abandoned; instead, they are given an opportunity to prove their true sonship by trusting their heavenly Father as no hypocrite ever could.

Though the night be dark and dreary,
Darkness cannot hide from Thee;
Thou art He, Who, never weary,
Watchest where Thy people be.

m.verse: No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us.
paras: We go to Christ for forgiveness, and then too often turn to the law for power to overcome our sins. Paul sternly rebukes this error: "You foolish Galatians! Who has bewitched you? ... I would like to learn just one thing from you: Did you receive the Spirit by works of the law, or by hearing with faith? Are you so foolish? After beginning by the Spirit, are you now being perfected by the flesh?" Take your sins to the cross of Christ, for our old self can only be put to death there; we were crucified with Him. The most effective weapon against sin is the spear that pierced the side of Jesus. For example, if you want to conquer an angry temper, how do you set about it? It is quite possible that you have never tried the true remedy of taking it directly to Jesus. How did I receive salvation? I came to Jesus just as I was, and I trusted Him to save me. I must put my angry temper to death in exactly the same way; indeed, it is the only way I can ever overcome it. I must bring it to the cross and cry to Jesus, "Lord, I trust You to deliver me from it!" That is the only way to strike its deathblow. Are you struggling with greed? Do you feel the world entangling you? You may wrestle against this evil as long as you like, but if it is your besetting sin, you will never find deliverance except through the blood of Jesus. Take it straight to Christ. Tell Him, "Lord, I have trusted You, and Your name is Jesus, for You save Your people from their sins. Lord, this is one of my sins—save me from it!" Outward religious practices are useless without Christ as a means of putting sin to death. Your prayers, your tears of repentance, and your resolutions—all taken together—are powerless apart from Him. "None but Jesus can do helpless sinners good"—nor helpless saints either! If you are to be a conqueror at all, you must be more than a conqueror through Him Who loved you. The laurels of our victory must grow among His olive trees in Gethsemane.

e.verse: ... a Lamb who appeared to have been slain, standing in the center of the throne ...
paras: Why should our exalted Lord appear in His wounds in glory? The wounds of Jesus are His glories, His jewels, His sacred ornaments. To the eye of faith, Jesus is supremely beautiful because He is "dazzling and ruddy"—white in His sinless innocence, and ruddy with His own precious blood. We see Him as the lily of matchless purity, and as the rose stained crimson with His own blood. Christ is lovely upon the Mount of Olives, upon Mount Tabor, and beside the Sea of Galilee; but never was Christ so gloriously beautiful as when He hung upon the cross! There we beheld all His perfections displayed, all His divine attributes revealed, all His love poured out, and all His character unveiled. Beloved, the wounds of Jesus are far more precious in our eyes than all the splendor and pomp of earthly monarchs. His crown of thorns outshines every imperial diadem. It is true that He no longer holds the mock scepter of reed, yet there was a divine glory in it that never shone from a scepter of gold. Jesus wears the likeness of a slain Lamb as the royal vesture in which He won our hearts and redeemed us by His finished atonement. Nor are these scars merely the ornaments of Christ; they are the glorious trophies of His love and victory. He has divided the spoils with the strong; He has redeemed for Himself a vast multitude that no one can number; and these scars are the everlasting memorials of the battle. If Christ delights to keep the marks of His sufferings for His people, how infinitely precious His wounds should be to us!

Behold how every wound of His
A precious balm distills,
Which heals the scars that sin had made,
And cures all mortal ills.

Those wounds are mouths that preach His grace;
The ensigns of His love;
The seals of our expected bliss
In paradise above.

m.verse: In view of all this, we make a binding agreement ...
paras: There are many occasions in our Christian walk when we may rightly and profitably renew our covenant with God. After recovering from serious illness when, like King Hezekiah, we have received a fresh grant of life, it is most fitting to do so. After any great deliverance from trouble, when joy blooms anew, let us return to the foot of the cross and renew our consecration. Above all, let us do this whenever we have fallen into some sin that has grieved the Holy Spirit or brought dishonor upon the cause of Christ; let us look once more to that cleansing blood which makes us whiter than snow, and present ourselves anew to the Lord. We should not only allow our afflictions to deepen our dedication to God, but our prosperity should do the same. Whenever we experience what may truly be called "crowning mercies," surely if He has crowned us with lovingkindness, we ought in return to crown our God! Let us bring forth all the jewels of praise stored within the treasury of our hearts, and enthrone our God upon our deepest love, clothed in royal honor. If we would learn to profit from our blessings, we would not require so much adversity; if we received from God's gentle embraces all the good they are intended to convey, we would not so frequently suffer under the rod of discipline. Have you recently received some unexpected blessing? Has the Lord set your feet in a spacious place? Can you sing of multiplied mercies? Then today is the day to lay your hand upon the horns of the altar and pray, "Bind me here, my God; bind me to Your altar with cords of love forever!" Since we continually need the fulfillment of fresh promises from God, let us offer earnest prayers that our past vows may never be dishonored. Let us make a solemn and binding agreement with Him this morning, drawn by the suffering love of Jesus which we have contemplated with overflowing gratitude.

e.verse: The flowers have appeared in the countryside; the season of singing has come, and the cooing of turtledoves is heard in our land.
paras: How sweet is the season of spring! The long, bleak winter helps us appreciate its gentle warmth, and the bright promise of summer heightens its present joys. After seasons of spiritual depression, it is delightful to behold once more the light of the Sun of Righteousness. Then our slumbering graces awaken from their lethargy, like the crocus and the daffodil rising from the earth; our hearts overflow with joyful notes of thanksgiving, far sweeter than the singing of birds; and the comforting assurance of peace, infinitely more delightful than the cooing of the turtledove, echoes within the soul. Now is the time for the believer to seek intimate communion with her Beloved; now she must rise above earthly distractions and leave behind the entanglements of the world. If we fail to hoist the sail when the heavenly breeze is favorable, we are deeply at fault; times of spiritual refreshing should never pass us by unheeded. When Jesus Himself draws near in tender love and bids us arise, how could we ever be so ungrateful as to turn Him away? He has risen so that He might draw us upward to Himself; and by His Holy Spirit He revives our hearts so that we may walk in newness of life, ascend into heavenly places, and abide in fellowship with Him. Let the past winter suffice for our coldness and spiritual indifference; now that the Lord creates a springtime within, let fresh spiritual life surge through our souls, bearing abundant fruit for His glory. O Lord, if it is not yet springtime in my cold heart, I pray that You will make it so, for I am utterly weary of living at a distance from You. Oh, this long and barren winter—when will You bring it to an end? Come, Holy Spirit, and renew my soul! Revive me, restore me, and have mercy upon me! This very night I earnestly plead that the Lord would look with favor upon His servant and send a gracious revival of life and joy into my soul!

m.verse: ... Arise, my darling. Come away with me, my beautiful one.
paras: Listen! I hear the voice of my Beloved! He speaks to me! Pleasant weather smiles upon the earth, and He would not have me slumber spiritually while all around me nature awakens from its winter rest. He calls to me, "Arise!"—and well He may, for I have lingered far too long among the rubbish heaps of worldliness. He is risen, and I am risen with Him; why then should I cling to the dust? Above all earthly loves, desires, pursuits, and ambitions, I long to rise toward Him. He calls me by the tender name of "My darling," and considers me beautiful; this is a compelling reason for me to arise! If He has so highly exalted me and delights in my beauty, how can I linger among the tents of worldly darkness, seeking fellowship with those who do not know God? He bids me, "Come away." Further and further from everything selfish, degrading, worldly, and sinful, He summons me. Yes, even from that external, formal religious world that does not know Him and has no heart for the deeper life of the Spirit, He calls me. "Come away" has no harsh sound to my ears, for what is there to hold me in this wilderness of empty vanity and sin? O my Lord, how I long to come away! Yet I find myself caught among the thorns of life, unable to break free as I desire. If it were possible, I would have neither eyes, nor ears, nor heart for sin. You call me to Yourself, saying, "Come away"—and what a sweet, melodious invitation it is! To come to You is to return home from exile; it is to step onto dry land out of a raging tempest; it is to enter into rest after weary striving; it is to reach the fulfillment of my deepest longings. Yet Lord, how can a stone rise? How can a lump of clay climb out of the miry pit? Raise me up; draw me close! Your grace alone can do it. Send forth Your Holy Spirit to kindle the sacred fire of love within my soul, and I will continue to rise until I leave earth and time behind, and truly come away to You!

e.verse: ... If anyone hears My voice and opens the door, I will come in ...
paras: What is your desire this evening? Is your heart set upon heavenly things? Do you long to experience the profound depths of God's eternal love? Do you desire true freedom in intimate communion with Him? Do you aspire to grasp the width and length and height and depth of Christ's love? Then you must draw near to Jesus; you must obtain a clear vision of Him in all His preciousness and all-sufficiency. You must behold Him in His finished work, in His divine offices, and in His glorious person. Whoever truly understands Christ receives an anointing from the Holy One, by which he knows the truth. Christ is the great Master Key to all the treasury of God; there is no storehouse of divine blessing that will not unlock and reveal its riches to the soul that lives in close fellowship with Jesus. Are you crying out, "Oh, that He would dwell within my heart! If only He would make my soul His dwelling place forever!"? Open the door, beloved, and He will enter in. He has been knocking persistently, with this gracious purpose: that He may dine with you, and you with Him. He dines with you because you provide the home of a welcoming heart, and you dine with Him because He provides the feast! He could not dine with you unless your heart is opened to receive Him; nor could you dine with Him—for you possess only an empty cupboard—unless He brought the heavenly banquet with Him. Throw wide open the doors of your soul! He will enter with that divine love you yearn to feel; He will bring that supernatural joy which your downcast spirit could never produce on its own; He will grant that deep peace which you currently lack. He will refresh you with the sweet fruit of His grace and comfort your soul with the richness of His presence. Only open the door to Him, cast out His enemies, give Him the keys to every chamber of your heart, and He will dwell there forever. What wondrous love, that brings such a glorious Guest to dwell in such a humble home!

m.verse: ... do this in remembrance of Me.
paras: It seems, then, that Christians can actually forget Christ! There would be no need for this tender command if there were not a grave danger that our memories might prove treacherous. Nor is this a mere theory; it is, alas, confirmed by our daily experience—not as a remote possibility, but as a sorrowful reality. It seems almost inconceivable that those who have been redeemed by the blood of the dying Lamb, and loved with an everlasting love by the eternal Son of God, should ever forget that gracious Savior. Yet however startling it may sound, our lives make it far too obvious to deny. Forget Him Who never forgot us! Forget Him Who poured out His blood for our sins! Forget Him Who loved us even to death! Can it really be possible? Yes, it is not only possible, but conscience compels us to confess that it is the tragic fault of every one of us: we treat Him like a traveler lodging only for a night. He Whom we ought to make the permanent resident of our thoughts is treated as nothing more than an occasional visitor. The cross, where memory should continually linger and neglect should never enter, is trampled by the feet of our forgetfulness. Does not your own conscience convict you of this truth? Do you not find yourself prone to forget Jesus? Some earthly pursuit steals away your heart, and you become careless toward Him on Whom your supreme affection should be set. Some passing business absorbs your attention when you should be fixing your eyes steadily upon the cross. The relentless clamor of the world and the magnetic pull of temporal things draw the soul away from Christ. While our memory carefully preserves the poisonous weeds of worldliness, it allows the Rose of Sharon to wither! Let us charge our souls to bind a heavenly remembrance around our hearts for Jesus our Beloved; and whatever else we allow to slip away, let us hold fast to Him!

e.verse: ... Blessed is the one who remains awake ...
paras: "I die daily," declared the apostle. Such was the daily experience of the early Christians; they lived constantly with their lives in their hands. We are not called in our day to endure the same violent persecutions; if we were, the Lord would supply abundant grace to withstand the trial. Yet the spiritual dangers of our present time, though outwardly less terrifying, are perhaps even more likely to overcome us than the fiery trials of the past. We may have to endure the world's sneer—that is a small matter; but its subtle flatteries, its deceitful promises, its seductive charms, and its hypocrisy are far more dangerous. Our peril is that we may grow prosperous and proud, conform to the patterns of this present evil world, and abandon our faith. Or if wealth is not our temptation, the anxieties of life can be equally destructive. Whether we are torn apart by a roaring lion or smothered in the deadly embrace of a bear, the enemy cares little, so long as he destroys our love for Christ and our trust in Him. I fear that the church of God is in far greater danger of losing its integrity in these comfortable, easy days than in times of fierce opposition. We must stay alert, for we are walking across the enchanted ground of spiritual slumber, where we are prone to fall asleep to our own ruin unless our faith in Jesus is genuine and our love for Him burns as a vehement flame. Many in an age of casual profession will prove to be weeds rather than wheat—counterfeits wearing religious masks, but not true-born children of the living God. Believer, never imagine that these are days when you can lay aside spiritual vigilance or holy fervor! You need them now more than ever. May God the eternal Spirit display His almighty power within you, so that amid seductive comforts just as through fierce trials, you may triumphantly declare, "We are more than conquerors through Him Who loved us!"

m.verse: ... God, our God, blesses us.
paras: It is strange how little use we make of the spiritual blessings God gives us, but stranger still how little use we make of God Himself. Though He is "our own God," we turn so seldom to Him and ask so little of Him. How rarely do we seek counsel from the Lord! How often do we pursue our daily business without seeking His guidance! In our troubles, how constantly we struggle to bear our burdens alone, instead of casting them upon the Lord so that He may sustain us! It is not because we are forbidden to do so, for the Lord seems to say: "I am yours, believer; come and draw from Me as you will. You may freely come to My store, and the more often you come, the more welcome you are." It is our own fault if we do not partake freely of the riches of our God. Since you have such a Friend, and He invites you, draw from Him daily! Never live in want while you have a God to go to; never fear or faint while you have God to help you. Go to your treasure and take whatever you need—everything you could ever want is there. Learn the divine skill of making God all things to you. He can supply you with all, or better still, He can be everything to you in place of all else. Let me urge you, then, to lean upon your God. Come to Him continually in prayer. Go to Him often, because He is your God. Will you neglect so priceless a privilege? Run to Him and tell Him all your needs. Trust Him continually by faith at all times. If some dark trial has overshadowed your path, look to your God as a "sun"; if some powerful enemy has confronted you, find in the LORD a "shield," for He is a sun and shield to His people. If you have lost your way in the confusing paths of life, look to Him as your "guide," for He will direct your steps. Whatever you are and wherever you may be, remember that God is just what you need, just where you need Him, and able to do all you require!

e.verse: The LORD is King forever and ever ...
paras: Jesus Christ is no despotic tyrant claiming arbitrary power, but He is truly and rightfully the Lord's Anointed! "For God was pleased to have all His fullness dwell in Him." The Father has given Him all power and all authority. As the exalted Son of Man, He is now Head over all things for the church; and He reigns over heaven, earth, and the realm of the dead, bearing the keys of death and Hades at His side. Certain earthly rulers have proudly styled themselves kings by the popular will, and our Lord Jesus Christ is truly King by the joyful consent of His church. If it could be put to a vote whether He should reign over us, every believing heart would enthusiastically crown Him! Oh, that we could crown Him far more gloriously than we do! We would count no sacrifice too great if it brought glory to Christ; suffering would become our joy, and loss our greatest gain, if by it we could place brighter crowns upon His brow and display His glory before angels and men. Yes, He shall reign! Long live the King! All hail to You, King Jesus! Go forth, all you faithful souls who love your Lord; bow at His feet, and strew His pathway with the lilies of your love and the roses of your thanksgiving: "Bring forth the royal diadem, and crown Him Lord of all!" Furthermore, our Lord Jesus is King in Zion by right of conquest: He has won the hearts of His people, vanquishing the spiritual foes that once held us in cruel slavery. In the Red Sea of His own blood, our Redeemer has drowned the Pharaoh of our sins—shall He not be King in Jeshurun? He has delivered us from the iron yoke and crushing curse of the law—shall not our great Deliverer be crowned? We are His treasured inheritance, which He took from the enemy with His sword and His bow; who can ever snatch His conquered people from His hand? All hail, King Jesus! We joyfully submit to Your gracious rule! Reign in our hearts forever, You glorious Prince of Peace!

m.verse: Remember Your word to Your servant, upon which You have given me hope.
paras: Whatever your specific need may be, you will readily find a promise in the Scriptures suited to meet it. Are you faint and weary because your path is rough? Here is the promise: "He gives power to the faint, and increases the strength of the weak." When you read such an assurance, bring it directly back to the great Promiser, and ask Him to fulfill His own word. Are you seeking after Christ and thirsting for deeper communion with Him? This promise shines upon you like a star: "Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be filled." Take that promise continually to the throne of grace; plead nothing else, but go to God repeatedly with this plea: "Lord, You have promised it; now do as You have said!" Are you distressed over your sin and weighed down beneath the heavy burden of your guilt? Listen to these comforting words: "I, yes I, am He who blots out your transgressions for My own sake, and remembers your sins no more." You have no merit of your own to present for pardon, but plead His written promises and He will faithfully perform them. Are you terrified that you may not persevere to the end—fearing that, after professing to be a child of God, you might ultimately fall away? If so, carry this word of grace to the throne and plead it: "Though the mountains may be removed and the hills may shake, My loving devotion will not depart from you, nor My covenant of peace be disturbed." If you have lost the sweet assurance of your Savior's presence and seek Him with a sorrowful heart, remember His steadfast word: "Return to Me, and I will return to you"; and again, "For a brief moment I forsook you, but with great compassion I will bring you back." Feast your faith upon God's infallible Word! Whatever your fears or necessities, come boldly to the treasury of grace with your Father's signed promissory note, praying: "Remember Your word to Your servant, upon which You have given me hope!"

e.verse: ... the whole house of Israel is hard-headed and hard-hearted.
paras: Are there no exceptions? No, not one. Even God's chosen people are described in these terms. If the best are so corrupt, what must the worst be? Come, my heart, examine how far you share in this universal indictment; and as you reflect, be ready to take shame to yourself wherever you have been guilty. The first charge is obstinacy, or a hardened forehead—a complete lack of holy shame, and a reckless boldness in doing evil. Before my conversion, I could sin without remorse, hear of my guilt and remain completely unhumbled, and even confess my iniquity without feeling genuine brokenness of heart. For a sinner to enter God's house and pretend to worship and pray to Him reveals a brazen defiance of the worst kind! Alas, even since the day of my new birth, I have doubted my Lord to His face, complained openly in His presence, worshiped Him in a careless manner, and sinned without grieving over my offense. If my heart were not as hard as flint, I would possess far more reverent fear and a much deeper contrition of spirit. Woe is me, for I too have shared in the stubbornness of Israel! The second charge is hardheartedness, and I dare not claim innocence here. Once I possessed only a heart of stone; and though by grace I now have a new and tender heart of flesh, much of my former stubbornness still remains. I am not moved by the death of Jesus as I ought to be; nor am I stirred as I should be by the ruin of my fellow men, the wickedness of our times, the loving chastening of my heavenly Father, and my own frequent failures. Oh, that my heart would melt at the remembrance of my Savior's sufferings and cross! How I long to be completely delivered from this stubborn stone within me, this body of death! Yet blessed be the name of the Lord, this spiritual disease is not incurable! The Savior's precious blood is the sovereign cure; and it will powerfully soften even my stubborn soul, until my heart melts like wax before the holy fire of His love.

m.verse: ... You are my refuge in the day of disaster.
paras: The path of the Christian is not always bright with sunshine; he has his seasons of darkness and storm. It is true that God's Word declares, "Her ways are pleasant ways, and all her paths are peace"; and it is a great truth that true religion is meant to give us happiness on earth as well as bliss in heaven. Yet experience teaches us that even though the path of the righteous is "like the light of dawn, shining brighter and brighter until the full day," that light is sometimes eclipsed. At times, clouds cover the believer's sun, and he walks in darkness, seeing no light. Many have rejoiced in the presence of God for a season; they basked in the sunshine during the earlier stages of their Christian walk; they walked in green pastures beside quiet waters. But suddenly the glorious sky becomes clouded; instead of the fertile land of Goshen, they must tread the sandy desert; and in place of sweet waters, they find troubled streams, bitter to their taste, and they say, "Surely, if I were a child of God, this would not happen to me!" Oh, do not say so, you who now walk in darkness! The best of God's saints must drink the bitter wormwood; the dearest of His children must bear the cross. No Christian has enjoyed unbroken prosperity; no believer can always keep his harp from hanging on the willows. Perhaps the Lord gave you a smooth and unclouded path at first because you were weak and timid. He tempered the wind to the shorn lamb; but now that you are stronger in the spiritual life, you must enter into the deeper and rougher experiences of God's mature children. We need winds and tempests to exercise our faith, to tear off the rotten branch of self-reliance, and to root us more firmly in Christ. The day of evil reveals to us the value of our glorious hope!

e.verse: For the LORD takes pleasure in His people ...
paras: How vast and all-embracing is the love of Jesus! There is no part of His people's interests that He does not consider, and there is nothing concerning their welfare that is not important to Him. He does not think of you, believer, merely as an immortal being, but as a mortal being as well. Do not deny it or doubt it: "Even the very hairs of your head are all numbered"; and "The steps of a man are ordered by the LORD who takes delight in his journey." It would be a sad thing for us if this mantle of love did not cover all our concerns; for what harm might overtake us in any part of our lives that did not come under our gracious Lord's watchful eye! Believer, rest assured that the heart of Jesus cares about your smallest everyday affairs. The breadth of His tender love is so vast that you may turn to Him in all matters; for in all your affliction He is afflicted, and just as a father has compassion on his children, so the Lord has compassion on you. The humblest concerns of all His saints are carried upon the broad bosom of the Son of God. Oh, what a heart is His, that does not merely embrace the persons of His people, but encompasses all the diverse and countless concerns of their lives! Do you think, O Christian, that you can measure the love of Christ? Think of what His love has brought you—justification, adoption, sanctification, and eternal life! The riches of His goodness are unsearchable; you will never be able to fully recount them or even conceive them. Oh, the breadth of the love of Christ! Shall such a love as this have only half our hearts? Shall it be met with cold love in return? Shall the marvelous lovingkindness and tender care of Jesus meet with only a faint response and delayed gratitude? O my soul, tune your harp to a glad song of thanksgiving! Go to your rest rejoicing, for you are no desolate wanderer, but a beloved child—watched over, cared for, provided for, and defended by your Lord!

m.verse: ... All the Israelites grumbled ...
paras: There are grumblers among Christians today, just as there were in the camp of Israel of old. There are those who, when the rod falls, cry out against the painful trial. They ask, "Why am I afflicted like this? What have I done to be disciplined in this way?" A word with you, complainer! Why should you grumble against the providences of your heavenly Father? Can He treat you more harshly than you deserve? Remember what a rebel you once were, yet He has pardoned you! Surely, if in His wisdom He now sees fit to discipline you, you should not complain. After all, are you struck as hard as your sins deserve? Consider the corruption that is in your heart; will you then wonder that it takes so much of the rod to drive it out? Weigh yourself, and see how much dross is mixed with your gold; do you think the fire is too hot to purge away all that dross? Does not that proud, rebellious spirit of yours prove that your heart is not thoroughly sanctified? Are not those grumbling words contrary to the holy, submissive character of God's children? Is not this correction needed? But if you grumble against this discipline, take heed, for it will go hard with grumblers. God always disciplines His children twice if they do not bear the first stroke patiently. But know this one thing: "He does not afflict from His heart, nor grieve the children of men." All His corrections are sent in love, to purify you and to draw you nearer to Himself. Surely it must help you bear this discipline with submission if you are able to recognize your Father's hand. For "the Lord disciplines the one He loves, and He chastises everyone He accepts as a son. Endure suffering as discipline; God is treating you as sons." Therefore, "do not grumble, as some of them did—and were killed by the destroying angel."

e.verse: How precious to me are Your thoughts, O God ...
paras: Divine omniscience brings no comfort to an ungodly mind, but to the child of God it overflows with consolation. God is always thinking upon us, never turning His mind away from us, and keeping us continually before His eyes. This is precisely as we would desire it, for it would be dreadful to exist for even a moment beyond the watchful eye of our heavenly Father. His thoughts toward us are always tender, loving, wise, and purposeful, bringing us countless blessings; therefore, it is a choice delight to remember them. The Lord has always thought upon His people—from this eternal love springs their election and the covenant of grace by which their salvation is secured. He will always think upon them—from this unfailing care flows their final perseverance, ensuring they will be brought safely to their eternal rest. In all our wanderings, the watchful glance of the Eternal Watcher is continually fixed upon us; we never roam beyond the Shepherd's eye. In our sorrows, He observes us constantly, and not a single pang escapes Him; in all our daily toil, He marks our weariness and writes in His book all the struggles of His faithful ones. These thoughts of the Lord encompass us in all our paths and penetrate the innermost parts of our being. Not a nerve or tissue, valve or vessel of our bodily frame is uncared for; every small detail of our little world is thought upon by the great God!

Dear reader, is this precious to you? Then hold fast to it! Never be led astray by those philosophic fools who preach an impersonal God and talk of self-existent, self-governing matter. The Lord lives and thinks upon us—this truth is far too precious for us to be easily robbed of it. The favor of an earthly nobleman is prized so highly that whoever receives it considers his fortune made; but what is it to be thought of by the King of kings! If the Lord thinks upon us, all is well, and we may rejoice always!

m.verse: His cheeks are like beds of spice, towers of perfume...
paras: Look, the month of flowers has come! March winds and April showers have done their work, and the earth is completely adorned with beauty. Come, my soul, put on your holiday attire and go out to gather garlands of heavenly thoughts. You know where to direct your steps, for to you the "beds of spice" are well known, and you have so often smelled the fragrance of the "towers of perfume," that you will go at once to your Well-Beloved and find all loveliness and all joy in Him. That cheek once so rudely struck with a rod, often wet with tears of sympathy, and then defiled with spitting—that cheek, as it smiles with mercy, is like a fragrant aroma to my heart. You did not hide Your face from shame and spitting, O Lord Jesus, and therefore I will find my deepest delight in praising You. Those cheeks were furrowed by the plow of grief, and crimsoned with red lines of blood from Your thorn-crowned temples; such marks of boundless love cannot fail to charm my soul far more than "towers of perfume." If I may not see the whole of His face, I would behold His cheeks, for the least glimpse of Him is exceedingly refreshing to my spiritual senses and brings a variety of delights. In Jesus I find not only fragrance, but a bed of spices; not merely one flower, but all kinds of sweet flowers. He is to me my rose and my lily, my heart's-ease and my cluster of henna blossoms. When He is with me, it is May all the year round, and my soul goes out to wash her happy face in the morning dew of His grace, and to comfort herself with the singing of the birds of His promises. Precious Lord Jesus, let me truly know the blessedness that dwells in abiding, unbroken fellowship with You. I am a poor, worthless one whose cheek You have deigned to kiss! Oh, let me kiss You in return with the kisses of my lips.

e.verse: I am a rose of Sharon...
paras: Whatever beauty there may be in the material world, Jesus Christ possesses all of it in the spiritual realm to a tenfold degree. Among flowers the rose is considered the sweetest, but Jesus is infinitely more beautiful in the garden of the soul than the rose can ever be in the gardens of earth. He takes the first place as the most outstanding among ten thousand. He is the sun, and all others are the stars; the heavens and the day are dark in comparison with Him, for the King in His beauty transcends all things. "I am a rose of Sharon." This was the best and rarest of roses. Jesus is not merely "the rose" alone; He is "the rose of Sharon," just as He calls His righteousness "gold," and then adds, "the gold of Ophir"—the very best of the best. He is positively lovely, and superlatively the loveliest. There is variety in His charms. The rose is delightful to the eye, and its scent is pleasant and refreshing; so each of the senses of the soul, whether it be taste or touch, hearing, sight, or spiritual fragrance, finds appropriate gratification in Jesus. Even the recollection of His love is sweet. Take the rose of Sharon, pull it petal from petal, and store the petals in the jar of memory, and you will find each petal fragrant long afterward, filling the house with perfume. Christ satisfies the highest taste of the most cultivated spirit to the very full. The greatest connoisseur of perfumes is completely satisfied with the rose; and when the soul has arrived at her highest summit of true taste, she will still be content with Christ; indeed, she will be all the better able to appreciate Him. Heaven itself possesses nothing that excels the rose of Sharon. What emblem can fully set forth His beauty? Human speech and earth-born things fail to tell of Him. Earth's choicest charms, mingled together, feebly picture His abounding preciousness. Blessed Rose, bloom in my heart forever!

m.verse: I am not asking that You take them out of the world...
paras: It is a sweet and blessed event that will occur to all believers in God's own time—the going home to be with Jesus. In a few more years the Lord's soldiers, who are now fighting "the good fight of faith," will have finished with conflict and will have entered into the joy of their Lord. But although Christ prays that His people may eventually be with Him where He is, He does not ask that they should be taken at once away from this world to heaven. He desires them to remain here. Yet how frequently does the weary pilgrim offer the prayer, "Oh, that I had wings like a dove! For then I would fly away and be at rest"; but Christ does not pray like that. He leaves us in His Father's hands until, like shocks of grain fully ripe, each of us shall be gathered into our Master's barn. Jesus does not plead for our immediate departure by death, for to remain in the body is necessary for others, even if not profitable for ourselves. He asks that we may be kept from the evil one, but He never asks for us to be admitted into the inheritance in glory until we have reached full maturity. Christians often want to die whenever they encounter any trouble. Ask them why, and they will tell you, "Because we want to be with the Lord." We fear it is not so much because they are longing to be with the Lord as because they desire to get rid of their troubles; otherwise they would feel the same wish to die at other times when not under the pressure of trial. They want to go home, not so much for the Savior's company as simply to be at rest. Now it is entirely right to desire to depart if we can do so in the same spirit that Paul did, because to be with Christ is far better; but the wish to escape from trouble is a selfish one. Rather let your care and desire be to glorify God by your life here as long as He pleases, even though it be in the midst of toil, conflict, and suffering, and leave Him to say when "it is enough."

e.verse: All these people died in faith...
paras: Behold the epitaph of all those blessed saints who fell asleep before the coming of our Lord! It matters nothing how else they died, whether of old age or by violent means; this one point, in which they all agree, is the most worthy of record: "All these people died in faith." In faith they lived—it was their comfort, their guide, their motive, and their support; and in the same spiritual grace they died, ending their life-song in the sweet strain in which they had so long continued. They did not die resting in the flesh or upon their own attainments; they made no departure from their first ground of acceptance with God, but held to the way of faith to the end. Faith is as precious to die by as to live by.

Dying in faith has distinct reference to the past. They believed the promises that had gone before, and were assured that their sins were blotted out through the mercy of God. Dying in faith has to do with the present. These saints were confident of their acceptance with God; they enjoyed the beams of His love and rested in His faithfulness. Dying in faith looks into the future. They fell asleep affirming that the Messiah would surely come, and that when He would appear upon the earth in the last days, they would rise from their graves to behold Him. To them the pains of death were only the birth pangs of a better state. Take courage, my soul, as you read this epitaph. Your course, through grace, is one of faith, and sight seldom cheers you; this has also been the pathway of the brightest and the best. Faith was the orbit in which these stars of the first magnitude moved all the time of their shining here; and how happy you are that it is yours! Look anew tonight to Jesus, the author and perfecter of your faith, and thank Him for giving you like precious faith with souls now in glory.

m.verse: ... In the world you will have tribulation...
paras: Are you asking the reason for this, believer? Look upward to your heavenly Father, and behold Him pure and holy. Do you know that you are one day to be like Him? Will you easily be conformed to His image? Will you not require much refining in the furnace of affliction to purify you? Will it be an easy thing to get rid of your corruptions, and make you perfect, even as your Father in heaven is perfect? Next, Christian, turn your eyes downward. Do you know what foes you have beneath your feet? You were once a servant of Satan, and no king willingly loses his subjects. Do you think that Satan will leave you alone? No, he will always be attacking you, for he "prowls around like a roaring lion, seeking someone to devour." Expect trouble, therefore, Christian, whenever you look beneath you. Then look around you. Where are you? You are in an enemy's country, a stranger and a sojourner. The world is not your friend. If it is, then you are not God's friend, for he who is the friend of the world is the enemy of God. Be well assured that you will find foes everywhere. When you sleep, remember that you are resting on the battlefield; when you walk, suspect an ambush in every hedge. As mosquitoes are said to bite strangers more than natives, so will the trials of earth be sharpest to you. Lastly, look within yourself, into your own heart, and observe what is there. Sin and self are still within your own heart. Ah! If you had no devil to tempt you, no enemies to fight you, and no world to ensnare you, you would still find in yourself enough evil to be a sore and heavy trouble to you, for "the heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately sick." Expect trouble then, but do not despair on account of it, for God is with you to help and strengthen you. He has said, "I will be with him in trouble; I will deliver him and honor him."

e.verse: ... an ever-present help...
paras: Covenant blessings are not meant to be looked at only, but to be appropriated. Even our Lord Jesus is given to us for our present use. Believer, you do not make use of Christ as you ought to do. When you are in trouble, why do you not tell Him all your grief? Does He not have a sympathizing heart, and can He not comfort and relieve you? No, you go about to all your friends except your best Friend, telling your tale everywhere except into the bosom of your Lord. Are you burdened with this day's sins? Here is a fountain filled with blood: use it, saint, use it. Has a sense of guilt returned upon you? The pardoning grace of Jesus may be proved again and again. Come to Him at once for cleansing. Do you deplore your weakness? He is your strength; why not lean upon Him? Do you feel naked? Come here, soul; put on the robe of Jesus' righteousness. Do not stand merely looking at it, but wear it. Strip off your own righteousness, and your own fears as well; put on the fine white linen, for it was meant to be worn. Do you feel sick? Ring the night bell of prayer, and call upon the Beloved Physician! He will give the restorative that will revive you. You are poor, but then you have "a kinsman, a man of great wealth." What! Will you not go to Him and ask Him to give you from His abundance, when He has given you this promise, that you will be a joint heir with Him, and has made over all that He is and all that He has to be yours? There is nothing Christ dislikes more than for His people to make an ornament of Him and not use Him. He loves to be employed by us. The more burdens we put on His shoulders, the more precious will He be to us.

Let us be simple with Him, then,
Not backward, stiff, or cold,
As though our Bethlehem could be
What Sinai was of old.

m.verse: Can man make gods for himself? Such are not gods!
paras: One great besetting sin of ancient Israel was idolatry, and spiritual Israel is troubled with a tendency to the same folly. Remphan's star shines no longer, and the women weep no more for Tammuz, but Mammon still intrudes his golden calf, and the shrines of pride are not forsaken. Self in various forms struggles to subdue the chosen ones under its dominion, and the flesh sets up its altars wherever it can find space for them. Favorite children are often the cause of much sin in believers; the Lord is grieved when He sees us doting upon them above measure; they will live to be as great a curse to us as Absalom was to David, or they will be taken from us to leave our homes desolate. If Christians desire to grow thorns to stuff their sleepless pillows, let them dote on their dear ones.

It is truly said that "they are no gods," for the objects of our foolish love are very doubtful blessings; the comfort which they give us now is dangerous, and the help that they can give us in the hour of trouble is little indeed. Why, then, are we so bewitched with vanities? We pity the poor pagans who adore a god of stone, and yet we worship a god of gold. Where is the vast superiority between a god of flesh and one of wood? The principle, the sin, the folly is the same in either case, only that in ours the crime is more aggravated because we have more light, and sin in the face of it. The pagan bows to a false deity, but the true God he has never known; we commit two evils, inasmuch as we forsake the living God and turn to idols. May the Lord purge us all from this grievous iniquity!

The dearest idol I have known,
Whate'er that idol be;
Help me to tear it from Your throne,
And worship only Thee.

e.verse: For you have been born again, not of perishable seed, but of imperishable...
paras: Peter most earnestly exhorted the scattered saints to love each other "deeply, from a pure heart," and he wisely drew his argument, not from the law, from nature, or from philosophy, but from that high and divine nature which God has implanted in His people. Just as some judicious tutor of princes might work to cultivate and foster in them a kingly spirit and dignified conduct, finding arguments in their position and descent, so, looking upon God's people as heirs of glory, princes of royal blood, descendants of the King of kings, earth's truest and oldest aristocracy, Peter says to them, "See that you love one another, because of your noble birth, being born of imperishable seed; because of your pedigree, being descended from God, the Creator of all things; and because of your immortal destiny, for you will never pass away, though the glory of the flesh will fade, and even its existence will cease." It would be well if, in the spirit of humility, we recognized the true dignity of our regenerated nature, and lived up to it. What is a Christian? If you compare him with a king, he adds priestly sanctity to royal dignity. The king's royalty often lies only in his crown, but with a Christian it is infused into his inmost nature. He is as much above his fellows through his new birth as a man is above the beast that perishes. Surely he ought to conduct himself, in all his dealings, as one who is not of the multitude, but chosen out of the world, distinguished by sovereign grace, written among God's own treasured people, who therefore cannot grovel in the dust as others, nor live after the manner of the world's citizens. Let the dignity of your nature, and the brightness of your prospects, O believers in Christ, constrain you to cling to holiness, and to avoid the very appearance of evil.

m.verse: ... I will be their God, and they will be My people.
paras: What a sweet title: "My people!" What a cheering revelation: "Their God!" How much meaning is couched in those two words, "My people!" Here is special distinction.
