Let this be our family rule, and our personal bond—SPEAK EVIL OF NO MAN.

The Holy Spirit, however, permits us to censure sin, and prescribes the way in which we are to do it. It must be done by rebuking our brother to his face, not by railing behind his back. This course is manly, brotherly, Christlike, and under God's blessing will be useful. Does the flesh shrink from it? Then we must lay greater stress upon our conscience, and keep ourselves to the task, lest by allowing sin in our friend we ourselves become partakers in it. Hundreds have been saved from gross sins by the timely, wise, and affectionate warnings of faithful ministers and brothers. Our Lord Jesus has set us a gracious example of how to deal with erring friends in His warning given to Peter, the prayer with which He preceded it, and the gentle way in which He bore with Peter's boastful denial that he needed such a caution.

e.verse: ...spices for the anointing oil...
paras: Much use was made of this anointing oil under the law, and that which it represents is of primary importance under the gospel. The Holy Spirit, Who anoints us for all holy service, is indispensable to us if we would serve the Lord acceptably. Without His aid our religious services are only a vain offering, and our inward experience is a dead thing. Whenever our ministry is without unction, what miserable stuff it becomes; nor are the prayers, praises, meditations, and efforts of private Christians one jot superior. A holy anointing is the soul and life of piety, its absence the most grievous of all calamities. To go before the Lord without anointing is as though some common Levite had thrust himself into the priest's office—his ministrations would rather have been sins than services. May we never venture upon hallowed exercises without sacred anointings. They drop upon us from our glorious Head; from His anointing we, who are as the hem of His garments, partake of a plentiful unction. Choice spices were compounded with the rarest skill of the perfumer to form the anointing oil, to make known to us how rich are all the influences of the Holy Spirit. All good things are found in the divine Comforter. Matchless consolation, infallible instruction, immortal quickening, spiritual energy, and divine sanctification all lie compounded with other excellencies in that sacred eye salve, the heavenly anointing oil of the Holy Spirit. It imparts a delightful fragrance to the character and person of the man upon whom it is poured. Nothing like it can be found in all the treasuries of the rich, or the secrets of the wise. It is not to be imitated. It comes alone from God, and it is freely given, through Jesus Christ, to every waiting soul. Let us seek it, for we may have it, may have it this very evening. O Lord, anoint Your servants.

m.verse: Amaziah asked the man of God, "What should I do about the hundred talents I have given to the troops of Israel?" And the man of God replied, "The LORD is able to give you much more than this."
paras: This seemed to be a very important question to the king of Judah, and possibly it carries even more weight with you, O tried and tempted Christian. To lose money is at no time pleasant, and when principle involves it, the flesh is not always ready to make the sacrifice. "Why lose that which may be so usefully employed? May not the truth itself be bought too dearly? What will we do without it? Remember the children and our small income!" All these things and a thousand more would tempt the Christian to put forth his hand to unrighteous gain, or to restrain himself from carrying out his conscientious convictions when they involve serious loss. Not all men can view these matters in the light of faith; and even with the followers of Jesus, the doctrine of "we must live" carries quite enough weight.

"The LORD is able to give you much more than this" is a very satisfying answer to this anxious question. Our Father holds the purse strings, and what we lose for His sake He can repay a thousandfold. It is ours to obey His will, and we may rest fully assured that He will provide for us. The Lord will be no man's debtor at the last. Saints know that a grain of heart's ease is of more value than a ton of gold. He who wraps a threadbare coat about a good conscience has gained a spiritual wealth far more desirable than any he has lost. God's smile and a dungeon are enough for a true heart; His frown and a palace would be hell to a gracious spirit. Let the worst come to the worst, let all the talents go, we have not lost our treasure, for that is above, where Christ sits at the right hand of God. Meanwhile, even now, the LORD causes the meek to inherit the earth, and no good thing does He withhold from those who walk uprightly.

e.verse: ...Michael and his angels fought against the dragon, and the dragon and his angels fought back.
paras: War will always rage between the two great kingdoms until one or the other is crushed. Peace between good and evil is an impossibility; the very pretense of it would, in fact, be the triumph of the powers of darkness. Michael will always fight; his holy soul is vexed with sin, and will not endure it. Jesus will always be the dragon's foe, and that not in a quiet sense, but actively, vigorously, with full determination to exterminate evil. All His servants, whether angels in heaven or messengers on earth, will and must fight; they are born to be warriors—at the cross they enter into a covenant never to make truce with evil; they are a warlike company, firm in defense and fierce in attack. The duty of every soldier in the army of the Lord is daily, with all his heart, and soul, and strength, to fight against the dragon.

The dragon and his angels will not decline the battle; they are incessant in their onslaughts, sparing no weapon, fair or foul. We are foolish to expect to serve God without opposition: the more zealous we are, the more sure we are to be assailed by the minions of hell. The church may become slothful, but not so her great antagonist; his restless spirit never allows the war to pause; he hates the woman's seed, and would gladly devour the church if he could. The servants of Satan partake much of the old dragon's energy, and are usually an active race. War rages all around, and to dream of peace is dangerous and futile.

Glory be to God, we know the end of the war. The great dragon will be cast out and forever destroyed, while Jesus and those who are with Him will receive the crown. Let us sharpen our swords tonight, and pray for the Holy Spirit to strengthen our arms for the conflict. Never was a battle so important, never a crown so glorious. Every man to his post, you warriors of the cross, and may the Lord tread Satan under your feet shortly!

m.verse: ...You made the summer and winter.
paras: My soul, begin this wintry month with your God. The cold snows and the piercing winds all remind you that He keeps His covenant with day and night, and they tend to assure you that He will also keep that glorious covenant which He has made with you in the person of Christ Jesus. He Who is true to His Word in the changing cycles of the seasons of this poor, sin-polluted world will not prove unfaithful in His dealings with His own dearly beloved Son.

Winter in the soul is by no means a comfortable season, and if it is upon you right now, it will be very painful to you; but there is this comfort, namely, that the Lord brings it about. He sends the sharp blasts of adversity to nip the buds of expectation; He scatters the frost like ashes over the once-verdant meadows of our joy; He casts forth His ice like fragments, freezing the streams of our delight. He does it all; He is the great Winter King and rules in the realms of frost, and therefore you cannot complain. Losses, crosses, heaviness, sickness, poverty, and a thousand other troubles are sent by the Lord and come to us with wise design. Frosts kill noxious insects and put a check to raging diseases; they break up the hard clods and sweeten the soul. Oh, that such good results would always follow our winters of affliction!

How we prize the fire right now! How pleasant is its cheerful glow! Let us in the same way prize our Lord, Who is the constant source of warmth and comfort in every time of trouble. Let us draw near to Him, and in Him find joy and peace in believing. Let us wrap ourselves in the warm garments of His promises and go forth to the work that befits the season, for it would be shameful to be like the sluggard who will not plow because of the cold, for he will beg during the harvest and have nothing.

e.verse: Let them give thanks to the LORD for His loving devotion and His wonders to the sons of men.
paras: If we complained less and praised more, we would be happier, and God would be more glorified. Let us daily praise God for common mercies—common as we frequently call them, and yet so priceless that when deprived of them we are ready to perish. Let us bless God for the eyes with which we behold the sun, for the health and strength to walk abroad, for the bread we eat, and for the clothing we wear. Let us praise Him that we are not cast out among the hopeless or confined among the guilty; let us thank Him for liberty, for friends, for family associations and comforts; let us praise Him, in fact, for everything that we receive from His bountiful hand, for we deserve so little, and yet are most richly endowed. But, beloved, the sweetest and the loudest note in our songs of praise should be of redeeming love. God's redeeming acts toward His chosen are forever the favorite themes of their praise. If we know what redemption means, let us not withhold our songs of thanksgiving. We have been redeemed from the power of our corruptions and uplifted from the depth of sin in which we were naturally plunged. We have been led to the cross of Christ—our shackles of guilt have been broken off; we are no longer slaves, but children of the living God, and we can look forward to the time when we will be presented before the throne without stain or wrinkle or any such blemish. Even now by faith we wave the palm branch and wrap ourselves in the fine linen that will be our everlasting garments, and shall we not unceasingly give thanks to the Lord our Redeemer? Child of God, can you be silent? Awake, awake, you heirs of glory, and lead your captivity captive, as you cry with David, "Bless the LORD, O my soul; and all that is within me, bless His holy name." Let the new month begin with new songs.

m.verse: You are altogether beautiful, my darling...
paras: The Lord's admiration of His church is very wonderful, and His description of her beauty is glowing indeed. She is not merely beautiful, but "altogether beautiful." He views her in Himself, washed in His sin-atoning blood and clothed in His meritorious righteousness, and He considers her to be full of comeliness and beauty. No wonder that such is the case, since it is only His own perfect excellence that He admires; for the holiness, glory, and perfection of His church are His own glorious garments on the back of His own dearly beloved spouse. She is not simply pure or well-proportioned; she is positively lovely and fair! She has actual merit! Her deformities of sin are removed; but more, she has through her Lord obtained a meritorious righteousness by which an actual beauty is conferred upon her. Believers have a positive righteousness given to them when they become "accepted in the Beloved" (Eph. 1:6). Nor is the church merely lovely; she is superlatively so. Her Lord addresses her as "fairest among women." She has a real worth and excellence which cannot be rivaled by all the nobility and royalty of the world. If Jesus could exchange His elect bride for all the queens and empresses of earth, or even for the angels in heaven, He would not, for He puts her first and foremost—"fairest of women." Like the moon she far outshines the stars. Nor is this an opinion of which He is ashamed, for He invites all men to hear it. He places a "Behold!" before it—a special note of exclamation, inviting and arresting attention: "Behold, you are beautiful, my love; behold, you are beautiful!" (Song of Sol. 4:1). He publishes His opinion abroad even now, and one day from the throne of His glory He will openly avow the truth of it before the assembled universe. "Come, you who are blessed by My Father" (Matt. 25:34), will be His solemn affirmation of the loveliness of His elect.

e.verse: ...and have found them all to be futile...
paras: Nothing can satisfy the entire man but the Lord's love and the Lord's own self. Saints have tried to anchor in other sheltered waters, but they have been driven out of such fatal refuges. Solomon, the wisest of men, was permitted to make experiments for us all, and to do for us what we must not dare to do for ourselves. Here is his testimony in his own words: "So I became great and surpassed all who were before me in Jerusalem; also my wisdom remained with me. And whatever my eyes desired I did not keep from them; I did not withhold my heart from any joy, for my heart rejoiced in all my work, and this was my reward for all my toil. Then I considered all the works that my hands had accomplished and the toil that I had exerted to achieve them; and behold, all was futile, a pursuit of the wind, and there was no profit under the sun." "Futility of futilities, all is futile!" What! The whole of it futile? O favored monarch, is there nothing in all your wealth? Nothing in that wide dominion reaching from the river even to the sea? Nothing in Palmyra's glorious palaces? Nothing in the House of the Forest of Lebanon? In all your music and dancing, your wine and luxury, is there nothing? "Nothing," he says, "but a pursuit of the wind." This was his verdict when he had walked the entire round of worldly pleasure. To embrace our Lord Jesus, to dwell in His love, and to be fully assured of union with Him—this is all in all. Dear reader, you need not try other forms of life in order to see whether they are better than the Christian's: if you roam the world around, you will see no sights like a sight of the Savior's face; if you could have all the comforts of life, yet lost your Savior, you would be wretched; but if you win Christ, then even if you were to rot in a dungeon, you would find it a paradise; should you live in obscurity, or die of famine, you will still be satisfied with favor and full of the goodness of the Lord.

m.verse: ...in you there is no flaw.
paras: Having pronounced His church positively full of beauty, our Lord confirms His praise by a precious negative: "In you there is no flaw." As if the thought occurred to the Bridegroom that the carping world would insinuate that He had only mentioned her comely parts, and had purposely omitted those features that were deformed or defiled, He sums up all by declaring her universally and entirely beautiful, and utterly devoid of stain. A flaw may soon be removed, and is the very least thing that can disfigure beauty, but even from this little blemish the believer is delivered in his Lord's sight. If He had said there is no hideous scar, no horrible deformity, no deadly ulcer, we might even then have marveled; but when He testifies that she is free from the slightest spot, all these other forms of defilement are included, and the depth of wonder is increased. If He had only promised to remove all spots in the future, we would have had eternal reason for joy; but when He speaks of it as already done, who can restrain the most intense emotions of satisfaction and delight? O my soul, here is marrow and richness for you; eat your fill, and be satisfied with royal delicacies.

Christ Jesus has no quarrel with His spouse. She often wanders from Him, and grieves His Holy Spirit, but He does not allow her faults to affect His love. He sometimes chides, but it is always in the tenderest manner, with the kindest intentions: it is "my love" even then. There is no remembrance of our follies; He does not cherish ill thoughts of us, but He pardons and loves just as much after the offense as before it. It is well for us that it is so, for if Jesus were as mindful of injuries as we are, how could He commune with us? Many a time a believer will put himself out of humor with the Lord over some slight turn in providence, but our precious Husband knows our foolish hearts too well to take any offense at our ill manners.

e.verse: ...the LORD mighty in battle.
paras: Well may our God be glorious in the eyes of His people, seeing that He has worked such wonders for them, in them, and through them. For them, the Lord Jesus upon Calvary routed every foe, breaking all the weapons of the enemy to pieces by His finished work of satisfactory obedience; by His triumphant resurrection and ascension He completely overturned the hopes of hell, leading captivity captive, making a public spectacle of our enemies openly, and triumphing over them by His cross. Every arrow of guilt that Satan might have shot at us is broken to pieces, for who will bring any charge against God's elect? Vain are the sharp swords of infernal malice and the perpetual battles of the serpent's seed, for in the midst of the church the lame take the plunder, and even the feeblest of warriors are crowned.

The saved may well adore their Lord for His conquests in them, since the arrows of their natural hatred are snapped and the weapons of their rebellion are broken. What victories has grace won in our evil hearts! How glorious is Jesus when the will is subdued and sin is dethroned! As for our remaining corruptions, they will suffer an equally sure defeat, and every temptation, doubt, and fear will be utterly destroyed. In the Salem of our peaceful hearts, the name of Jesus is great beyond compare: He has won our love, and He will wear it. Even thus securely may we look for victories wrought through us. We are more than conquerors through Him Who loved us. We will cast down the powers of darkness that are in the world by our faith, zeal, and holiness; we will win sinners to Jesus, overturn false systems, and convert nations, for God is with us, and none will stand before us. This evening let the Christian warrior chant the battle song and prepare for tomorrow's fight. Greater is He Who is in us than he who is in the world.

m.verse: ...I have many people in this city.
paras: This should be a great encouragement to try to do good, since God has among the vilest of the vile, the most reprobate, the most debauched and drunken, an elect people who must be saved. When you take the Word to them, you do so because God has ordained you to be the messenger of life to their souls, and they must receive it, for so the decree of predestination runs. They are as much redeemed by blood as the saints before the eternal throne. They are Christ's property, and yet perhaps they are lovers of the tavern and haters of holiness; but if Jesus Christ purchased them, He will have them. God is not unfaithful to forget the price that His Son has paid. He will not allow His substitution to be in any case an ineffectual, dead thing. Tens of thousands of redeemed ones are not regenerated yet, but regenerated they must be; and this is our comfort when we go forth to them with the life-giving Word of God.

Even more, these ungodly ones are prayed for by Christ before the throne. "I do not pray for these alone," says the great Intercessor, "but also for those who will believe in Me through their word." Poor, ignorant souls, they know nothing about praying for themselves, but Jesus prays for them. Their names are on His breastplate, and before long they will bow their stubborn knees, breathing a penitent sigh before the throne of grace. "The season for figs has not yet come." The predestined moment has not struck; but when it comes, they will obey, for God will have His own; they must, for the Spirit cannot be resisted when He comes forth with the fullness of power—they must become the willing servants of the living God. "My people will be willing in the day of My power." "My righteous Servant will justify many." "He will see the fruit of the travail of His soul." "I will allot Him a portion with the great, and He will divide the spoils with the strong."

e.verse: ...we ourselves... groan inwardly as we wait eagerly for our adoption as sons, the redemption of our bodies.
paras: This groaning is universal among the saints: to a greater or lesser extent we all feel it. It is not the groan of murmuring or complaint: it is a note of desire rather than of distress. Having received a pledge of the Spirit, we desire the full measure of our portion; we sigh that our entire humanity, in its threefold nature of spirit, soul, and body, may be set free from the last vestige of the fall; we long to put off corruption, weakness, and dishonor, and to clothe ourselves with incorruption, with immortality, with glory, in the spiritual body which the Lord Jesus will bestow upon His people. We long for the full revelation of our adoption as the children of God. "We groan," but it is "within ourselves." It is not the hypocrite's groan, by which he tries to make men believe that he is a saint because he is wretched. Our sighs are sacred things, too hallowed for us to broadcast abroad. We reserve our deepest longings for our Lord alone. Then the apostle says we are "waiting," by which we learn that we are not to be petulant, like Jonah or Elijah, when they said, "Let me die"; nor are we to whimper and sigh for the end of life because we are tired of work, nor wish to escape from our present sufferings until the will of the Lord is done. We are to groan for glorification, but we are to wait patiently for it, knowing that whatever the Lord appoints is best. Waiting implies being ready. We are to stand at the door expecting the Beloved to open it and take us away to Himself. This "groaning" is a test. You may judge a man by what he groans after. Some men groan after wealth—they worship Mammon; some groan continually under the troubles of life—they are merely impatient; but the man who sighs after God, who is uneasy until he is made like Christ, that is the blessed man. May God help us to groan for the coming of the Lord, and the glorious resurrection that He will bring to us.

m.verse: Ask, and it will be given to you...
paras: We know of a place in England, still in existence, where a portion of bread is served to every passerby who chooses to ask for it. Whoever the traveler may be, he has only to knock at the door of the Hospital of St. Cross, and there is bread for him. Jesus Christ so loves sinners that He has established a Hospital of the Holy Cross, so that whenever a sinner is hungry, he has only to knock and have his needs supplied. Indeed, He has done even better: He has attached to this Hospital of the Cross a bath; and whenever a soul is dark and filthy, it has only to go there and be washed. The fountain is always full, always effective. No sinner ever entered it and found that it could not wash away his stains. Sins that were scarlet and crimson have completely vanished, and the sinner has been made whiter than snow. As if this were not enough, there is attached to this Hospital of the Cross a storehouse of clothing, and a sinner coming simply as a sinner may be clothed from head to foot; and if he desires to be a soldier, he may receive not merely a garment for ordinary wear, but armor to cover him from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head. If he asks for a sword, it will be given to him, and a shield as well. Nothing that is good for him will be denied him. He will have daily provision as long as he lives, and he will receive an eternal heritage of glorious treasure when he enters into the joy of his Lord.

If all these things are to be had by simply knocking at mercy's door, O my soul, knock hard this morning, and ask great things of your generous Lord. Do not leave the throne of grace until all your needs have been spread before the Lord, and until by faith you have a comforting assurance that they will all be supplied. No hesitation should hold you back when Jesus invites. No unbelief should hinder you when Jesus promises. No coldness of heart should restrain you when such blessings are to be obtained.

e.verse: Then the LORD showed me four craftsmen.
paras: In the vision described in this chapter, the prophet saw four terrifying horns. They were thrusting this way and that way, throwing down the strongest and the mightiest; and the prophet asked, "What are these?" The answer was, "These are the horns that have scattered Israel." He saw before him a representation of those hostile powers that had oppressed the church of God. There were four horns, for the church is attacked from all quarters. Well might the prophet have felt dismayed; but all of a sudden there appeared before him four craftsmen. He asked, "What are these coming to do?" These are the workmen whom God has found to break those horns to pieces. God will always find servants for His work, and He will find them at the right time. The prophet did not see the craftsmen first, when there was nothing to do, but first the "horns," and then the "craftsmen." Moreover, the Lord provides enough men. He did not find three craftsmen, but four; there were four horns, and therefore there must be four workmen. God finds the right men: not four men with pens to write, not four architects to draw blueprints, but four rugged craftsmen to do rough work. Rest assured, you who tremble for the cause of God, that when the "horns" grow menacing, the "craftsmen" will be found. You need not fret concerning the apparent weakness of the church of God at any moment; there may be growing up in obscurity the valiant reformer who will shake the nations: Chrysostoms may come forth from our ragged charity schools, and Augustines from the thickest darkness of London's poverty. The Lord knows where to find His servants. He holds in reserve a multitude of mighty warriors, and at His word they will spring up for the battle; "for the battle is the LORD's," and He will secure the victory for Himself. Let us remain faithful to Christ, and He, at the right time, will raise up a defense for us, whether in the day of our personal need or in a time of danger for His church.

m.verse: ...as is the heavenly man, so also are those who are of heaven.
paras: The head and the members are of one nature, and not like that colossal statue that Nebuchadnezzar saw in his dream. The head was of fine gold, but the belly and thighs were of bronze, the legs of iron, and the feet partly of iron and partly of clay. Christ's mystical body is no absurd combination of opposites: the members were mortal, and therefore Jesus died; the glorified Head is immortal, and therefore the body is immortal too, for thus the sacred record stands: "Because I live, you also will live." As is our loving Head, such is the body, and every member in particular. A chosen Head and chosen members; an accepted Head and accepted members; a living Head and living members. If the Head is pure gold, all the parts of the body are of pure gold as well. Thus there is a double union of nature serving as a foundation for the closest communion. Pause here, devout reader, and see if you can, without ecstatic amazement, contemplate the infinite grace of the Son of God in stooping down to lift your lowliness into blessed union with His glory. You are so humble in your mortality that you may say to corruption, "You are my father," and to the worm, "You are my sister"; and yet in Christ you are so honored that you can say to the Almighty, "Abba, Father," and to the Incarnate God, "You are my brother and my husband." Surely, if relations to ancient and noble lineages cause people to think highly of themselves, we have far greater reason to boast above them all. Let the poorest and most despised believer take hold of this privilege; let no senseless sluggishness make him neglect to trace his spiritual lineage, and let no foolish attachment to empty worldly pursuits occupy his thoughts to the exclusion of this glorious, this heavenly honor of union with Christ.

e.verse: ...with a golden sash around His chest.
paras: "One like the Son of Man" appeared to John on Patmos, and the beloved disciple observed that He wore a golden sash. A sash, for Jesus never set aside His sash of readiness while on earth, but stood always prepared for service; and now before the eternal throne He does not cease His holy ministry, but as a Priest wears the skillfully woven sash of the ephod. What a blessing it is for us that He has not ceased to fulfill His ministry of love on our behalf, since it is one of our greatest safeguards that He always lives to make intercession for us. Jesus is never idle; His garments are never loosened as though His holy work were finished; He diligently carries forward the cause of His people. A golden sash, to display the excellence of His service, the royalty of His person, the dignity of His state, and the glory of His reward. No longer does He cry from the dust, but He pleads with authority, a King as well as a Priest. Safe indeed is our cause in the hands of our enthroned Melchizedek.

Our Lord presents all His people with an example. We must never unfasten our belts. This is not the time for lying down at ease; it is the season of active service and spiritual warfare. We need to secure the belt of truth more and more tightly around our waists. It is a golden belt, and so will be our richest ornament, and we greatly need it; for a heart that is not well fortified with the truth as it is in Jesus, and with the faithfulness produced by the Spirit, will be easily entangled with the affairs of this life and tripped up by the traps of temptation. It does us no good to possess the Scriptures unless we wrap them around us like a belt, surrounding our entire nature, keeping each part of our character in order, and giving firm cohesion to our whole being. If in heaven Jesus does not loosen His belt, much less should we upon earth. Stand firm, therefore, with the belt of truth buckled around your waist.

m.verse: He chose the lowly and despised things of the world...
paras: Walk the streets by moonlight, if you dare, and you will see sinners then. Watch when the night is dark, the wind is howling, and the lockpick is grating in the door, and you will see sinners then. Go to that prison, walk through the wards, and observe the men with heavy, overhanging brows, men whom you would not like to meet at night, and there are sinners there. Go to the reform schools, and note those who have shown rampant juvenile depravity, and you will see sinners there. Go across the seas to the place where a man gnaws a bone with reeking human flesh, and there is a sinner there. Go wherever you will, you do not need to search the entire earth to find sinners, for they are common enough; you may find them in every lane and street of every city, town, village, and hamlet. It is for such as these that Jesus died. If you will select for me the grossest specimen of humanity, if he is only born of woman, I will still have hope for him, because Jesus Christ has come to seek and to save sinners. Electing love has selected some of the worst to be made the best. Grace turns pebbles from the brook into jewels for the royal crown. He transforms worthless dross into pure gold. Redeeming love has set apart many of the worst of mankind to be the reward of the Savior's passion. Effectual grace calls forth many of the vilest of the vile to sit at the table of mercy, and therefore let no one despair.

Reader, by that love looking out of Jesus' tearful eyes, by that love streaming from those bleeding wounds, by that faithful love, that strong love, that pure, selfless, and abiding love; by the tender heart and by the deep compassion of the Savior, we plead with you not to turn away as though it were nothing to you; but believe in Him and you will be saved. Trust your soul with Him, and He will bring you to His Father's right hand in glory everlasting.

e.verse: ...I have become all things to all people so that by all possible means I might save some.
paras: Paul's great goal was not merely to instruct and improve, but to save. Anything short of this would have disappointed him; he desired that people be renewed in heart, forgiven, sanctified—in fact, saved. Has our Christian work been aimed at anything below this great point? Then let us amend our ways, for what good will it do on the last great day to have taught and moralized people if they appear before God unsaved? Our clothes will be blood-red if through life we have sought inferior goals, and forgotten that people needed to be saved. Paul knew the ruin of man's fallen state, and did not try to educate him, but to save him; he saw people sinking toward hell, and did not speak of refining them, but of saving them from the wrath to come. To accomplish their salvation, he gave himself up with untiring zeal to proclaiming the gospel far and wide, warning and imploring people to be reconciled to God. His prayers were earnest, and his work was tireless. To save souls was his consuming passion, his ambition, his calling. He became a servant to all, toiling for his fellow man, feeling a woe within him if he did not preach the gospel. He laid aside his preferences to avoid prejudice; he submitted his will in nonessential matters, and if only people would receive the gospel, he raised no questions about forms or ceremonies: the gospel was the one all-important business with him. If he could save some, he would be content. This was the crown for which he strove, the sole and sufficient reward of all his toil and self-denial. Dear reader, have you and I lived to win souls with such noble devotion? Are we possessed with the same all-absorbing desire? If not, why not? Jesus died for sinners; can we not live for them? Where is our tenderness? Where is our love for Christ, if we do not seek His honor in the salvation of souls? O that the Lord would saturate us through and through with an undying zeal for the souls of men.

m.verse: But you do have a few people in Sardis who have not soiled their garments, and because they are worthy, they will walk with Me in white.
paras: We may understand this to refer to justification. "They will walk in white"; that is, they will enjoy a constant sense of their own justification by faith; they will understand that the righteousness of Christ is imputed to them, and that they have all been washed and made whiter than the newly fallen snow.

Again, it refers to joy and gladness, for white robes were festive attire among the Jews. Those who have not soiled their garments will have their faces always bright; they will understand what Solomon meant when he said, "Go, eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a cheerful heart, for God has already approved your works. Let your garments always be white." The one who is accepted by God will wear white garments of joy and gladness, while walking in sweet communion with the Lord Jesus. Why so many doubts, so much misery, and mourning? It is because so many believers soil their garments with sin and error, and therefore they lose the joy of their salvation and the comforting fellowship of the Lord Jesus; they do not walk in white here below.

The promise also refers to walking in white before the throne of God. Those who have not soiled their garments here will most certainly walk in white up above, where the white-robed hosts sing perpetual hallelujahs to the Most High. They will possess joys inconceivable, happiness beyond a dream, bliss that imagination does not know, and blessedness that even the reach of desire has not attained. The "blameless in the way" will have all this—not by merit, nor by works, but of grace. They will walk with Christ in white, for He has made them worthy. In His sweet company they will drink from springs of living water.

e.verse: ...O God, from Your bounty You provided for the poor.
paras: All God's gifts are prepared gifts laid up in store for anticipated needs. He anticipates our wants; and out of the fullness that He has treasured up in Christ Jesus, He provides from His goodness for the poor. You may trust Him for all the necessities that can ever occur, for He has infallibly foreknown every one of them. He can say of us in all our conditions, "I knew that you would be this and that." A traveler goes on a journey across the desert, and when he has advanced for a day and pitched his tent, he discovers that he lacks many comforts and necessities that he did not bring in his baggage. "Ah!" he says, "I did not foresee this; if I were to make this journey again, I would bring these things with me, which are so necessary to my comfort." But God has marked with a foreseeing eye all the requirements of His poor wandering children, and when those needs occur, supplies are ready. It is goodness that He has prepared for the poor in heart, pure goodness and goodness alone. "My grace is sufficient for you." "Your strength will match your days.

Reader, is your heart heavy this evening? God knew it would be; the comfort that your heart needs is treasured in the sweet assurance of our text. You are poor and needy, but the Lord thinks of you, and He has the exact blessing that you require in store for you. Plead the promise, believe it, and receive its fulfillment. Do you feel that you were never so consciously vile as you are right now? Behold, the crimson fountain remains open still, with all its former efficacy, to wash your sin away. You will never come into such a position that Christ cannot help you. No crisis will ever arise in your spiritual affairs in which Jesus Christ will not be equal to the emergency, for your history has all been foreknown and provided for in Jesus.

m.verse: Therefore the LORD longs to be gracious to you...
paras: God often delays in answering prayer. We have several clear examples of this in sacred Scripture. Jacob did not receive the blessing from the angel until near the break of dawn—he had to wrestle all night for it. The poor Syrophoenician woman was answered not a single word for a long time. Paul pleaded with the Lord three times that the "thorn in the flesh" might be taken from him, and he received no promise that it would be removed, but instead received the assurance that God's grace would be sufficient for him. If you have been knocking at the gate of mercy and have received no answer, shall I tell you why the mighty Maker has not yet opened the door and welcomed you in? Our Father has reasons unique to Himself for keeping us waiting in this way. Sometimes it is to display His sovereign power, that people may know that the LORD has the sovereign right to give or to withhold. More frequently, the delay is for our own benefit. You are perhaps kept waiting so that your desires may become more fervent. God knows that delay will quicken and intensify your longing; if He keeps you waiting, you will see your need more clearly, you will seek more earnestly, and you will treasure the mercy all the more because of its long delay. There may also be something wrong within you that needs to be removed before the joy of the Lord is granted. Perhaps your understanding of the gospel plan is confused, or you may be placing some small reliance on yourself instead of trusting simply and entirely in the Lord Jesus. Or perhaps God makes you wait awhile so that He may more fully display the riches of His grace to you in the end. Your prayers are all recorded in heaven, and if not immediately answered, they are certainly not forgotten; in a little while, they will be fulfilled to your delight and satisfaction. Let no despair make you silent, but remain constant in earnest prayer.

e.verse: Then my people will dwell in a peaceful place, in safe and secure places of rest.
paras: Peace and rest do not belong to the unregenerate; they are the treasured possession of the Lord's people, and of them alone. The God of peace gives perfect peace to those whose minds are stayed on Him. When man was unfallen, his God gave him the fragrant bowers of Eden as his quiet resting places; alas, how quickly sin blighted that fair home of innocence! In the day of universal wrath, when the flood swept away a guilty world, the chosen family were safely sheltered in the resting place of the ark, which carried them from the old condemned world into the new earth of the rainbow and the covenant—in this prefiguring Jesus, the true ark of our salvation. Israel rested safely beneath the blood-sprinkled homes of Egypt when the destroying angel struck down the firstborn; and in the wilderness, the shadow of the pillar of cloud and the water from the rock gave the weary pilgrims sweet repose. At this hour, we rest in the promises of our faithful God, knowing that His words are full of truth and power; we rest in the doctrines of His Word, which are comfort itself; we rest in the covenant of His grace, which is a haven of delight. We are more highly favored than David in the cave of Adullam, or Jonah beneath his sheltering plant, for no enemy can invade or destroy our shelter. The person of Jesus is the quiet resting place of His people; and when we draw near to Him in the breaking of bread, in the hearing of the Word, in searching the Scriptures, in prayer, or in praise, we find every approach to Him brings the return of sweet peace to our souls.

I hear the words of love,
I gaze upon the blood,
I see the mighty sacrifice,
And I have peace with God.

'Tis everlasting peace,
Sure as Jehovah's name,
'Tis stable as His steadfast throne,
Forevermore the same:

The clouds may go and come,
And storms may sweep my sky,
This blood-sealed friendship changes not,
The cross is ever nigh.

m.verse: ...And so we will always be with the Lord.
paras: Even the sweetest visits from Christ, how short they are—and how fleeting! One moment our eyes see Him, and we rejoice with joy inexpressible and full of glory; but soon a little while passes and we do not see Him, for our Beloved withdraws Himself from us. Like a gazelle or a young stag, He leaps over the rugged mountains; He has gone to the land of spices, and feeds no more among the lilies.

If today He deigns to bless us
With a sense of pardoned sin,
He tomorrow may distress us,
Make us feel the plague within.

Oh, how sweet is the prospect of that day when we will no longer behold Him from afar, but see Him face to face: when He will no longer be like a traveler staying only for a night, but will eternally enfold us in the embrace of His glory! We will not see Him merely for a brief season, but—

Millions of years our wondering eyes
Shall o'er our Savior's beauties rove;
And myriad ages we'll adore
The wonders of His love.

In heaven there will be no interruptions from anxiety or sin; no tears will dim our eyes; no earthly concerns will distract our joyful thoughts; we will have nothing to hinder us from gazing forever upon the Sun of Righteousness with unwearied vision. Oh, if it is so sweet to see Him now and then, how sweet to gaze upon that blessed face forever, with no cloud rolling between, and never having to turn our eyes away to look upon a world of weariness and sorrow! Blessed day, when will you dawn? Rise, O unsetting Sun! The fleeting pleasures of this world may leave us whenever they will, for this sight will make glorious amends. If to die is only to enter into unbroken communion with Jesus, then death is indeed gain, and that bitter drop is swallowed up in an ocean of victory.

e.verse: ...The Lord opened her heart...
paras: In Lydia's conversion there are many points of deep interest. It was brought about through providential circumstances. She was a dealer in purple cloth from the city of Thyatira, but just at the right time for hearing Paul, we find her at Philippi; providence, which is the servant of grace, guided her to the very spot. Again, grace was preparing her soul for the blessing—grace preparing the way for grace. She did not yet know the Savior, but as a worshiper of God, she knew many truths that served as excellent stepping-stones to the knowledge of Jesus. Her conversion took place through the use of the appointed means. On the Sabbath, she went where prayer was customarily made, and there her prayer was heard. Never neglect the means of grace; God may bless us when we are outside His house, but we have far greater reason to expect His blessing when we are in fellowship with His saints. Observe the inspired words: "The Lord opened her heart." She did not open her own heart. Her prayers did not do it; Paul did not do it. The Lord Himself must open the heart to receive the things that belong to our peace. He alone can place the key in the lock, open the door, and enter in for Himself. He is the heart's Master, even as He is the heart's Maker. The first outward evidence of this opened heart was obedience. As soon as Lydia believed in Jesus, she was baptized. It is a precious sign of a humble and contrite heart when a child of God willingly obeys a command that is not essential to salvation, not forced by a selfish fear of condemnation, but performed as a simple act of loving obedience and communion with the Master. The next evidence was love, showing itself in acts of grateful hospitality to the apostles. Love for the saints has always been the true mark of a genuine convert. Those who do nothing for Christ or His church give only poor evidence of an opened heart. Lord, continually grant me an opened heart.

m.verse: The One who calls you is faithful, and He will do it.
paras: Heaven is a place where we will never sin; where we will cease our constant watch against a tireless enemy, because there will be no tempter to trap our feet. There the wicked cease from raging, and the weary find rest. Heaven is the "undefiled inheritance"; it is the land of perfect holiness, and therefore of complete security. But do not the saints even on earth sometimes taste the joys of blissful security? The doctrine of God's Word is that all who are in union with the Lamb are safe; that all the righteous will hold to their way; that those who have committed their souls to the keeping of Christ will find Him a faithful and unchanging protector. Sustained by such a doctrine, we can enjoy security even on earth—not that absolute and final security that frees us from every misstep, but that holy security that arises from the sure promise of Jesus that none who believe in Him will ever perish, but will be with Him where He is. Believer, let us often reflect with joy on the doctrine of the perseverance of the saints, and honor the faithfulness of our God with holy confidence in Him.

May our God bring home to you a deep sense of your safety in Christ Jesus! May He assure you that your name is engraved on the palms of His hands, and whisper in your ear the promise, "Do not fear, for I am with you." Look upon Him, the great Surety of the covenant, as faithful and true, and therefore bound and committed to present you, the weakest of the family, together with all the chosen race, before the throne of God. In such sweet contemplation you will drink the juice of the spiced pomegranate wine of the Lord, and taste the choice fruits of Paradise. You will enjoy a foretaste of the delights that captivate the souls of the perfected saints above, if you can believe with unwavering faith that "the One who calls you is faithful, and He will do it."

e.verse: ...It is the Lord Christ you are serving.
paras: To what choice order of officials was this word spoken? To kings who proudly boast of divine right? Ah, no! All too often they serve themselves or Satan, and forget the God Whose forbearance permits them to wear their mimic majesty for their brief hour. Does the apostle speak, then, to those so-called "right reverend fathers in God," the bishops, or "the venerable archdeacons"? No, indeed; Paul knew nothing of these mere human inventions. Not even to pastors and teachers, or to the wealthy and esteemed among believers, was this word spoken, but to servants, yes, and even to slaves. Among the toiling multitudes—the apprentices, the day workers, the domestic servants, and the kitchen drudges—the apostle found, as we still find today, some of the Lord's chosen. To them he says, "Whatever you do, work at it with your whole being, for the Lord and not for men, because you know that you will receive an inheritance from the Lord as your reward—it is the Lord Christ you are serving." This word ennobles the weary routine of earthly employment, and casts a sacred glow around the humblest tasks. To wash feet may be menial, but to wash His feet is royal service. To untie a sandal strap is a lowly task, but to untie the great Master's sandal is a princely privilege. The workshop, the barn, the scullery, and the forge become temples when men and women do all things to the glory of God! Then "divine service" is not confined to a few hours and a few sacred places, but all of life becomes holiness to the Lord, and every place and thing becomes as consecrated as the tabernacle and its golden lampstand.

m.verse: ...His ways are everlasting.
paras: What He has done at one time, He will do yet again. Man's ways are changeable, but God's ways are everlasting. There are many reasons for this most comforting truth, among which are the following: the Lord's ways are the result of wise deliberation; He orders all things according to the counsel of His own will. Human action is frequently the hasty result of passion or fear, and is followed by regret and change; but nothing can take the Almighty by surprise, or happen differently from what He has foreseen. His ways are the natural expression of an unchanging character, and in them the fixed and settled attributes of God are clearly displayed. Unless the Eternal One Himself could undergo change, His ways, which are Himself in action, must remain forever the same. Is He eternally just, gracious, faithful, wise, and tender? Then His ways must ever be distinguished by these same excellences. Created beings act according to their nature; when those natures change, their conduct varies as well; but since God cannot know the shadow of turning, His ways will abide everlastingly the same. Furthermore, there is no external power that could reverse the divine ways, since they are the embodiment of irresistible might. The prophet describes the earth cleft with rivers, mountains trembling, the deep lifting up its hands, and the sun and moon standing still, when the LORD marches forth for the salvation of His people. Who can hold back His hand or say to Him, "What have You done?" But it is not might alone that gives stability; God's ways are the manifestation of the eternal principles of righteousness, and therefore can never pass away. Wrong breeds decay and leads to ruin, but truth and goodness possess a vitality that the passing ages cannot diminish.
This morning let us go to our heavenly Father with confidence, remembering that Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever, and in Him the Lord is always gracious to His people.

e.verse: They have been unfaithful to the LORD...
paras: Believer, here is a sorrowful truth! You are the beloved of the Lord, redeemed by blood, called by grace, preserved in Christ Jesus, accepted in the Beloved, on your way to heaven; and yet, you have been unfaithful to God, your best Friend; unfaithful to Jesus, Whose you are; unfaithful to the Holy Spirit, by Whom you have been made alive to eternal life! How unfaithful you have been in the matter of vows and promises. Do you remember the love of your early devotion, that joyful spring season of your spiritual life? Oh, how closely did you cling to your Master then, saying, "He will never charge me with indifference; my feet will never grow slow in the way of His service; I will not allow my heart to wander after other loves; in Him is every store of ineffable sweetness. I give up everything for the sake of my Lord Jesus." Has it been so? Alas, if conscience speaks, it will say, "The one who promised so well has performed so poorly. Prayer has often been hurried—it has been short, but not sweet; brief, but not fervent. Communion with Christ has been forgotten. Instead of a heavenly mind, there have been worldly cares, carnal pursuits, and thoughts of evil. Instead of service, there has been disobedience; instead of fervency, lukewarmness; instead of patience, irritation; instead of faith, trust in an arm of flesh; and as a soldier of the cross there has been cowardice, disloyalty, and desertion, to a truly shameful degree." You have been unfaithful! Treachery to Jesus—what words can be used to denounce it? Words accomplish little: let our penitent thoughts abhor the sin that is so surely within us. Unfaithful to Your wounds, O Jesus! Forgive us, and let us not sin again! How shameful to be unfaithful to Him Who never forgets us, but Who today stands with our names engraved on His breastplate before the eternal throne.

m.verse: ...and salt without limit.
paras: Salt was used in every offering made by fire to the Lord, and from its preserving and purifying qualities it was a fitting emblem of divine grace in the soul. It is worthy of our careful attention that, when Artaxerxes gave salt to Ezra the priest, he set no limit on the quantity; and we may be quite certain that when the King of kings distributes grace among His royal priesthood, the supply is never cut short by Him. We are often limited within ourselves, but never in the Lord. The one who chooses to gather much manna will find that he may have as much as he desires. There is no such famine in Jerusalem that the citizens should eat their bread by weight and drink their water by measure. Some things in the economy of grace are measured; for instance, our vinegar and gall are given to us with such exactness that we never receive a single drop too much; but of the salt of grace no restriction is made: "Ask whatever you wish, and it will be given to you." Parents need to lock up the fruit cupboard and the jars of sweets, but there is no need to keep the salt box under lock and key, for few children will eat too greedily from that. A person may have too much money, or too much worldly honor, but he cannot have too much grace. When Jeshurun grew fat in the flesh, he kicked against God, but there is no danger of a believer becoming too full of grace: a surplus of grace is impossible. More wealth brings more anxiety, but more grace brings more joy. Increased worldly wisdom is increased sorrow, but the abundance of the Spirit is fullness of joy. Believer, go to the throne of grace for a large supply of heavenly salt. It will season your afflictions, which are tasteless without salt; it will preserve your heart, which corrupts if salt is absent; and it will destroy your sins even as salt kills noxious vermin. You need much; seek much, and receive much.

e.verse: I will make your windows of agates...
paras: The church is most instructively symbolized by a building erected by heavenly power and designed by divine skill. Such a spiritual house must not be dark, for the Israelites had light in their dwellings; there must therefore be windows to let the light in and to allow the inhabitants to gaze abroad. These windows are precious as agates: the ways in which the church beholds her Lord and heaven, and spiritual truth in general, are to be held in the highest esteem. Agates are not the most transparent of gems; they are only semitransparent at best:

Our knowledge of that life is small,
Our eye of faith is dim.

Faith is one of these precious agate windows, but alas, it is often so misty and beclouded that we see only dimly, and misunderstand much of what we do see. Yet if we cannot gaze through windows of diamonds and know fully even as we are known, it is a glorious thing to behold the altogether lovely One, even though the glass is hazy as the agate. Experience is another of these dim but precious windows, giving to us a subdued spiritual light, in which we see the sufferings of the Man of Sorrows through our own afflictions. Our weak eyes could not endure windows of transparent glass to let in the full splendor of the Master's glory; but when they are dimmed with weeping, the beams of the Sun of Righteousness are softened, and shine through the windows of agate with a quiet radiance inexpressibly soothing to tempted souls. Sanctification, as it conforms us to our Lord, is another agate window. Only as we become heavenly can we comprehend heavenly things. The pure in heart see a pure God. Those who are like Jesus see Him as He is. Because we are so little like Him, the window is only agate; because we are somewhat like Him, it is agate. We thank God for what we have, and long for more. When will we see God and Jesus, and heaven and truth, face to face?

m.verse: They go from strength to strength...
paras: They go from strength to strength. There are various translations of these words, but all of them express the clear idea of spiritual progress.

Our own familiar translation is sufficient for us this morning: "They go from strength to strength." That is, they grow stronger and stronger. Usually, in natural walking, we go from strength to weakness; we start out fresh and energetic for our journey, but before long the road becomes rough and the sun grows hot, so we sit down by the wayside and then painfully resume our weary way. But the Christian pilgrim, having obtained fresh supplies of grace, is as vigorous after years of toilsome travel and struggle as when he first set out. He may not be quite so elated and buoyant, nor perhaps quite so eager and hasty in his zeal as he once was, but he is much stronger in all that constitutes true spiritual power, and he travels, if more slowly, far more surely. Some gray-haired veterans have been as firm in their grasp of truth, and as zealous in spreading it, as they were in their youth; but alas, it must be confessed that often it is otherwise, for the love of many grows cold and iniquity abounds. Yet this is their own failure and not the fault of the promise, which still holds true: "Even youths grow tired and weary, and young men stumble and fall; but those who wait upon the LORD will renew their strength. They will soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary; they will walk and not faint." Fretful spirits sit down and torment themselves about the future. "Alas!" they say, "we go from affliction to affliction." That is very true, O you of little faith, but remember that you go from strength to strength as well. You will never find a bundle of affliction that does not have enclosed within it all-sufficient grace. God will supply the strength of mature spiritual manhood for the burden placed upon full-grown shoulders.

e.verse: I have been crucified with Christ...
paras: The Lord Jesus Christ acted in what He did as a great public representative person, and His dying upon the cross was the virtual death of all His people. In that hour, all His saints rendered to divine justice what was due, and made an expiation for all their sins. The apostle of the Gentiles delighted to know that as one of Christ's chosen people, he had died upon the cross in Christ. He did more than believe this doctrinally; he accepted it with confident assurance, resting his entire hope upon it. He believed that by virtue of Christ's death, he had satisfied divine justice and found true reconciliation with God. Beloved, what a blessed thing it is when the soul can, as it were, stretch itself upon the cross of Christ and feel, "I am dead; the law has slain me, and I am therefore delivered from its power, because in my Surety I have borne the curse, and in the person of my Substitute everything that the law could do by way of condemnation has been executed upon me, for I have been crucified with Christ."

Yet Paul meant even more than this. He not only believed in Christ's death and trusted in it, but he actively experienced its power within himself, bringing about the crucifixion of his old corrupt nature. When he saw the pleasures of sin, he declared, "I cannot enjoy these: I am dead to them." Such is the true experience of every genuine Christian. Having received Christ, he is to this world as one who is completely dead. Yet, while conscious of death to the world, he can, at the same time, exclaim with the apostle, "Nevertheless I live." He is fully alive to God in Christ Jesus. The Christian's life is a matchless riddle. No worldly person can comprehend it; even the believer himself cannot fully explain it. Dead, yet alive! Crucified with Christ, and yet at the same time risen with Christ in newness of life! Vital union with the suffering, bleeding Savior, and death to the world and sin, are soul-cheering things. O for more enjoyment of them!

m.verse: ...Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth clung to her.
paras: Both of them had an affection for Naomi, and therefore set out with her upon her return to the land of Judah. But the hour of testing came; Naomi most unselfishly set before each of them the trials that awaited them, and urged them, if they cared for ease and comfort, to return to their Moabite friends. At first both of them declared that they would cast their lot with the Lord's people; but upon further consideration, Orpah, with much grief and a respectful kiss, left her mother-in-law, her people, and her gods, and went back to her idolatrous friends; while Ruth with all her heart gave herself up to the God of her mother-in-law. It is one thing to love the ways of the Lord when all is fair, and quite another to cling to them amidst all discouragements and difficulties. The kiss of outward profession is very cheap and easy, but practical devotion to the Lord, which must show itself in holy decision for truth and holiness, is no small matter. How does the case stand with us? Is our heart fixed upon Jesus? Is the sacrifice secured with cords to the horns of the altar? Have we counted the cost, and are we solemnly ready to suffer all worldly loss for the Master's sake? The future gain will be an abundant recompense, for Egypt's treasures are not to be compared with the glory to be revealed. Orpah is heard of no more; in worldly ease and idolatrous pleasure her life melts into the gloom of death; but Ruth lives in history and in heaven, for grace has placed her in the noble lineage from which sprang the King of kings. Blessed among women will they be who for Christ's sake can renounce all; but forgotten, and worse than forgotten, will they be who in the hour of temptation violate conscience and turn back to the world. O that this morning we may not be content with the mere form of devotion, which may be no better than Orpah's kiss; but may the Holy Spirit work in us a clinging of our whole heart to our Lord Jesus.

e.verse: ...and lay your foundations with sapphires.
paras: Not only that which is seen of the church of God, but that which is unseen, is beautiful and precious. Foundations are out of sight, and as long as they are firm, it is not expected that they should be valuable; but in the LORD's work everything is harmonious and complete, with nothing neglected and nothing cheap. The deep foundations of the work of grace are as sapphires for preciousness; no human mind is able to measure their glory. We build upon the covenant of grace, which is firmer than granite, and as enduring as jewels upon which age spends itself in vain. Sapphire foundations are eternal, and the covenant abides throughout the lifetime of the Almighty. Another foundation is the person of the Lord Jesus, which is clear and spotless, everlasting and beautiful as the sapphire, blending in one the deep blue of earth's rolling ocean and the azure of its all-embracing sky. At one time our Lord might have been likened to the ruby as He stood covered with His own blood, but now we see Him radiant with the soft blue of love—love abounding, deep, and eternal. Our everlasting hopes are built upon the justice and the faithfulness of God, which are clear and cloudless as the sapphire. We are not saved by a compromise, by mercy defeating justice, or by law suspending its operations; no, we defy the eagle's eye to detect a flaw in the groundwork of our confidence—our foundation is of sapphire, and will endure the fire.

The Lord Himself has laid the foundation of His people's hopes. It is a matter for serious inquiry whether our hopes are built upon such a basis. Good works and empty ceremonies are not a foundation of sapphires, but of wood, hay, and straw; neither are they laid by God, but by our own conceit. Foundations will all be tried before long: woe to him whose lofty tower comes crashing down because it was based upon shifting sand. The one who is built upon sapphires may await storm or fire with peace of mind, for he will endure the test.

m.verse: Come to Me...
paras: The cry of the Christian faith is the gentle word, "Come." The Jewish law sternly said, "Go, watch your steps along the path in which you walk. Break the commandments, and you will perish; keep them, and you will live." The law was a dispensation of terror, which drove people before it as with a whip; the gospel draws with cords of love. Jesus is the Good Shepherd going before His sheep, bidding them follow Him, and ever leading them onward with the sweet word, "Come." The law repels, but the gospel attracts. The law shows the distance that exists between God and man; the gospel bridges that awful chasm, and brings the sinner safely across.

From the first moment of your spiritual life until you are ushered into glory, the language of Christ to you will be, "Come, come to Me." As a mother extends her finger to her little child and encourages it to walk by saying, "Come," even so does Jesus. He will always be ahead of you, bidding you follow Him as the soldier follows his captain. He will always go before you to prepare your way and clear your path, and you will hear His encouraging voice calling you after Him all through life; while in the solemn hour of death, His sweet words with which He will welcome you into the heavenly world will be: "Come, you who are blessed by My Father."

Indeed, this is not only Christ's call to you, but if you are a believer, this is your cry to Christ: "Come! Come!" You will be longing for His second coming; you will be saying, "Come quickly; even so, come, Lord Jesus!" You will be thirsting for nearer and closer communion with Him. As His voice to you is "Come," your response to Him will be, "Come, Lord, and abide with me. Come, and occupy alone the throne of my heart; reign there without a rival, and consecrate me entirely to Your service."

e.verse: You have never heard; you have never understood; for a long time your ears have not been open...
paras: It is painful to remember that, to a certain degree, this accusation may be laid at the door of believers, who too often are spiritually insensitive. We may well grieve that we do not hear the voice of God as we ought: "You have never heard." There are gentle promptings of the Holy Spirit in the soul that are unheeded by us; there are whisperings of divine command and heavenly love that are alike unobserved by our dull minds. Alas, we have been carelessly ignorant: "You have never understood." There are inner corruptions that have advanced unnoticed; sweet affections that are blighted like flowers in the frost, untended by us; and glimpses of the divine face that might be enjoyed if we did not close the windows of our soul. But we "have not known." As we reflect upon this, we are humbled in deepest self-abasement. How we must adore the grace of God as we learn from the context that all this folly and ignorance on our part was foreknown by Him, and yet, in spite of that foreknowledge, He has been pleased to deal with us in boundless mercy! Admire the marvelous sovereign grace that could have chosen us in view of all this! Wonder at the price that was paid for us when Christ knew what we would be! He Who hung upon the cross foresaw us as unbelieving, backsliding, cold of heart, indifferent, careless, and lax in prayer, and yet He said, "For I am the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Savior... Because you are precious in My eyes and honored, and I have loved you, I will give people in exchange for you and nations in place of your life"! O redemption, how wondrously radiant you shine when we consider how dark with sin we are! O Holy Spirit, give us from this day forward a hearing ear and an understanding heart!

m.verse: ...I remember the devotion of your youth...
paras: Let us note that Christ delights to think upon His church, and to look upon her beauty. As the bird returns often to its nest, and as the traveler hastens to his home, so does the mind continually pursue the object of its choice. We cannot look too often upon that beloved face that we love; we desire always to have our most precious treasures before our eyes. It is even so with our Lord Jesus. From all eternity, "His delights were with the sons of men"; His thoughts rolled onward to the time when His elect should be born into the world; He viewed them in the mirror of His foreknowledge. "In Your book," He says, "all My members were written, which in days to come were fashioned, when as yet there was none of them." When the world was established upon its pillars, He was there, and He set the boundaries of the peoples according to the number of the children of Israel. Many a time before His incarnation, He descended to this lower earth in the likeness of a man: on the plains of Mamre, beside the brook of Jabbok, beneath the walls of Jericho, and in the midst of the fiery furnace of Babylon, the Son of Man visited His people. Because His soul delighted in them, He could not rest away from them, for His heart yearned after them. Never were they absent from His heart, for He had written their names upon His hands, and engraved them upon His side. As the breastplate containing the names of the tribes of Israel was the most brilliant ornament worn by the high priest, so the names of Christ's elect were His most precious jewels, glittering upon His heart. We may often forget to meditate upon the perfections of our Lord, but He never ceases to remember us. Let us chide ourselves for past forgetfulness, and pray for grace ever to bear Him in fondest remembrance. Lord, paint upon the eyes of my soul the image of Your Son.

e.verse: I am the gate. If anyone enters through Me, he will be saved. He will come in and go out and find pasture.
paras: Jesus, the great I AM, is the entrance into the true church and the way of access to God Himself. He gives to the one who comes to God by Him four choice privileges.

1. He will be saved. The fleeing manslayer passed the gate of the city of refuge and was safe. Noah entered the door of the ark and was secure. None can be lost who take Jesus as the door of faith to their souls. Entrance through Jesus into peace is the guarantee of entrance by the same door into heaven. Jesus is the only door, an open door, a wide door, a safe door; and blessed is he who rests all his hope of admission to glory upon the crucified Redeemer.

2. He will go in. He will be privileged to go in among the divine family, sharing the children's bread, and participating in all their honors and enjoyments. He will go in to the chambers of communion, to the banquets of love, to the treasures of the covenant, and to the storehouses of the promises. He will go in to the King of kings in the power of the Holy Spirit, and the secret of the Lord will be with him.

3. He will go out. This blessing is often forgotten. We go out into the world to work and suffer, but what a mercy it is to go in the name and power of Jesus! We are called to bear witness to the truth, to cheer the disconsolate, to warn the careless, to win souls, and to glorify God; and as the angel said to Gideon, "Go in this your might," even so the Lord would have us proceed as His messengers in His name and strength.

4. He will find pasture. He who knows Jesus will never lack. Going in and out will be alike helpful to him: in fellowship with God he will grow, and in watering others he will be watered himself. Having made Jesus his all, he will find all in Jesus. His soul will be as a well-watered garden, and as a spring of water whose waters never fail.

m.verse: So rend your hearts and not your garments...
paras: The tearing of garments and other outward signs of religious emotion are easily displayed and are frequently hypocritical; but to feel genuine repentance is far more difficult, and consequently far less common. People will readily attend to the most elaborate and minute ceremonial regulations—for such things are pleasing to the flesh—but true religion is too humbling, too heart-searching, and too thorough for the tastes of worldly minds; they prefer something more ostentatious, superficial, and popular. Outward observances provide temporary comfort; eye and ear are pleased, self-conceit is fed, and self-righteousness is puffed up. Yet they are ultimately delusive, for in the hour of death and at the day of judgment, the soul needs something far more substantial than ceremonies and rituals to lean upon. Apart from vital godliness, all religion is utterly empty; offered without a sincere heart, every form of worship is a solemn sham and an insolent mockery of the majesty of heaven.

Heart-rending is produced by God and solemnly felt. It is a secret grief that is personally experienced, not as a mere outward form, but as a deep, soul-moving work of the Holy Spirit upon the inmost heart of each believer. It is not a matter merely to be talked of and believed in, but keenly and sensitively felt in every living child of the living God. It is powerfully humbling and completely sin-purging; yet it is sweetly preparatory for those gracious consolations that proud, unhumbled spirits are unable to receive; and it is distinctly discerning, for it belongs to the elect of God, and to them alone.

Our text commands us to rend our hearts, but they are naturally hard as marble: how, then, can this be done? We must take them to Calvary. A dying Savior's voice split the rocks of old, and it is just as powerful now. O blessed Spirit, let us hear the death cries of Jesus, and our hearts will be torn even as people tear their garments in the day of mourning.

e.verse: Be sure to know the state of your flocks, and pay close attention to your herds...
paras: Every wise merchant will occasionally take inventory, when he will balance his accounts, examine what stock he has on hand, and ascertain decisively whether his business is prosperous or declining. Every person who is wise in the kingdom of heaven will cry, "Search me, O God, and know my heart"; and he will frequently set apart special seasons for self-examination, to discover whether matters are right between God and his soul. The God Whom we worship is a great heart-searcher; and of old His servants knew Him as the Lord Who searches the heart and tests the inmost thoughts of the children of men. Let me stir you up in His name to make diligent search and solemn trial of your spiritual state, lest you fall short of the promised rest. That which every prudent person does, and that which God Himself does with us all, I urge you to do with yourself this evening. Let the oldest saint look well to the foundation of his piety, for gray heads may cover black hearts; and let not the young professor of religion despise this word of warning, for the freshness of youth may be joined to the rottenness of hypocrisy. Every now and then a great cedar falls in our midst. The enemy still continues to sow tares among the wheat. It is not my aim to introduce doubts and fears into your mind; no, indeed, but I hope instead that the searching wind of self-examination will help to drive them away. It is not security, but carnal security, that we wish to destroy; not confidence, but fleshly confidence, that we wish to overthrow; not true peace, but false peace, that we seek to banish. By the precious blood of Christ, which was not shed to make you a hypocrite, but that sincere souls might display His praise, I implore you, search and see, lest at the last it be said of you: "Mene, Mene, Tekel: you have been weighed in the balances, and found wanting."

m.verse: The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the LORD.
paras: If the decision of the lot is the Lord's, whose is the arrangement of our whole life? If the simple casting of a lot is guided by Him, how much more the events of our entire life—especially when we are told by our blessed Savior: "The very hairs of your head are all numbered: not a sparrow falls to the ground apart from your Father." It would bring a holy calm over your mind, dear friend, if you were always to remember this. It would so relieve your mind from anxiety that you would be better able to walk in patience, quietness, and cheerfulness, as a Christian should. When a person is anxious, he cannot pray with faith; when he is troubled about the world, he cannot serve his Master, for his thoughts are serving himself. If you would "seek first the kingdom of God and His righteousness," all these things would then be added to you. You are meddling with Christ's business and neglecting your own when you fret about your lot and circumstances. You have been trying "providing" work and forgetting that it is yours to obey. Be wise and attend to obedience, and let Christ manage the providing. Come and survey your Father's storehouse, and ask whether He will let you starve while He has laid up so great an abundance in His granary! Look at His heart of mercy; see if that can ever prove unkind! Look at His inscrutable wisdom; see if that will ever be at fault! Above all, look up to Jesus Christ your Intercessor, and ask yourself, while He pleads, can your Father deal ungraciously with you? If He remembers even sparrows, will He forget one of the least of His poor children? "Cast your burden upon the LORD, and He will sustain you; He will never let the righteous be shaken."

My soul, rest happy in thy low estate,
Nor hope nor wish to be esteemed or great;
To take the impress of the Will Divine,
Be that thy glory, and those riches thine.

e.verse: ...and the sea was no more.
paras: We could scarcely rejoice at the thought of losing the glorious old ocean: the new heavens and the new earth are no more appealing to our imagination if, indeed, literally there is to be no great and wide sea, with its gleaming waves and shell-strewn shores. Is not the text to be read as a metaphor, tinged with the hesitation with which the ancient Eastern mind universally regarded the sea in olden times? It is mournful to imagine a real physical world without a sea; it would be like an iron ring without the sapphire that made it precious. There must be a spiritual meaning here. In the new dispensation there will be no division—the sea separates nations and divides peoples from each other. To John on Patmos the deep waters were like prison walls, shutting him off from his brothers and his work; there will be no such barriers in the world to come. Leagues of rolling billows lie between us and many a loved one whom we prayerfully remember tonight, but in the bright world to which we go there will be unbroken fellowship for all the redeemed family. In this sense there will be no more sea. The sea is also the emblem of change: with its ebbs and flows, its glassy smoothness and its mountainous billows, its gentle murmurs and its tumultuous roarings, it is never long the same.
